# ChargeItemDefinition

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitemdefinition.mdx

title: ChargeItemDefinition
sidebar_position: 17

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/chargeitemdefinition.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# ChargeItemDefinition

The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitemdefinition">ChargeItemDefinition</Link> resource provides the properties that apply to the (billing) codes necessary to calculate costs and prices. The properties may differ largely depending on type and realm, therefore this resource gives only a rough structure and requires profiling for each type of billing code system.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitemdefinition">ChargeItemDefinition</Link> holds all relevant billing information pertaining to a billing code or a product. </p> <p> Many billing systems have rules associated with the code which may define whether a billing code is applicable in a specific context or whether certain billing details (surcharges, discounts) apply. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitemdefinition">ChargeItemDefinitions</Link> may also be used to hold pricing information pertaining to only one specific instance of a product (e.g. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/device">Device</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medication">Medication</Link> or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/substance">Substance</Link>) which may be a requirement for custom made devices or medications or other products where prices vary by instance. Rules for applicability may include </p><ul> <li>a billing code is only applicable in an outpatient setting</li> <li>a surcharge that applies only to services provided outside regular business hours</li> <li>a discount that applies only to patients up to the age of 14</li> <li>a billing code that may only be charged once per <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link></li> <li>a billing code that can only be charged in combination with another code from the same billing system</li> </ul> <p></p> <p> A billing engine will apply the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitemdefinition">ChargeItemDefinitions</Link> to all <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitem">ChargeItems</Link> within a specific <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/account">Account</Link> in order to select all billable items  an acquire the pricing details to create an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/invoice">Invoice</Link>. However, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitem">ChargeItems</Link> may be validated against a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitemdefinition">ChargeItemDefinition</Link> at any point in time, using the $apply-Operation </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p> While the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitem">ChargeItem</Link> resource represents the occurrence of a billing code (for services rendered or products supplied to a specific patient), the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitemdefinition">ChargeItemDefinition</Link> represents the properties and rules that a billing engine needs to determine the pricing and applicability of a billing code in the context of a specific setting. </p><p> Billing Codes may be defined in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> Resource, however, each of these codes - if it is used in a financial context - can have a large number of business rules and properties associated with it, that lay outside the scope of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> and may change in time independently from the underlying Code's validity period. Even though <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> can associate a concept with any number of additional properties, such a construct would be very hard to maintain. This is why the ChargItemDefinition has been introduced. It allows to maintain the attributes of each billing code independently and has a wider scope to also include business rules. </p><p> In most use cases, billing codes will be both defined as semantical concepts in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> and as a financial artifact in <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitemdefinition">ChargeItemDefinition</Link>. </p><p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitemdefinition">ChargeItemDefinitions</Link> that pertain to codes from the same <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> may be aggregated using the Catalog profile for <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link>. </p><p> Resources representing products that can be sold or billed (Device, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medication">Medication</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/substance">Substance</Link>...), do not specify financial details for the product instance. Most of the time, such products are not billed seperately but are a part of a generic billing code that covers both the product and the service rendered.  In some occasions however, product prices may vary depending on type or manufactuer or even on instance (e.g. custom made products). For these cases,  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitemdefinition">ChargeItemDefinitions</Link> may be created to specify the financial details for a product kind, type or instance. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitem">ChargeItem</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# Claim

title: Claim

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';

# Claim

A provider issued list of professional services and products which have been provided, or are to be provided, to a patient which is sent to an insurer for reimbursement.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> is used by providers and payors, insurers, to exchange the financial information, and supporting clinical information, regarding the provision  of health care services with payors and for reporting to regulatory bodies and firms which provide data analytics. The primary uses of this resource is to support eClaims,  the exchange of information relating to the proposed or actual provision of healthcare-related goods and services for patients to their benefit payors, insurers and national health programs, for treatment payment planning and reimbursement. </p> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> resource is a "request" resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#request">Workflow Request.</a></p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> resource may be interpreted differently depending on its intended use (and the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>.use element contains the code to indicate): </p><ul> <li>claim - where the provision of goods and services is <b>complete</b> and adjudication under a plan and payment is sought.</li> <li>preauthorization - where the provision of goods and services is <b>proposed</b> and authorization and/or the reservation of funds is desired.</li> <li>predetermination - where the provision of goods and services is <b>explored</b> to determine what services may be covered and to what amount. Essentially a 'what if' claim.</li> </ul>  <p></p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> also supports: </p><ul> <li>Up to a 3-tier hierarchy of Goods, products, and Services, to support simple to complex billing.</li> <li>Multiple insurance programs arranged in a Coordination of Benefit sequence to enable exchange with primary, secondary, tertiary etc. insurance coverages.</li> <li>Assignment of benefit - the benefit may be requested to be directed to the subscriber, the provider or another party.</li> </ul> <p></p> <p> <b>Mapping to other <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> specifications:</b> Mappings are currently maintained by the Financial Management Work <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</Link> to UB04 and CMS1500 and are available  at <a href="https://confluence.hl7.org/display/FM/FHIR+Resource+Development">https://confluence.hl7.org/display/FM/FHIR+Resource+Development </a>. Mappings to other specifications may be made available where IP restrictions permit.   </p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Additional Information <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/claim.html#13.6.1.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> Additional information regarding electronic claims content and usage may be found at: </p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#resource-status">Financial Resource Status Lifecycle</a>: how .status is used in the financial resources.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#secondary-use">Secondary Use of Resources</a>: how resources such as <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</Link> may used for  reporting and data exchange for analytics, not just for eClaims exchange between providers and payors.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#subrogation">Subrogation</a>: how eClaims may handle patient insurance coverages when another insurer rather than  the provider will settle the claim and potentially recover costs against specified coverages.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#cob">Coordination of Benefit</a>: how eClaims may handle multiple patient insurance coverages.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#batch">Batches</a>: how eClaims may handle batches of eligibility, claims and responses.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#attachments">Attachments and Supporting Information</a>: how eClaims may handle the provision of supporting  information, whether provided by content or reference, within the eClaim resource when submitted to the payor or later in a resource which refers  to the subject eClaim resource. This also includes how payors may request additional supporting information from providers.</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> resource is used to request the adjudication and/or authorization of a set of healthcare-related goods and services for a patient against the patient's insurance coverages, or to request what the adjudication would be for a supplied set of goods or services should they be actually supplied to the patient.</p> <p>When requesting whether the patient's coverage is inforce, whether it is valid at this or a specified date, or requesting the benefit details or preauthorization requirements  associated with a coverage, then <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityrequest">CoverageEligibilityRequest</a> should be used instead.</p> <p>When using the resources for reporting and transferring claims data, which may have originated in some standard other than FHIR, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> resource is useful if only the request side of the information exchange is of interest. If, however, both the request and the adjudication information is to be reported then the  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</a> should be used instead.</p> <p>For reporting out to patients or transferring data to patient centered applications, such as patient health Record (PHR) application, the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</a>  should be used instead of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> resources as those resources may contain provider and payer specific information which is not appropriate for sharing with  the patient.</p> <p> <b>The eClaim domain includes a number of related resources</b> </p> <table border="1" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="2" frame="box"> <tbody><tr> <td>Claim</td> <td>A suite of goods and services and insurances coverages under which adjudication or authorization is requested.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityrequest">CoverageEligibilityRequest</a></td> <td>A request to a payor to: ascertain whether a coverage is in-force at the current or at a specified time; list the table of benefits; determine whether coverage is provided for specified categories or specific services; and whether preauthorization is required, and if so what supporting information would be required.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</a></td> <td>A payor's adjudication and/or authorization response to the suite of services provided in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>. Typically the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> references the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> but does not duplicate the clinical or financial information provided in the claim.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</a></td> <td>This resource combines the information from the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> and the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link>, stripping out any provider or payor proprietary information, into a unified information model  suitable for use for: patient reporting; transferring information to a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> Health Record system; and, supporting complete claim and adjudication information exchange  with regulatory and analytics organizations and other parts of the provider's organization. </td> </tr> </tbody></table> </div>
  </TabItem>

# ClaimResponse

This resource provides the adjudication details from the processing of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> resource.

  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> resource provides application level adjudication results, or an application level error,  which are the result of processing a submitted <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> resource where that <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> may be the functional corollary of   a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>, Predetermination or a Preauthorization.This resource is the only appropriate response to a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> which a  processing system recognizes as a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> resource.  </p>  <p>  This is the adjudicated response to a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>, Predetermination or Preauthorization. The strength   of the payment aspect of the response is matching to the strength of the original request. For a   <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> the adjudication indicates payment which is intended to be made. For Preauthorization no payment will  actually be made however funds may be reserved to settle a claim submitted later. For   Predetermination no payment will  actually be made and no assurance is given that the adjudication of a claim submitted later will  match the adjudication provided, for example funds may have been exhausted in the interim.   Only an actual claim may be expected to result in actual payment.  </p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> resource may also be returned with the response for the submission of: Re-adjudication and Reversals. </p> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> resource is an "event" resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">Workflow Event.</a></p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Additional Information <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/claimresponse.html#13.7.1.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> Additional information regarding electronic claims content and usage may be found at: </p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#resource-status">Financial Resource Status Lifecycle</a>: how .status is used in the financial resources.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#secondary-use">Secondary Use of Resources</a>: how resources such as <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</Link>  may be used for  reporting and data exchange for analytics, not just for eClaims exchange between providers and payors.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#subrogation">Subrogation</a>: how eClaims may handle patient insurance coverages when another insurer rather than  the provider will settle the claim and potentially recover costs against specified coverages.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#cob">Coordination of Benefit</a>: how eClaims may handle multiple patient insurance coverages.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#real-time">RealTime Exchange and Obtaining Deferred Responsess</a>: <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponses</Link> may be obtained using Polling or FHIR REST (SEARCH).</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#attachments">Attachments and Supporting Information</a>: how eClaims may handle the provision of supporting  information, whether provided by content or reference, within the eClaim resource when submitted to the payor or later in a resource which refers  to the subject eClaim resource. This also includes how payors may request additional supporting information from providers.</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> resource is used to provide the results of the adjudication and/or authorization of a set of healthcare-related products and services for a patient against the patient's insurance coverages, or to respond with what the adjudication would be for a supplied set of products or services should they be actually supplied to the patient. </p> <p>The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</a> resource is for reporting out to patients or transferring data to patient centered applications, such as patient health Record (PHR) application, the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</a>  should be used instead of the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</a> and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</a> resources as those resources may contain provider and payer specific information which is not appropriate for sharing with the patient.</p> <p>When using the resources for reporting and transferring claims data, which may have originated in some standard other than FHIR, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> resource is useful if only the request side of the information exchange is of interest. # ClinicalImpression

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/clinicalimpression.mdx

title: ClinicalImpression
sidebar_position: 20

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/clinicalimpression.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# ClinicalImpression

A record of a clinical assessment performed to determine what problem(s) may affect the patient and before planning the treatments or management strategies that are best to manage a patient's condition. Assessments are often 1:1 with a clinical consultation / encounter, but this varies greatly depending on the clinical workflow. This resource is called "ClinicalImpression" rather than "ClinicalAssessment" to avoid confusion with the recording of assessment tools such as Apgar score.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> Performing a clinical assessment is a fundamental part of a clinician's workflow, performed repeatedly throughout the day.  In spite of this - or perhaps, because of it - there is wide variance in how clinical impressions are recorded.  Some clinical assessments simply result in an impression recorded as a single text note in the patient 'record' (e.g. "Progress satisfactory,  continue with treatment"), while others are associated with careful, detailed record keeping of the  evidence gathered and the reasoning leading to a differential diagnosis, and there is a continuum between these. This resource is intended to be  used to cover all these use cases. </p> <p> The assessment is intimately linked to the process of care. It may occur in the context of a care plan, and it very often results in a new (or revised) care plan. Normally, clinical assessments are part of an  ongoing process of care, and the patient will be re-assessed repeatedly. For this reason, the clinical impression can explicitly reference both care plans (preceding and resulting) and reference a previous impression that this impression follows. </p>  <p>An impression is a clinical summation of information and/or an opinion formed, which is the outcome of the clinical assessment process.  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/clinicalimpression">ClinicalImpression</Link> may lead to a statement of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</Link> about a patient.</p>      <p>In FHIR, an assessment is typically an instrument or tool used to collect information about a patient.</p> <a name="dstu"></a> <blockquote class="stu-note"><p><b>Trial-Use Note:</b> Unlike many other resources, there is little prior art with regard to exchanging records of  clinical assessments. For this reason, this resource should be regarded as particularly  prone to ongoing revision. In terms of scope and usage, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> Care workgroup wishes to draw the attention of reviewers and implementers to the following issues:  <a name="dstu"></a> </p> <ul>  <li>When is an existing clinical impression revised, rather than a new one created (that references the existing one)? How does that affect the status? what's the interplay between the status of the diagnosis and the status of the impression? (e.g. for a 'provisional' impression, which bit is provisional?)</li>  <li>This structure doesn't differentiate between a working and a final diagnosis. Given an answer to the previous question, should it?</li>  <li>Further clarify around the relationship between care plan and impression is needed. Both answers to the previous questions and ongoing discussions around revisions to the care plan will influence the design of clinical impression</li>  <li>Should prognosis be represented, and if so, how much structure should it have?</li>  <li>Should an impression reference other impressions that are related? (how related?)</li>  <li>Investigations - the specification needs a good value set for the code for the group, and will be considering the name "investigations" further</li> </ul>  <p> Feedback is welcome <a href="http://hl7.org/fhir-issues">here </a>. </p></blockquote> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/clinicalimpression">ClinicalImpression</Link> is the equivalent of the "A" in Weed  SOAP.  It is the outcome of the clinical assessment process.  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/clinicalimpression">ClinicalImpression</Link> may lead to a statement of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</Link> about a patient. There is another related clinical concept often called an "assessment": assessment Tools such as Apgar (also known as "Assessment Scales"). This is not what the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/clinicalimpression">ClinicalImpression</Link> resource is about; assessment tools such as Apgar are represented as  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observations</a>, and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaires</a> may be used to help  generate these. Clinical Impressions may refer to these assessment tools as one of the investigations that was performed during the assessment process. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> An important background to understanding this resource is <a href="https://confluence.hl7.org/display/PC/Clinical+Assessment">the FHIR Confluence page for clinical assessment </a>. In particular, the storyboards there drove the design of the resource, and will be the basis for all examples created. </p> <p> <b>PLANNED CHANGE:</b> </p> <p> <b>ClinicalImpression</b> is one of the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">Event</a> resources in the FHIR <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">Workflow</a> specification.  As such, it is expected to be adjusted to align with the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/event.html">Event</a> workflow pattern which will involve adding a number of additional data elements and potentially renaming a few elements.  Any concerns about performing such alignment are welcome as ballot comments and/or tracker items. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>

# CodeSystem

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem.mdx

title: CodeSystem
sidebar_position: 21

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/codesystem.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# CodeSystem

The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> resource is used to declare the existence of and describe a code system or code system supplement and its key properties, and optionally define a part or all of its content.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The FHIR terminology specification is based on two key concepts, originally defined in <a href="http://www.hl7.org/documentcenter/public/standards/V3/core_principles/infrastructure/coreprinciples/v3modelcoreprinciples.html">HL7 v3 Core Principles </a>: </p> <ul> <li> <b>code system</b> - declares the existence of and describes a code system or code system supplement and its key properties, and optionally defines a part or all of its content. Also known as Ontology, Terminology, or Enumeration</li> <li> <b>value set</b> - specifies a set of codes drawn from one or more code systems, intended for use in a particular context. Value sets link between <code>CodeSystem</code> definitions and their use in <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/terminologies.html">coded elements</a></li> </ul> <p> Code systems define which codes (symbols and/or expressions) exist, and how they are understood. Value sets  select a set of codes from one or more code systems to specify which codes can be used in a particular context. </p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> resource is used to declare the existence of a code system, and its key properties: </p> <ul>  <li>Identifying URL and version</li>  <li>Description, Copyright, publication date, and other metadata</li>  <li>Some key properties of the code system itself - e.g. whether it exhibits concept permanence, whether it defines a compositional grammar, and whether the codes that it defines are case sensitive</li>  <li>What filters can be used in value sets that use the code system in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/valueset">ValueSet</Link>.compose element</li>   <li>What concept properties are defined by the code system</li> </ul> <p> In addition, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> resource may list some or all of the concepts in the code system, along with their basic properties (code, display, definition), designations, and additional properties. Code System resources may also be used to define supplements, which extend an existing code system with  additional designations and properties. </p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> resource is not intended to support the process of maintaining code systems.  Instead, the focus is on publishing the properties and optionally the content of a code  system for use throughout the FHIR eco-system, such as to support value set expansion and  validation.  Note that the important existing (large) code systems (SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm, ICD family, etc.)  all have their own maintenance systems and distribution formats, and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> is generally not an efficient way to distribute their content, though it is used as one way of  declaring the filters and properties associated with those code systems.  </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="relationships"></a> <ul>  <li>Code systems are used in <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/valueset">ValueSet</a> resources</li>  <li>The <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir//api/fhir/datatypes/coding">Coding</a> data type refers to <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> resources by their canonical URL</li>  <li>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> resource design is based, in part, on the code system functionality described in       the <a href="http://www.omg.org/spec/CTS2/1.0/">HL7 CTS 2 </a> specification.       A CTS2 server can be used to maintain code systems which are then published using the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> resource</li>  <li>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> resource documents the inherent structure and capabilities of code system, whereas     the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/terminologycapabilities">TerminologyCapabilities</a> resource documents what a server hosting the code system is capable of</li> </ul> <p> The <code>CodeSystem</code> resource declares the existence of a code system and its key properties including its preferred identifier. The <code>NamingSystem</code> resource identifies the existence of a code or identifier system, and its possible and preferred identifiers.  The key difference between the resources is who creates and manages them - <code>CodeSystem</code> resources are managed by the owner or publisher of the code system, who can properly define the code system features and content. <code>NamingSystem</code> resources, on the other hand, are frequently defined by 3rd parties that encounter the code system in use, and need to describe the use, but do not have the authority to define the features and content.  Additionally, there may be multiple authoritative <code>NamingSystem</code> resources for a code system, but ideally there would be only one authoritative <code>CodeSystem</code> resource (identified by its canonical URL) that is provided by the code system publisher, with multiple copies distributed on additional FHIR servers or elsewhere and used where needed. </p> <p> Both Code System supplements and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/conceptmap">Concept Maps</a> may be used to define relationships between concepts  in different systems. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/conceptmap">ConceptMaps</Link> are assertions of the relationships between different concepts  that are associated with particular contexts of use, while <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> supplements are used to  define inherent properties and semantics of the concepts in the code system </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="context"></a> <p> When using code systems and value sets, proper differentiation between a code system and a value set is important.  This is one very common area where significant clinical safety risks occur in practice. Implementers should be familiar with the content in <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/terminologies.html">Using Codes in Resources</a>. </p> <a name="ident"></a> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> Identification <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> A code system has three identifiers. The first two can be used to reference the code system in the FHIR context: </p> <ul>  <li><code>CodeSystem.id</code>: The <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/resource.html#id">logical id</a> on the system that holds the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> resource instance - this typically is expected to change as the resource moves from server to server. The location URI is constructed by appending the logical id to the server base address where the instance is found and the resource type. This URI should be a resolvable URL by which the resource instance may be retrieved, usually from a FHIR server, and it may be a relative reference typically to the server base URL.  </li>  <li><code>CodeSystem.url</code>: The canonical URL that never changes for this code system - it is the same in every copy. The element is named <code>url</code> rather than <code>uri</code> for legacy reasons and to strongly encourage providing a resolvable URL as the identifier whenever possible.  This canonical URL is used to refer to all instances of this particular code system across all servers and systems. Ideally, this URI should be a URL which resolves to the location of the master version of the code system, though this is not always possible.  </li> </ul> <blockquote> <p> For example, the code systems published as part of the FHIR specification all have a location ("literal") URI which is the URL where they may be accessed in the FHIR specification itself. However, while a new version of the FHIR specification is being prepared, code systems that are published in the drafts will not be found in the current FHIR specification version.  </p> </blockquote> <p> Because it is common practice to copy (cache) code systems locally, most  references to code systems can use either the canonical URL or the location ("literal") URL.  </p> <p> The third code system identifier is used typically for external references to the code system outside of FHIR: </p>  <ul>  <li><code>CodeSystem.identifier</code>: A system/value pair that is used to identify the code system in other contexts (such as an OID in an <a href="https://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=186">HL7 v3 </a> specification)</li> </ul> <p> For further information regarding resource identification, see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/resource.html#id">Resource Identity</a>. </p> <p> This means that each code system has 2 different URIs that can be used to reference it -  its canonical URL (the <code>url</code> element), and its local location from which it may be retrieved (which includes the <code>id</code> element). Because it is common practice to copy (cache) code systems locally, most references to  code systems use the canonical URL.  </p> <p> Alternatively, the <code>identifier</code> and <code>version</code> elements may be used to reference this code system in a  design, a profile, a <a href="http://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=7">CDA </a> template  or <a href="https://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=186">HL7 v3 </a> message (in the CD data  type codeSystem and codeSystemVersion properties). These different contexts may make additional restrictions on the  possible values of these elements.  The <code>identifier</code> is generally not needed when using code systems in a FHIR context, where the canonical URL is always the focus. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/datatypes.html#Coding">Coding</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/conceptmap">ConceptMap</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/terminologycapabilities">TerminologyCapabilities</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/valueset">ValueSet</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# Communication

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/communication.mdx

title: Communication
sidebar_position: 22

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/communication.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# Communication

An occurrence of information being transmitted; e.g. an alert that was sent to a responsible provider, a public health agency that was notified about a reportable condition.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a>        <p>Communication is one of the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">event</a> resources in the FHIR <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">workflow</a> specification.</p>     <p> This resource is a record of a communication even if it is planned or has failed. A communication is a conveyance of information from one entity, a sender, to another entity, a receiver.  The sender and receivers may be patients, practitioners, related persons, organizations, or devices. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communication">Communication</Link> use cases include: </p> <ul> <li>A reminder or alert delivered to a responsible provider</li> <li>A recorded notification from the nurse to the on-call physician (or any other specified person) that a patient's temperature exceeds a value</li> <li>A notification to a public health agency of a patient presenting with a communicable disease reportable to the public health agency</li> <li>Patient educational material sent by a provider to a patient</li> <li>Unable to deliver lab results to ordering physician</li> </ul> <p> Non-patient specific communication use cases may include: </p> <ul> <li>A nurse call from a hall bathroom</li> <li>Advisory for battery service from a pump</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> This resource is a record of a communication that has occurred. It does not represent the actual flow of communication. While <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/auditevent">AuditEvent</a> can track electronic disclosures of information, it cannot track conversations, phone calls, letters and other interactions that are not system-to-system.  And even for system-to-system communications, the specific end recipients might not be known.  Furthermore, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/auditevent">AuditEvents</a> are not considered to be "part" of the patient record, while <b>Communication</b> instances are.  The <b>Communication</b> resource is not used as a general audit mechanism to track every disclosure of every record.  Rather, it is used when a clinician or other user wants to ensure a record of a particular communication is itself maintained as part of the reviewable health record. </p> <p> <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flag</a> resources represent a continuous ongoing "communication" alerting anyone dealing with the patient of certain precautions to take or issues to be aware of.  The flags are continuously present as an ongoing reminder.  This is  distinct from <b>Communication</b> where there is a specific intended sender and receiver and the information is delivered only once. </p> <p><b>Communication and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link></b></p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communication">Communication</Link> is about the transfer of information (which might or might not occur as part of an encounter), while <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link>  is about the coming together (in person or virtually) of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> with a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link>.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communication">Communication</Link> does not deal with  the duration of a call, it represents the fact that information was transferred at a particular point in time. </p> <p> The phone calls involving the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> should be handled using <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</a>.  Phone calls not involving the patient  (e.g. between practitioners or practitioner to relative) that are tracked for billing or other purposes can use <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communication">Communication</Link>  to represent the information transferred but are not ideal to represent the call itself.   A better mechanism for handling such calls will be explored in a future release. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

</Tabs>

# CompartmentDefinition

A compartment definition that defines how resources are accessed on a server.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> Each resource may belong to one or more logical compartments. A compartment is a logical  grouping of resources which share a common property. Compartments have two principal roles: </p> <ul>  <li>Function as an access mechanism for finding a set of related resources quickly</li>  <li>Provide a definitional basis for applying access control to resources quickly</li> </ul> <p><b>Note:</b></p> <p> At present, compartment definitions can <i>only</i> be defined by HL7 International.  This is because their existence creates significant impact on the behavior of servers. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div>  <a name="bnr"></a>   <p> Compartment definitions describe how particular compartment instances are named and identified, and how systems know which resources are in the compartment. The following compartments are  defined by this specification: </p> <table class="grid">  <tbody><tr><td><b>Title</b></td><td><b>Description</b></td><td><b>Identity</b></td><td><b>Membership</b></td></tr>  <tr><td><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/compartmentdefinition-patient.html">Patient</a></td><td>The set of resources associated with a particular patient</td><td>There is an instance of the patient compartment for each patient resource, and the identity of the compartment is the same as the patient. When a patient is linked to another patient, all the records associated with the linked patient are in the compartment associated with the target of the link.</td><td>The patient compartment includes any resources where the subject of  the resource is the patient, and some other resources that are directly linked  to resources in the patient compartment</td></tr>  <tr><td><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/compartmentdefinition-encounter.html">Encounter</a></td><td>The set of resources associated with a particular encounter</td><td>There is an instance of the encounter compartment for each encounter resource, and the identity of the compartment is the same as the encounter</td><td>The encounter compartment includes any resources where the resource has an explicitly nominated encounter, and some other resources that themselves link  to resources in the encounter compartment. Note that for many resources, the exact nature of the link to encounter can be ambiguous (e.g. for a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link>, is it the encounter when it was initiated, or when it was reported?)</td></tr>  <tr><td><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/compartmentdefinition-relatedperson.html">RelatedPerson</a></td><td>The set of resources associated with a particular 'related person'</td><td>There is an instance of the relatedPerson compartment for each relatedPerson resource, and the identity of the compartment is the same as the relatedPerson</td><td>The relatedPerson compartment includes any resources where the resource is explicitly linked to relatedPerson (usually as author)</td></tr>  <tr><td><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/compartmentdefinition-practitioner.html">Practitioner</a></td><td>The set of resources associated with a particular practitioner</td><td>There is an instance of the practitioner compartment for each <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> resource, and the identity of the compartment is the same as the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link></td><td>The practitioner compartment includes any resources where the resource is explicitly linked to a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> (usually as author, but other kinds of linkage exist)</td></tr>  <tr><td><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/compartmentdefinition-device.html">Device</a></td><td>The set of resources associated with a particular device</td><td>There is an instance of the device compartment for each <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/device">Device</Link> resource, and the identity of the compartment is the same as the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/device">Device</Link></td><td>The device compartment includes any resources where the resource is explicitly linked to a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/device">Device</Link> (mostly subject or performer)</td></tr> </tbody></table> <p> The full definitions of these compartments are published as <code>CompartmentDefinition</code> resources. Servers typically do not support the full definition of a compartment, and are not  required to. Systems may publish <code>CompartmentDefinition</code> resources so that other systems may make use of compartments properly. </p> <ul>  <li>CompartmentDefinitions are used by <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/capabilitystatement">CapabilityStatement</a> instances for specifying how resources are accessed</li> </ul> </div>

# Composition

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition.mdx

title: Composition
sidebar_position: 25

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/composition.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# Composition

A set of healthcare-related information that is assembled together into a single logical package that provides a single coherent statement of meaning, establishes its own context and that has clinical attestation with regard to who is making the statement. A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> defines the structure and narrative content necessary for a document. However, a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> alone does not constitute a document. Rather, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> must be the first entry in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</Link> where <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</Link>.type=document, and any other resources referenced from <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> must be included as subsequent entries in the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</Link> (for example <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link>, etc.).

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p>  A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> is the basic structure from which <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/documents.html">FHIR Documents</a> -  immutable bundles with attested narrative - are built. A single logical composition may be  associated with a series of derived documents, each of which is a frozen copy of the  composition. </p> <p> Note: <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EN_13606">EN 13606 </a> uses the term "Composition"  to refer to a single commit to an EHR system, and offers some common examples: a composition  containing a consultation note, a progress note, a report or a letter, an investigation report,  a prescription form or a set of bedside nursing observations. Using <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> for an attested EHR commit is a valid use of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> resource, but for FHIR purposes, it would be usual to make more granular updates with individual provenance statements. </p> <p> The <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition-clinicaldocument.html">Clinical Document profile</a> constrains <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> to specify a clinical document (matching <a href="http://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=7">CDA </a>).   See also the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/comparison-cda.html">comparison with CDA</a>. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> is a structure for grouping information for purposes of persistence and attestability.  There are several other grouping structures in FHIR with distinct purposes: </p> <ul> <li> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</a> resource - enumerates a flat collection of resources and provides features for managing the collection.   While a particular <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> instance may represent a "snapshot", from a business process perspective, the notion of "list"  is dynamic – items are added and removed over time.  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> resource references other resources.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">Lists</Link> may be  curated and have specific business meaning. </li> <li> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</a> resource - defines a group of specific people, animals, devices, etc. by enumerating them,  or by describing qualities that group members have. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</Link> resource refers to other resources, possibly implicitly.   <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Groups</Link> are intended to be acted upon or observed as a whole (e.g., performing therapy on a group, calculating risk for a group,  etc.).  This resource will commonly be used for public health (e.g., describing an at-risk population), clinical trials (e.g.,  defining a test subject pool) and similar purposes. </li> <li> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</a> resource - is an infrastructure container for a group of resources.  It does not have narrative  and is used to group collections of resources for transmission, persistence or processing (e.g., messages, documents, transactions,  query responses, etc.).  The content of bundles is typically algorithmically determined for a particular exchange or persistence purpose. </li> <li> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</a> resource - defines a set of healthcare-related information that is assembled  together into a single logical document that provides a single coherent statement of meaning, establishes its own context and  that has clinical attestation with regard to who is making the statement. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> resource provides the basic structure  of a FHIR <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/documents.html">document</a>.  The full content of the document is expressed using a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</a>  containing the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> and its entries.  </li> </ul> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> resource organizes clinical and administrative content into sections, each of which contains a narrative,  and references other resources for supporting data. The narrative content of the various sections in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> are  supported by the resources referenced in the section entries.  The complete set of content to make up a document includes  the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> resource together with various resources pointed to or indirectly connected to the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link>, all gathered together into a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</a> for transport and persistence. Resources associated with the following list of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> references SHALL be included in the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</a>: </p> <ul>  <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition-definitions.html#Composition.subject">Composition.subject</a></li>  <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition-definitions.html#Composition.encounter">Composition.encounter</a></li>  <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition-definitions.html#Composition.author">Composition.author</a></li>  <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition-definitions.html#Composition.attester.party">Composition.attester.party</a></li>  <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition-definitions.html#Composition.custodian">Composition.custodian</a></li>  <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition-definitions.html#Composition.event.detail">Composition.event.detail</a></li>  <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition-definitions.html#Composition.section.author">Composition.section.author</a></li>  <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition-definitions.html#Composition.section.focus">Composition.section.focus</a></li>  <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition-definitions.html#Composition.section.entry">Composition.section.entry</a></li> </ul> <p> Other resources referred to by those resources MAY be included in the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</a> at the discretion of the authoring  system as documented in the system's operation definition (such as <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition-operation-document.html">$document</a> operation),  or as specified by any applicable profiles.  </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <a name="status"></a> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> Status Codes <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> Every composition has a status element, which describes the status of the content of the composition, taken from this list of codes: </p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> The workflow/clinical status of the composition. <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition.html#2.41.3.2" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <table class="codes">  <tbody><tr><td>preliminary</td><td>This is a preliminary composition or document (also known as initial or interim). The content may be incomplete or unverified.</td></tr>  <tr><td>final</td><td>This version of the composition is complete and verified by an appropriate person and no further work is planned. Any subsequent updates would be on a new version of the composition.</td></tr>  <tr><td>amended</td><td>The composition content or the referenced resources have been modified (edited or added to) subsequent to being released as "final" and the composition is complete and verified by an authorized person.</td></tr>  <tr><td>entered-in-error</td><td>The composition or document was originally created/issued in error, and this is an amendment that marks that the entire series should not be considered as valid.</td></tr> </tbody></table> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> status generally only moves down through this list - it moves from <code>preliminary</code> to <code>final</code> and then it may progress to <code>amended</code>.  Note that in many workflows, only <code>final</code> compositions are made available and the <code>preliminary</code> status is not used.  </p> <p> A very few compositions are created entirely in error in the workflow - usually the composition concerns the wrong patient or is written by the wrong author, and the error is only detected after the composition has been used or documents have been derived from it. To support resolution of this case,  the composition is updated to be marked as <code>entered-in-error</code> and a new derived document can be created. This means that the entire series of derived  documents is now considered to be created in error and systems receiving derived documents based on retracted compositions SHOULD remove data taken from earlier documents from routine use and/or take other appropriate actions. Systems are not required to  provide this workflow or support documents derived from retracted compositions, but they SHALL NOT ignore a status of <code>entered-in-error</code>.  Note that systems that handle compositions or derived documents and don't support the error status need to define  some other way of handling compositions that are created in error; while this is not a common occurrence, some clinical systems  have no provision for removing erroneous information from a patient's record, and there is no way for a user to know that it is not fit for use - this is not safe.  </p> <a name="cda"></a> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Note for CDA aware readers <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> Many users of this specification are familiar with the <a href="http://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=7">Clinical Document Architecture </a> (CDA) and related specifications. CDA is a primary design input to the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> resource (other principal inputs are other HL7 document specifications and EN13606). There are three important structural  differences between CDA and the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> resource: </p> <ul>  <li>A composition is a logical construct- its identifier matches to the CDA ClinicalDocument.setId.   <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> resources are wrapped into <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/documents.html">Document</a> structures, for exchange  of the whole package (the composition and its parts), and this wrapped, sealed entity is equivalent to a CDA document,   where the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</Link>.id is equivalent in function to ClinicalDocument.id (but it is not identical when interconverting, since it's a transform between them).</li>  <li>The composition section defines a section (or sub-section) of the document, but unlike CDA, the section entries are     actually references to other <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/resourcelist.html">resources</a> that hold the supporting data content for the section.     This design means that the data can be reused in many other ways.     </li>   <li>Unlike CDA, the context defined in the <code>Composition</code> (the confidentiality, subject, author, event, event period and encounter) apply to the composition and do not specifically apply to the resources referenced from    the <code>section.entry</code>. There is no context flow model in FHIR, so each resource referenced from    within a <code>Composition</code> expresses its own individual context.  In this way, clinical content can    safely be extracted from the composition.</li> </ul> <p> In addition, note that both the code lists (e.g., <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/valueset-composition-status.html">Composition.status</a>) and the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> resource are <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/composition-mappings.html">mapped</a> to <a href="https://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=186">HL7 v3 </a> and/or CDA. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# ConceptMap

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/conceptmap.mdx

title: ConceptMap
sidebar_position: 26

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

# ConceptMap

A statement of relationships from one set of concepts to one or more other concepts - either concepts in code systems, or data element/data element concepts, or classes in class models.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div>  <a name="scope"></a>   <p> A concept map defines a mapping from a set of concepts defined in a code system (commonly referred to as the "system") to one or more concepts defined in other code systems.  In the mapping context, a system can be a typical <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/terminologies.html">code system</a> based on a recognized standard or local terminology (in any of its forms), or in some cases it may be an <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/conceptmap">"implicit" code system</a> that is not based on a recognized terminology but still represents a set of "concepts" that can be usefully mapped. Mappings are one way - from the source to the target system. In many cases, the reverse mappings are valid, but this cannot be assumed to be the case.  </p> <p> Mappings between code system concepts are only intended to be defined in the context of a particular business usage.  The business use case is normally defined by the specification of the source and target value sets.  The mappings may be useful in other contexts, but this must be determined based on the context of use and meaning; it cannot be taken for granted automatically. An example where the usage context is important for choosing the correct mapping is mapping from a clinical terminology (e.g. SNOMED CT) to a classification (e.g. ICD-10) for either data analysis or billing.  Mappings in the data analysis context would be targeted for an appropriate classification (often at a higher level), whereas in the billing context there may be specific requirements to be met (e.g. leaf level codes only) that could result in multiple mappings for a single source concept and then require additional information beyond the source concept itself in order to select the correct final mapping. </p> <p> Note that all code systems (explicit or implicit) represented in FHIR have URI identifiers for value sets (also either explicit or implicit) that include the entire code system, and these <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/terminology-service.html#4.6.5">"all codes" value sets</a> can be used for mappings that are valid in all use contexts that are appropriate for the code system. </p> <p> Each mapping for a concept from the source to target system includes an <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/valueset-concept-map-equivalence.html">equivalence</a>  property that specifies how similar the mapping is (or, in some cases, that there is no valid mapping).  There is one <code>element</code> for each concept or field in the source value set or system that needs to be mapped. Each source concept may have multiple targets: </p> <ul>  <li>because there are multiple possible mappings (e.g., ambiguous)</li>  <li>to specify a correct map, and specify other mappings as invalid</li>  <li>when there are multiple mappings depending on the values of other elements (dependsOn)</li> </ul> <p> There SHOULD be at least one target for each element, but some incomplete concept maps  might not have a target for each concept.  </p> <p> A key concept for the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/conceptmap">ConceptMap</Link> resource is the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/conceptmap-operation-translate.html">$translate operation</a>. This operation  is a formal definition of an API by which a <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/terminology-service.html">terminology server</a> can allow clients to ask for a  translation to be done based on the content in the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/conceptmap">ConceptMap</Link> resource. As such it also provides useful perspective on the  operational use of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/conceptmap">ConceptMap</Link> resources in any context. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> While <code>ConceptMap</code> resources are not referred to directly from any other  resource, they may be included and used in <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/implementationguide">ImplementationGuide</a> resources, and provide background knowledge that is useful in many contexts, including <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/operations.html">operations</a> defined in this specification. </p> <p> In addition to <code>ConceptMap</code>, there is also the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/structuremap">StructureMap</a> resource. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/conceptmap">ConceptMap</Link> resource defines relationships between concepts in their own right, along with grading of their equivalencies, while the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/structuremap">StructureMap</Link> defines an executable  transform for instances that conform to a known structure. </p> <p> Both <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">Code System</a> supplements and Concept Maps may be used to define relationships between concepts  in different systems. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/conceptmap">ConceptMaps</Link> are assertions of the relationships between different concepts  that are associated with particular contexts of use, while <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/codesystem">CodeSystem</Link> supplements are used to  define inherent properties and semantics of the concepts in the code system </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> Further discussion of the issues involved in mapping between concept definition systems can be found in the   <a href="http://www.hl7.org/documentcenter/public/standards/V3/core_principles/infrastructure/coreprinciples/v3modelcoreprinciples.html">HL7 v3 Core Principles </a> document  and the functionality described in the <a href="http://www.omg.org/spec/CTS2/1.0/">OMG CTS 2 </a> specification.  </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

</Tabs>

# Condition

A clinical condition, problem, diagnosis, or other event, situation, issue, or clinical concept that has risen to a level of concern. Refer to the [US Core Condition profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-condition.html) and the US Core [Condition Encounter](http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/StructureDefinition-us-core-condition-encounter-diagnosis.html) profile.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p>Condition is one of the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">event</a> resources in the FHIR <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">workflow</a> specification.</p> <p> This resource is used to record detailed information about a condition, problem, diagnosis, or other event, situation, issue, or clinical concept that has risen to a level of concern.  The condition could be a point in time diagnosis in context of an encounter, it could be an item on the practitioner’s Problem <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link>, or it could be a concern that doesn’t exist on the practitioner’s Problem <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link>.  Often times, a condition is about a clinician's assessment and assertion of a particular aspect of a patient's state of health. It can be used to record information about a disease/illness identified from application of clinical reasoning over the pathologic and pathophysiologic findings (diagnosis), or identification of health issues/situations that a practitioner considers harmful, potentially harmful and may be investigated and managed (problem), or other health issue/situation that may require ongoing monitoring and/or management (health issue/concern). </p> <p> The condition resource may be used to record a certain health state of a patient which does not normally present a negative outcome, e.g. pregnancy.  The condition resource may be used to record a condition following a procedure, such as the condition of Amputee-BKA following an amputation procedure. </p> <p> While conditions are frequently a result of a clinician's assessment and assertion of a particular aspect of a patient's state of health, conditions can also be expressed by the patient, related person, or any care team member. A clinician may have a concern about a patient condition (e.g. anorexia) that the patient is not concerned about.  Likewise, the patient may have a condition (e.g. hair loss) that does not rise to the level of importance such that it belongs on a practitioner’s Problem <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link>. </p> <p> For example, each of the following conditions could rise to the level of importance such that it belongs on a problem or concern list due to its direct or indirect impact on the patient’s health.  These examples may also be represented using other resources, such as <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/familymemberhistory">FamilyMemberHistory</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a>, or <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a>. </p> <ul> <li>Unemployed</li> <li>Without transportation (or other barriers)</li> <li>Susceptibility to falls</li> <li>Exposure to communicable disease</li> <li>Family History of cardiovascular disease</li> <li>Fear of cancer</li> <li>Cardiac pacemaker</li> <li>Amputee-BKA</li> <li>Risk of Zika virus following travel to a country </li> <li>Former smoker</li> <li>Travel to a country planned (that warrants immunizations)</li> <li>Motor Vehicle Accident</li> <li>Patient has had coronary bypass graft</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p>     The condition resource may be referenced by other resources as "reasons" for an action (e.g. <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationrequest">MedicationRequest</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</a>, etc.) </p> <p> This resource is not typically used to record information about subjective and objective information that might lead to the recording of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</Link> resource. Such signs and symptoms are typically captured using the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a> resource; although in some cases a persistent symptom, e.g. fever, headache may be captured as a condition before a definitive diagnosis can be discerned by a clinician.   By contrast, headache may be captured as an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> when it contributes to the establishment of a meningitis <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</Link>. </p> <p> Use the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a> resource when a symptom is resolved without long term management, tracking, or when a symptom contributes to the establishment of a condition. </p> <p> Use <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</Link> when a symptom requires long term management, tracking, or is used as a proxy for a diagnosis or problem that is not yet determined. </p> <p> When the diagnosis is related to an allergy or intolerance, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</Link> and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</a> resources can both be used.  However, to be actionable for decision support, using <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</Link> alone is not sufficient as the allergy or intolerance condition needs to be represented as an <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</a>. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# Consent

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent.mdx

title: Consent
sidebar_position: 28

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';

import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
