# Consent

A record of a healthcare consumer’s choices, which permits or denies identified recipient(s) or recipient role(s) to perform one or more actions within a given policy context, for specific purposes and periods of time.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The purpose of this Resource is to be used to express a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> regarding Healthcare. There are four  anticipated uses for the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Resource, all of which are written or verbal agreements by a  healthcare consumer [grantor] or a personal representative, made to an authorized entity [grantee]  concerning authorized or restricted actions with any limitations on purpose of use, and  handling instructions to which the authorized entity must comply:  </p> <ul>  <li>Privacy <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive: Agreement to collect, access, use or disclose (share) information.</li>  <li>Medical Treatment <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive: <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> to undergo a specific treatment (or record of refusal to consent).</li>  <li>Research <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive: <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> to participate in research protocol and information sharing required.</li>  <li>Advance Care Directives: <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> to instructions for potentially needed medical treatment (e.g. DNR).</li> </ul> <p> This resource is scoped to cover all four uses, but at this time, only the privacy use case is modeled.   The scope of the resource may change when the other possible scopes are investigated, tested, or profiled. </p> <p> A FHIR <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive instance is considered the encoded legally binding <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive if it meets  requirements of a policy domain requirements for an enforceable contract.   In some domains, electronic  signatures of one or both of the parties to the content of an encoded representation of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Form  is deemed to constitute a legally binding <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive.  Some domains accept a notary’s electronic  signature over the wet or electronic signature of a party to the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive as the additional  identity proofing required to make an encoded <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive legally binding.  Other domains may  only accept a wet signature or might not require the parties’ signatures at all. </p> <p> Whatever the criteria are for making an encoded FHIR <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive legally binding, anything less  than a legally binding representation of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive must be identified as such, i.e., as a  derivative of the legally binding <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive, which has specific usage in <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive workflow management. </p> <p><b>Definitions:</b></p> <table class="grid">  <tbody><tr><td>Consent</td><td>The record of a healthcare consumer’s policy choices, which permits or denies identified recipient(s) or recipient role(s) to perform one or more actions within a given policy context, for specific purposes and periods of time</td></tr>  <tr><td>Consent Directive</td><td>The legal record of a healthcare consumer's agreement with a party responsible for enforcing the consumer’s choices, which permits or denies identified actors or roles to perform actions affecting the consumer within a given context for specific purposes and periods of time</td></tr>  <tr><td>Consent Form</td><td>Human readable consent content describing one or more actions impacting the grantor for which the grantee would be authorized or prohibited from performing.  It includes the terms, rules, and conditions pertaining to the authorization or restrictions, such as effective time, applicability or scope, purposes of use, obligations and prohibitions to which the grantee must comply. Once a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Form is “executed” by means required by policy, such as verbal agreement, wet signature, or electronic/digital signature, it becomes a legally binding <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive.</td></tr>  <tr><td>Consent Directive Derivative</td><td>Consent Content that conveys the minimal set of information needed to manage <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive workflow, including providing <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive content sufficient to: <ul><li>Represent a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive</li> <li>Register or index a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive</li> <li>Query and respond about a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive</li> <li>Retrieve a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive</li> <li>Notify authorized entities about <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive status changes</li> <li>Determine entities authorized to collect, access, use or disclose information about the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive or about the information governed by the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive.</li> </ul> <p>Derived <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> content includes the Security Labels encoding the applicable privacy and security policies.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Security Labels inform recipients about specific access control measures required for compliance.</p> </td></tr>  <tr><td>Consent Statement</td><td>A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive derivative has less than full fidelity to the legally binding <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive from which it was "transcribed".  It  provides recipients with the full content representation they may require for compliance purposes, and typically include a reference to or an attached unstructured representation for recipients needing an exact copy of the legal agreement.</td></tr>  <tr><td>Consent Registration</td><td>The legal record of a healthcare consumer's agreement with a party responsible for enforcing the consumer’s choices, which permits or denies identified actors or roles to perform actions affecting the consumer within a given context for specific purposes and periods of timeA <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive derivative that conveys the minimal set of information needed to register an active and revoked <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive, or to update <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> status as it changes during its lifecycle.</td></tr>  <tr><td>Consent Query/Response Types</td><td>The FHIR <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Resource specifies multiple <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Search parameters, which support many types of queries for <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Resource content. There are several Query/Response patterns that are typically used for obtaining information about consent directive content for the following use cases: <ul> <li>Find Active <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive:  A query that includes sufficient consent directive content to determine whether a specific party is authorized to share information governed by a consent directive with another specific party.  The Response is either: <ul> <li>“Yes” meaning that both parties are authorized to share the information with one another.</li> <li>“No” meaning that the authorized querier is not permitted to share with another specific party</li> <li>“No information found” meaning that there is no active <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive in which the querier is authorized to share the governed information.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Find <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive Authorized Entities: A query that includes sufficient consent directive content to return a list of entities with which the querier is authorized to share governed information.  The response to an authorized querier is the list of any authorized entities with which the querier is permitted to share governed information.  The response to an unauthorized querier is that “no information is found”.</li> <li>Find <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive(s): A query that includes sufficient consent directive content to return a list of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive metadata for an authorized querier to determine what <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directives are available, and to locate and retrieve one or more of those <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directives as needed.</li> </ul> </td></tr>  <tr><td>Policy context</td><td>Any organizational or jurisdictional policies, which may limit the consumer’s policy choices, and which includes the named range of actions allowed</td></tr>  <tr><td>Healthcare Consumer</td><td>The individual establishing his/her personal consent (i.e. Consenter). In FHIR, this is referred to as the 'Patient' though this word is not used across all contexts of care</td></tr> </tbody></table> <a name="PCD"></a> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Privacy <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive (PCD) <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> Privacy policies define how Individually Identifiable Health Information  (IIHI) is to be collected, accessed, used and disclosed. A Privacy <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link>  Directive as a legal record of a patient's (e.g. a healthcare consumer)  agreement with a party responsible for enforcing the patient's choices,  which permits or denies identified actors or roles to perform actions  affecting the patient within a given context for specific purposes and  periods of time. All consent directives have a policy context, which is any set of organizational or jurisdictional policies which may limit the  consumer’s policy choices, and which include a named range of actions allowed. In addition, Privacy <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directives provide the ability for a healthcare consumer  to delegate authority to a Substitute Decision Maker who may act on behalf of that individual. Alternatively, a consumer may author/publish their privacy preferences as a self-declared Privacy <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive.   </p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> resource on FHIR provides support for alternative representations for expressing  interoperable health information privacy consent directives in a standard form for the  exchange and enforcement by sending, intermediating, or receiving systems of privacy policies  that can be enforced by consuming systems (e.g., scanned documents, of computable structured  entries elements, FHIR structures with optional attached, or referenced unstructured representations.)  It may be used to represent the Privacy <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive itself, a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Statement, which  electronically represents a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive, or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Metadata, which is the minimum  necessary consent content derived from a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive for use in workflow management. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> management - particularly privacy consent - is complicated by the fact that consent to share  is often itself necessary to protect. The need to protect the privacy of the privacy statement itself competes with the execution of the consent statement. For this reason, it is common to deal with  'consent statements' that are only partial representations of the full consent statement that the  patient provided.  </p> <p> For this reason, the consent resource contains two elements that refer back to the source: a master identifier, and a direct reference to content from which this <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Statement was derived. That reference can be one of several things: </p> <ul>  <li>A reference to another consent resource from which this limited statement was derived</li>  <li>A reference to a document format for the original source (e.g. PDF or CDA - see the   <a href="http://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=280">HL7 CDAR2 ConsentDirective Implementation Guide </a>,   which incorporated the <a href="http://wiki.ihe.net/index.php?title=Basic_Patient_Privacy_Consents">IHE <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/basic">Basic</Link> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> Privacy <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consents</Link> (BPPC) </a> ), either directly, or in a reference</li>  <li>The source can be included in the consent as an attachment</li> </ul> <p> The consent statements represent a chain that refers back to the original source consent directive. Applications may be able to follow the chain back to the source but should not generally assume that they are authorized to do this. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directives are executed by verbal acknowledge or by being signed - either on paper, or digitally. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/signature">Signatures</Link> will be found in the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</a> resource (example <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/consent-example-signature.html">consent</a> and  <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/provenance-consent-signature.html">signature</a>). Implementation Guides will generally  make rules about what signatures are required, and how they are to be shared and used. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> Change to "The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> resource is structured with a base policy (represented as <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link>.policy/Consent.policyRule) which is either opt-in or opt-out, followed by a listing of exceptions to that policy (represented as <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link>.provision(s)). The exceptions can be additional positive  or negative exceptions upon the base policy. The set of exceptions include a list of data objects,  list of authors, list of recipients, list of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organizations</Link>, list of purposeOfUse, and Date <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/range">Range</Link>. </p> <p> The enforcement of the Privacy <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive is not included but is expected that  enforcement can be done using a mix of the various Access Control enforcement methodologies (e.g. OAuth, UMA, XACML). This enforcement includes the details of the enforcement meaning of the elements of the Privacy <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> Directive,  such as the rules in place when there is an opt-in consent would be specific about which  organizational roles have access to what kinds of resources (e.g. RBAC, ABAC).  The specification of these details is not in scope for the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> resource. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# Contract

# Contract

Legally enforceable, formally recorded unilateral or bilateral directive i.e., a policy or agreement.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> This resource allows for the instantiation of various types of legally enforceable agreements or policies as shareable, consumable, and executable artifacts as well as precursory content upon which instances may be based or derivative artifacts supporting management of their basal instance. The resource is general enough to encode broad range of legal artifacts such as: </p> <ul>  <li>A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> instance, which may undergo legal state transitions during its formation.</li> <li>Templates for or agreed upon instances of rules, obligations, and prohibitions.</li> <li>An organizational or jurisdictional policy, for example, for establishing rules of conduct or obligations necessary to achieve societal goods. Or it may encode a contract instance, which may be accepted by one party in exchange of considerations offered by another party.</li> <li>A derivative of a contract instance for purposes of workflow management of the agreement, e.g., for retrieval or indication of agreed upon terms, such as entities allowed to exchange governed assets.</li> </ul> <p>Contracts are promises or understandings that are enforceable by law in case of any violation or breech by any involved party or organization. A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link>  instance may be a unilateral mandate such as a policy, or a unilateral, bilateral, or multilateral agreement, which impacts the influence of the parties over the terms of the agreement, and the burdens and risks incurred.  </p>   <p>Contract Resource may be typed to support multiple types of domain policies and contractual agreements, and specializations of those types. </p>   <p>A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> instance must include at least one term with an offer, which obligates the offerer to or not to do, perform, or effectuate some action in exchange for some consideration in return from the offeree, e.g., another obligatory action or non-action, or an asset.  </p>   <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> action element follows the Request Pattern to describe the proposal, plan, or order to effectuate the obligatory service or activity specified in a term’s offer.  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> action may reference and specify the roles for one or more target entities, the requesters, and performers.  By following the Request Pattern, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> provides the criteria needed to assess whether the contract obligations have been enforced, for example, in the case of a privacy policy, by an access control system. </p> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> asset element supports detailed description of the consideration being exchanged in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> instance or the satisfaction of a policy imperative such as the obligation to render aid as required by local law. </p>   <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> valuedItem element supports detailed description of the monetary worth of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> asset being marketed, the price of products being sold, or the property taxes required under a jurisdictional tax law. </p>   <p>A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> may be used as a content derivative, which contains the minimal content derived from the basal information source at a specific stage in its lifecycle, which is needed  for management and communications about the basal information source. For example, the metadata used to register a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link>’s characteristics and retrieval address in a federated registry/repository exchange ecosystem. </p>   <p>In addition to other uses of derivatives, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> Resource may function simply as the computable representation of the executed contract, which may be the attached to the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> Resource as the 'legally binding' scanned paper contract attachment or referenced location, or as the 'friendly' electronic form such as an html page or a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaireresponse">QuestionnaireResponse</Link>.  </p>   <p>By using the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> linkID elements, which are associated with key <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> elements, a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> Resource may be automatically populated with the values expressed in a related <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaireresponse">QuestionnaireResponse</Link>. </p>   <p>Note that the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> Resource may be considered the legally binding contract only if it is intended to be the sole 'executed' encoding of this contract, and includes the legally binding signatures. I.e., even if the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> Resource is populated based on content in a hard-copy contract or an electronic contract form intended to collect both the content and the signature of relevant parties to the contract, if contracting parties have agreed or acknowledged that the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> Resource conveys the binding and enforceable legal contract and that it is fully traceable to the forms used to collect its content, meeting the legal concept of being within the 'four corners of a contract', i.e., that the meaning of the contract, will, or deed is represented solely by this instance of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> Resource. This usage could be implemented with digital ledger technology to form a 'smart contract' to the extent that an instance supports elements critical to computable algorithms intended to achieve some output. </p> <p>Where the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> resource applies, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> resource should be used. Where a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> exists for a consent directive then if a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> for this also exists the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</Link> shall reference the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link>. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <ul> <li>Contracts are used to record in machine processible form a legal agreement between parties</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> Implementers should be familiar with legal concepts, <a href="http://iang.org/papers/ricardian_contract.html">Ricardian <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contracts</Link> </a> and have a general knowledge of recording agreements. </p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Legal State Machine <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/contract.html#13.11.3.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p>   This Resource supports tracking of the progress of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> instance during its lifecycle as a 'legal instrument' from inception as a draft, possibly based on a definitional contract template to negotiations and the various permutation on term elements that may occur, on to execution.  Then it follows the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> as enforceable obligations, which may be breached, disputed, or modified, until the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> reaches renewal, termination, or revocation.   This is flow is orthogonal to the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link>.status, which tracks the progress of the documentation of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</Link> whether it is definitional, a derivative, or an instance.  The legal state value set specifies the characteristics of these states based on legal definitions. </p> <div> </div> </div>
  </TabItem>

# CoverageEligibilityRequest

The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityrequest">CoverageEligibilityRequest</Link> provides patient and insurance coverage information to an insurer for them to respond, in the form of an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityresponse">CoverageEligibilityResponse</Link>, with information regarding whether the stated coverage is valid and in-force and optionally to provide the insurance details of the policy.

  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityrequest">CoverageEligibilityRequest</Link> makes a request of an insurer asking them to provide, in the form of an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityresponse">CoverageEligibilityResponse</Link>,  information regarding: (validation) whether the specified coverage(s) is valid and in-force; (discovery) what coverages the insurer has for the specified patient; (benefits) the benefits provided under the coverage; whether benefits exist under the specified coverage(s) for specified classes of services and products; and (auth-requirements)  whether preauthorization is required, and if so what information may be required in that preauthorization, for the specified service classes or services. </p> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityrequest">CoverageEligibilityRequest</Link> resource is a "event" resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">Workflow Event.</a></p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Additional Information <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/coverageeligibilityrequest.html#13.2.1.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> Additional information regarding electronic coverage eligibility content and usage may be found at: </p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#resource-status">Financial Resource Status Lifecycle</a>: how .status is used in the financial resources.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#subrogation">Subrogation</a>: how eClaims may handle patient insurance coverages when another insurer rather than  the provider will settle the claim and potentially recover costs against specified coverages.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#cob">Coordination of Benefit</a>: how eClaims may handle multiple patient insurance coverages.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#batch">Batches</a>: how eClaims may handle batches of eligibility, claims and responses.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#attachments">Attachments and Supporting Information</a>: how eClaims may handle the provision of supporting  information, whether provided by content or reference, within the eClaim resource when submitted to the payor or later in a resource which refers  to the subject eClaim resource. This includes how payors how request additional supporting information from providers.</li> </ul> </div>

at this or a specified date, or requesting the benefit details or preauthorization requirements associated with a coverage. </p> <p> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</a> resource adjudication or authorization is requested.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverage">Coverage</a></td> <td>Provides the high-level identifiers and descriptors of an insurance # CoverageEligibilityResponse

This resource provides eligibility and plan details from the processing of an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityrequest">CoverageEligibilityRequest</Link> resource.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}

  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityresponse">CoverageEligibilityResponse</Link> resource provides eligibility and plan details from the processing of an  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityrequest">CoverageEligibilityRequest</Link> resource. It combines key information from a payor as to whether a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverage">Coverage</Link> is  in-force, and optionally the nature of the Policy benefit details as well as the ability for the insurer to indicate whether  the insurance provides benefits for requested types of services or requires preauthorization and if so what supporting information may be required. </p> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityresponse">CoverageEligibilityResponse</Link> resource is a "event" resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">Workflow Event.</a></p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Additional Information <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/coverageeligibilityresponse.html#13.3.1.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> Additional information regarding electronic coverage eligibility content and usage may be found at: </p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#resource-status">Financial Resource Status Lifecycle</a>: how .status is used in the financial resources.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#subrogation">Subrogation</a>: how eClaims may handle patient insurance coverages when another insurer rather than  the provider will settle the claim and potentially recover costs against specified coverages.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#cob">Coordination of Benefit</a>: how eClaims may handle multiple patient insurance coverages.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#batch">Batches</a>: how eClaims may handle batches of eligibility, claims and responses.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#attachments">Attachments and Supporting Information</a>: how eClaims may handle the provision of supporting  information, whether provided by content or reference, within the eClaim resource when submitted to the payor or later in a resource which refers  to the subject eClaim resource. This includes how payors how request additional supporting information from providers.</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityresponse">CoverageEligibilityResponse</Link> should be used to respond to a  request on whether the patient's coverage is inforce, whether it is valid at this or a specified date, or to report the benefit details or preauthorization requirements associated with a coverage. </p> <p>When requesting whether the patient's coverage is inforce, whether it is valid at this or a specified date, or requesting the benefit details or preauthorization requirements  associated with a coverage <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityrequest">CoverageEligibilityRequest</a> should be used instead.</p> <p> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</a> resource is an insurer's adjudication and/or authorization of a set of healthcare-related goods and services for a patient against the patient's insurance coverages. </p> <p> For reporting out to patients or transferring data to patient centered applications, such as patient health Record (PHR) application, the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</a>  should be used . </p> <p> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverage">Coverage</a> resource contains the information typically found on the health insurance card for an individual used to identify the covered individual to the insurer and is referred to by the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityresponse">CoverageEligibilityResponse</Link>. </p> <p> <b>The eClaim domain includes a number of related resources</b> </p> <table border="1" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="2" frame="box"> <tbody><tr> <td>CoverageEligibilityResponse</td> <td>Patient and insurance coverage information provided to an insurer for them to respond, in the form of an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityresponse">CoverageEligibilityResponse</Link>, with information regarding whether the stated coverage is valid and in-force and optionally to provide the insurance details of the policy.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</a></td> <td>A payor's adjudication and/or authorization response to the suite of services provided in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>. Typically the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> references the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> but does not duplicate the clinical or financial information provided in the claim.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityrequest">CoverageEligibilityRequest</a></td> <td>Patient and insurance coverage information provided to an insurer for them to respond, in the form of an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityresponse">CoverageEligibilityResponse</Link>, with information regarding whether the stated coverage is valid and in-force and optionally to provide the insurance details of the policy.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverage">Coverage</a></td> <td>Provides the high-level identifiers and descriptors of an insurance plan, typically the information which would appear on an insurance card, which may be used to pay, in part or in whole, for the provision of health care products and services.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</a></td> <td>This resource combines the information from the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> and the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link>, stripping out any provider or payor proprietary information, into a unified information model  suitable for use for: patient reporting; transferring information to a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> Health Record system; and, supporting complete claim and adjudication information exchange  with regulatory and analytics organizations and other parts of the provider's organization. </td> </tr> </tbody></table> </div>

# DetectedIssue

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/detectedissue.mdx

title: DetectedIssue

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';

# DetectedIssue

Indicates an actual or potential clinical issue with or between one or more active or proposed clinical actions for a patient; e.g. Drug-drug interaction, Ineffective treatment frequency, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</Link>-condition conflict, etc.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p><strong>This resource is an <em>event</em> resource from a FHIR workflow perspective</strong> - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">Workflow</a>, specifically <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">Event</a>.</p> <p> This resource applies to various circumstances where there is a concern about an existing or proposed set of clinical activity.  The issue could relate to single, proposed, or multiple actions.   It does not apply to technical issues (e.g. lack of user permissions) but could relate to violation of patient consent limitations.  Examples include: </p> <ul>   <li>Drug-drug interactions</li>   <li>Inappropriate therapy (wrong dose, frequency, body site)</li>   <li>Duplicate therapy</li> </ul>    <p> This resource represents a specific instance of a potential issue for a particular patient. It is <b>not</b> intended to represent general patient-independent knowledge. This resource is also <b>not</b> intended to be used in defining general prohibitions on actions such as "No NSAIDs", "No solid oral dose forms" or "No MRIs - metallic tattoos".   These guidelines can be captured using the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</a>, and/or <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flag</a> resources.   Similarly, this resource is not to be used to capture clinical facts that may imply contraindications such as pregnancy, breast feeding, patient preferences, past procedures, etc.  These would be represented using <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a> or other resources. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> This resource only applies to documenting a risk associated with a specific planned or ongoing action, or the lack of an action which should be planned - not a general propensity to risk. The latter would be handled using <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</a> for substance-specific issues or <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flag</a> for other types of issues. In addition, the resource represents patient-specific and time-bound risk manifestations, not generic knowledge statements about risks that can exist. </p> <p>This resource is limited to clinical issues associated with a proposed or ongoing action.  It does not cover technical issues such as lack of permission, duplicate identifiers, insufficient data, and other business rule violations. Technical issues are conveyed using the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationoutcome">OperationOutcome</a> resource.   It is possible to have both <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationoutcome">OperationOutcome</a> and <code>DetectedIssue</code> together, where the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationoutcome">OperationOutcome</Link> might  indicate that a requested action was rejected due to a clinical issue and the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/detectedissue">DetectedIssue</Link> provides the details of the issue.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> Detected issues are typically identified by decision support systems.  However, they may also be captured directly by clinicians.  The latter typically happens for one of two reasons: </p> <ol>   <li>A clinician wishes to communicate an issue to another clinician whose responsibility would be to resolve it (e.g. a pharmacist identifying an issue with a prescription prior to putting it on hold)</li>   <li>A clinician wishes to pre-emptively identify that an issue is known and is being managed (to avoid red flags being raised as part of downstream workflow); e.g. Submitting a new order and including a link to    a "duplicate therapy" issue with mitigation indicating that the therapy is not considered to be duplicate.</li> </ol> <p> Decision-support generated issues can result from calling a decision-support engine directly (e.g. via a custom <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationdefinition">OperationDefinition</a>) or as part of an attempt to perform some other function (creating an order, submitting an insurance claim, capturing a medication list).  When the issues are generated as a by-product of performing some other sort of action, they may be included in the "response" to the requested action in the same manner as an <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationoutcome">OperationOutcome</a>.  In fact, both may be present - the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationoutcome">OperationOutcome</a> indicating that there was a warning or error associated with the request and a <b>DetectedIssue</b> providing the clinical details.  (The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationoutcome">OperationOutcome</a> could point to the <b>DetectedIssue</b> via an extension.) </p> <p> In those circumstances where requested operations are rejected as a result of a detected issue, the workflow may support allowing the operation to be re-tried, provided that the identified issue is included as part of the submission (possibly also including a mitigation).  In doing so, the sender acknowledges the issue and takes responsibility for it, thus allowing the requested operation to proceed.  See <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/#linking">Linking to Detected Issues</a> for guidance on how a <b>DetectedIssue</b> instance might be included as part of another operation. </p> <p> Systems that require such workflows should document expected behavior as part of their <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/capabilitystatement">CapabilityStatement</a> declarations. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationdispense">MedicationDispense</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationknowledge">MedicationKnowledge</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationrequest">MedicationRequest</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# Device

A type of a manufactured item that is used in the provision of healthcare without being substantially changed through that activity. The device may be a medical or non-medical device. For more on implantable devices, refer to [US Core Implantable Device Profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-implantable-device.html).

It is referenced by other resources for recording which device performed an action such as a procedure or an observation, referenced when prescribing and dispensing devices for patient use or for ordering supplies, and used to record and transmit <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/#udi">Unique <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/device">Device</Link> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/identifier">Identifier</Link> (UDI)</a> information about a device such as a patient's implant. </p> </div>

The physical composition of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/device">Device</Link> is represented by the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/device">Devices</Link> pointing to their "parent". </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/device">Devices</Link> differ from medications because they are not "used up" - they remain active in a patient in an ongoing fashion.  However, the specific boundary between medications and devices is defined at the implementation level and this standard does not enforce a boundary with the exception of devices that are implanted in a patient.   The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medication">Medication</a> resource should not be used to represent implanted devices. </p> </div>

# DeviceRequest

Represents a request for a patient to employ a medical device. The device may be an implantable device, or an external assistive device, such as a walker.

  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <a name="dstu"></a> <blockquote class="stu-note"><p><b>Trial-Use Note:</b> In terms of scope and usage, the  Orders and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observations</Link> workgroups wish to draw the attention of reviewers and implementers to the following issue: </p> <ol> <li>  We are seeking input from the implementation community on whether to combine <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/devicerequest">DeviceRequest</Link> and  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/visionprescription">VisionPrescription</a> for R4.  The <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/devicerequest-definitions.html#parameters">parameters</a> element  was added to <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/devicerequest">DeviceRequest</Link> for representing custom details for ordering devices.  With this change,  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/visionprescription">VisionPrescription</Link> significantly overlaps  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/devicerequest">DeviceRequest</Link>. To illustrate this, the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/devicerequest-left-lens.html">devicerequest-left-lens</a> and <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/devicerequest-right-lens.html">devicerequest-right-lens</a> examples are based on the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/visionprescription-example.html">general glasses example</a> in <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/visionprescription">VisionPrescription</Link>.    </li> </ol> </blockquote> <p> <strong>This resource is a <em>request</em> resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">Workflow</a>.</strong> </p> <p>         This resource describes the request for the use of a device by a patient. The device may be any         pertinent device specified in the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/device">Device</Link> resource. Examples of devices that may be requested         include wheelchair, hearing aids, or an insulin pump. The request may lead to the dispensing         of the device to the patient or for use by the patient.         </p> <p>         The device use request may represent an order or a prescription entered by a practitioner in a CPOE         system or a proposal made by a clinical decision support (CDS) system based         on a patient's clinical record and context of care.         </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> This resource deals with the allocation of a device to a patient and while it may contain instructions on how to use the device, the data about getting the device to the patient is addressed in other resources.  For example, certain devices must be implanted via a surgical or other procedure and the implantation or explantation is represented in the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</Link> or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</Link> resource. </p> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/supplyrequest">SupplyRequest</Link> resource is similar in that it deals with requesting a particular item for a specific patient. However, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/devicerequest">DeviceRequest</Link> is concerned with items where there is a patient focus, or instructions regarding their use, whereas <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/supplyrequest">SupplyRequest</Link> is concerned with inventory management.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# DiagnosticReport

The findings and interpretation of diagnostic tests performed on patients, groups of patients, devices, and locations, and/or specimens derived from these. The report includes clinical context such as requesting and provider information, and some mix of atomic results, images, textual and coded interpretations, and formatted representation of diagnostic reports. Refer to the [US Core DiagnosticReport profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-diagnosticreport-note.html) for Report and Note exchange.

<Tabs queryString="section">

## Inherited Elements

  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p><strong>This resource is an <em>event</em> resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">Workflow</a>.   It is the intent of the Orders and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> Workgroup to align this resource with  the workflow pattern for <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event"><em>event</em> resources</a>.</strong></p> <p> A diagnostic report is the set of information that is typically provided by a diagnostic service when investigations are complete. The information includes a mix of atomic results, text reports, images, and codes. The mix varies depending on the nature of the diagnostic procedure, and sometimes on the nature of the outcomes for a particular investigation.  In FHIR, the report can be conveyed in a variety of ways including a <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/documents.html">Document</a>, <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/http.html">RESTful API</a>, or <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/messaging.html">Messaging </a> framework.  Included within each of these, would be the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> resource itself. </p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> resource has information about the diagnostic report itself, and about the subject and, in the case of laboratory tests, the specimen of the report.  It can also refer to the request details and atomic observations details or image instances.  Report conclusions can be expressed as a simple text blob, structured coded data or as an attached fully formatted report such as a PDF.</p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> resource is suitable for the following kinds of diagnostic reports: </p> <ul>  <li>Laboratory (Clinical Chemistry, Hematology, Microbiology, etc.)</li>  <li>Pathology / Histopathology / related disciplines</li>  <li>Imaging Investigations (x-ray, CT, MRI etc.)</li>  <li>Other diagnostics - Cardiology, Gastroenterology etc.</li> </ul> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> resource is not intended to support cumulative result presentation (tabular presentation of past and present results in the resource). The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> resource does not yet provide full support for detailed structured reports of sequencing; this is planned for a future release. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> Note that many diagnostic processes are procedures that generate observations and diagnostic reports. In many cases, such an observation does not require an explicit representation of the procedure used to create the observation, but where there are details of interest about how the diagnostic procedure was performed, the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a> resource is used to describe the activity. </p> <p> In contrast to the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a> resource, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> resource typically includes additional clinical context and some mix of atomic results, images, imaging reports, textual and coded interpretation, and formatted representations. Laboratory reports, pathology reports, and imaging reports should be represented using the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> resource. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> resource is referenced by the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> to provide the atomic results for a particular investigation. </p> <p> If you have a highly structured report, then use <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> - it has data and workflow support.  Details about the request for a diagnostic investigation are captured in the various "request" resources (e.g., the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</a>) and allow the report to connect to clinical workflows. For more narrative driven reports with less work flow (histology/mortuary, etc.), the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</a> resource would be more appropriate. </p> <p> Image and media representations of the report and supporting images are referenced in the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> resource.  The details and actual image instances can be referenced directly in Diagnostic report using the "imaging" element or by indirect reference through the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/imagingstudy">ImagingStudy</a> resources which represent the content produced in a DICOM imaging study or set of DICOM Instances for a patient. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a>    <b>Diagnostic Report Names</b> <p> The words "tests", "results", "observations", "panels" and "batteries" are often used interchangeably when describing the various parts of a diagnostic report. This leads to much confusion. The naming confusion is worsened because of the wide variety of forms that the result of a diagnostic investigation can take, as described above. Languages other than English have their own variations on this theme. </p> <p> This resource uses one particular set of terms. A practitioner "requests" a set of "tests". The diagnostic service returns a "report" which may contain a "narrative" - a written summary of the outcomes, and/or "results" - the individual pieces of atomic data which each are "observations". The results are assembled in "groups" which are nested structures of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observations</Link> (traditionally referred to as "panels" or " batteries" by laboratories) that can be used to represent relationships between the individual data items. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# DocumentReference

# DocumentReference

A reference to a document of any kind for any purpose. Provides metadata about the document so that the document can be discovered and managed. The scope of a document is any seralized object with a mime-type, so includes formal patient centric documents (CDA), clinical notes, scanned paper, and non-patient specific documents like policy text. Refer to the [US Core DocumentReference profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-documentreference.html).

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p>  A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/documentreference">DocumentReference</Link> resource is used to index a document, clinical note, and other binary objects  to make them available to a healthcare system.  A document is some sequence of bytes that is identifiable, establishes its own context (e.g., what subject,  author, etc. can be displayed to the user), and has defined update management. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/documentreference">DocumentReference</Link> resource can be  used with any document format that has a recognized mime type and that conforms to this definition. </p> <p> Typically, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/documentreference">DocumentReference</Link> resources are used in document indexing systems, such as <a href="http://wiki.ihe.net/index.php?title=Cross-Enterprise_Document_Sharing">IHE XDS </a>, such as profiled in <a href="http://wiki.ihe.net/index.php/Mobile_access_to_Health_Documents_(MHD)">IHE Mobile access to Health Documents </a>. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/documentreference">DocumentReference</Link> is metadata describing a document such as:</p> <ul>  <li><a href="http://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=7">CDA </a> documents in FHIR systems</li>  <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/documents.html">FHIR documents</a> stored elsewhere (i.e. registry/repository following the XDS model)</li>  <li><a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portable_Document_Format">PDF documents </a>, Scanned Paper, and digital records of faxes</li>  <li>Clinical Notes in various forms</li>  <li>Image files (e.g., JPEG, GIF, TIFF)</li>  <li>Non-Standard formats (e.g., WORD)</li>  <li>Other kinds of documents, such as records of prescriptions or immunizations</li>  </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> FHIR defines both a <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/documents.html">document format</a> and this document reference. FHIR documents are for documents  that are authored and assembled in FHIR. This resource is mainly intended for general references to assembled documents.  </p> <p> The document that is a target of the reference can be a reference to a FHIR document served by another server, or  the target can be stored in the special <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/http.html#binary">FHIR <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/binary">Binary</Link> Resource</a>, or the target can be  stored on some other server system. The document reference is also able to address documents that are retrieved  by a service call such as an XDS.b RetrieveDocumentSet, or a DICOM exchange, or an <a href="http://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=185">HL7 v2 </a> message query - though  the way each of these service calls works must be specified in some external standard or other documentation. </p> <p> A <code>DocumentReference</code> describes some other document. This means that there are two sets of  provenance information relevant here: the provenance of the document, and the provenance of the document reference. Sometimes, the provenance information is closely related, as when the document producer also  produces the document reference, but in other workflows, the document reference is generated later by other actors. In the <code>DocumentReference</code> resource, the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/resource.html#Meta">meta</a> content refers to the provenance of the reference itself, while the content described below concerns the document it references. Like all resources, there is overlap between the information in the  resource directly, and in the general <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</a> resource. This is  discussed as <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">part of the description of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resource</a>. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/effectevidencesynthesis">EffectEvidenceSynthesis</Link> resource describes the difference in an outcome between exposures states in a population where the effect estimate is derived from a combination of research studies.

Effect estimates are a measure of difference between the exposure state and an alternative exposure state (often called the control or comparator state) Expressing effect estimates is done throughout reporting of biomedical research, systematic reviews, and clinical reference across all disciplines.    </p> </div>

# Encounter

An interaction between a patient and healthcare provider(s) for the purpose of providing healthcare service(s) or assessing the health status of a patient. Refer to the US Core [Encounter](http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/StructureDefinition-us-core-encounter.html) Profile and the US Core [Condition Encounter](http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/StructureDefinition-us-core-condition-encounter-diagnosis.html) profile.

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p>  A patient encounter is further characterized by the setting in which it takes place. Amongst them are ambulatory,  emergency, home health, inpatient and virtual encounters. An <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link> encompasses the lifecycle from pre-admission,   the actual encounter (for ambulatory encounters), and admission, stay and discharge (for inpatient encounters).  During the encounter the patient may move from practitioner to practitioner and location to location. </p> <p> Because of the broad scope of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link>, not all elements will be relevant in all settings. For this reason,  admission/discharge related information is kept in a separate Hospitalization component within <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link>.  The <i>class</i> element is used to distinguish between these settings, which will guide further validation and application of business rules. </p> <p> There is also substantial variance from organization to organization (and between jurisdictions and countries)  on which business events translate to the start of a new <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link>, or what level of aggregation is used for <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link>. For example, each single visit of a practitioner during a hospitalization may lead to a new instance of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link>, but depending on local practice and the systems involved, it may well be that this is aggregated to a single instance for a whole hospitalization. Even more aggregation may occur where jurisdictions introduce groups of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounters</Link> for financial or other reasons. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounters</Link> can be aggregated or grouped under other <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounters</Link> using the <i>partOf</i> element.  See <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/#examples">below</a> for examples. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link> instances may exist before the actual encounter takes place to convey pre-admission information, including using <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounters</Link> elements to reflect the planned start date or planned encounter locations. In  this case the <i>status</i> element is set to 'planned'. </p> <p> The Hospitalization component is intended to store the extended information relating to a hospitalization event. It is always expected to be the same period as the encounter itself. Where the period is different, another encounter instance should be used to capture this information as a partOf this encounter instance. </p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</Link> and encounter have references to each other, and these should be to different procedures; one for the procedure that was performed during the encounter (stored in <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</Link>.encounter), and another for cases where an encounter is a result of another procedure (stored in <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link>.indication) such as a follow-up encounter to resolve complications from an earlier procedure. </p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Status Management <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/encounter.html#8.11.1.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> During the life-cycle of an encounter it will pass through many statuses. Typically these are in order or the organization's workflow: planned, in-progress, finished/cancelled.<br/> This status information is often used for other things, and often an analysis of the status history is required. This could be done by scanning through all the versions of the encounter, checking the period of each, and then doing some form of post processing. To ease the burden of this (or where a system doesn't support resource histories) a status history component is included. </p> <p> There is no direct indication purely by the status field as to whether an encounter is considered "admitted".<br/> The context of the encounter and business practices/policies/workflows/types can influence this definition. (e.g., acute care facility, aged care center, outpatient clinic, emergency department, community-based clinic).<br/> Statuses of "arrived", "triaged" or "in progress" could be considered the start of the admission, and also have the  presence of the hospitalization sub-component entered. </p> <p> The "on leave" status might or might not be a part of the admission, for example if the patient  was permitted to go home for a weekend or some other form of external event.<br/> The location is also likely to be filled in with a location status of "present".<br/> For other examples such as an outpatient visit (day procedure - colonoscopy), the patient could also be  considered to be admitted, hence the encounter doesn't have a fixed definition of admitted. At a minimum, we do believe that a patient IS admitted when the status is in-progress. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p>  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link> resource is not to be used to store appointment information, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/appointment">Appointment</Link> resource is intended to be used for that. Note that in many systems outpatient encounters (which are in scope for <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link>) and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/appointment">Appointment</Link> are used  concurrently. In FHIR, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/appointment">Appointment</Link> is used for establishing a date for the encounter, while <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link> is  applicable to information about the actual <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link>, i.e., the patient showing up.<br/> As such, an encounter in the "planned" status is not identical to the appointment that scheduled it, but it is the encounter prior to its actual occurrence, with the expectation that encounter will be updated as it progresses to completion. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> arrival at a location does not necessarily mean the start of the encounter (e.g. a patient arrives an hour earlier than he is actually seen by a practitioner). </p> <p> An appointment is normally used for the planning stage of an appointment, searching, locating an available time, then making the appointment. Once this process is completed and the appointment is about to start, then the appointment will be marked as fulfilled, and linked to the newly created encounter.<br/> This new encounter may start in an "arrived" status when they are admitted at a location of the facility, and then will move to the ward where another part-of encounter may begin. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communication">Communication</Link> resources are used for a simultaneous interaction between a practitioner and a patient where there is no direct contact. Examples include a phone message, or transmission of some correspondence documentation.<br/> There is no duration recorded for a communication resource, but it could contain sent and received times. </p> <p> Standard <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/extension">Extension</Link>: <b>Associated <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link></b><br/> This extension should be used to reference an encounter where there is no property that already defines this association on the resource. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# Endpoint

The technical details of an endpoint that can be used for electronic services, such as for web services providing XDS.b or a REST endpoint for another FHIR server. This may include any security context information.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a>          <p>         An endpoint describes the technical details of a location that can be connected to for the delivery/retrieval of information.         Sufficient information is required to ensure that a connection can be made securely, and appropriate data transmitted as         defined by the endpoint owner. This is not a description of details of the current system, as found in <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/capabilitystatement">CapabilityStatement</a>, but of         another (potentially external) system.<br/>         These may be locally hosted services, regional services, or national service.     </p>     <p>       These resources are typically used to identify where to locate endpoint details for:     </p>     <ul>       <li>Questionnaires: Where to send information (currently an SDC extension with just the address)</li>       <li>ValueSet: Where related Terminology Services can be found (where not local)</li>       <li>Subscription: The destination to send the subscribed data (or to pull)</li>       <li>Messaging: (currently defined in the Message Header, but only as the address)</li>       <li>Referrals: Where to send referral requests<br/>           (linked to the services directory resources - <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link>/Location/Practitioner/HealthcareService)</li>       <li>Referrals - Templates: Where to locate referral templates (Questionnaires)<br/>           (linked to the services directory resources - <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link>/Location/Practitioner/HealthcareService)</li>       <li>CarePlans: Where a shared <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</Link> can be found</li>       <li>Scheduling: Where to lookup to discover schedules/availability information<br/>           (linked to the services directory resources - <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link>/Location/Practitioner/HealthcareService)</li>       <li>Scheduling: Where to lookup to send appointment requests<br/>           (linked to the services directory resources - <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link>/Location/Practitioner/HealthcareService)</li>       <li>Patient/Person: <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/location">Location</Link> of Master <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link>/Person Indexes</li>       <li>Service Provider Directories: <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/location">Location</Link> of related directories (parent/child/federated) </li>   <li>DICOM/imaging: <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/location">Location</Link> of where to query for imaging content and metadata (QIDO-RS, WADO-RS, or WADO-URI)</li>     </ul>   </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div>      <a name="bnr"></a>  <h3 class="self-link-parent"> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/capabilitystatement">CapabilityStatement</Link> <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/endpoint" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3>     <p>       The endpoint is distinct from a capability statement in that the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/capabilitystatement">CapabilityStatement</Link> statement describes the entire capability       of a server (and in the metadata case, just this server)<br/>       Where the endpoint resource describes the technical details for how to connect, and for what purposes        (which could be a small sub-set of the server's capabilities, and might not be a FHIR endpoint).     </p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/contactpoint">ContactPoint</Link> <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/endpoint.html#8.9.2.2" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/endpoint">Endpoints</Link> are used to facilitate system to system communication, providing the details of the addressing of the system, purpose of use,    protocols required/provided, and any other details required to communicate between the systems. (such as configuration parameters,    require headers ...) The address value in the endpoint can only be used in the context of the provided details. </p><p> E.g. If the endpoint has a URL for an XDS service, using that in a browser by a user is meaningless. </p><p> E.g.2 If the endpoint has a US Direct address, using this to send a normal email message will not work, as they are not true email addresses (even though they appear to be) </p><p> A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/contactpoint">ContactPoint</Link> contains contact information, such as a phone number, web address that a user can directly interact with, no additional  information would be required to use the value. The value is generally used to communicate with an entity directly, not a system. </p>   </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div>  <a name="bnc"></a>         <p>     </p>     <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Expected Implementations <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/endpoint.html#8.9.3.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3>     <ul>       <li>Any solution where there are distributed FHIR servers deployed and need discovery/configuration</li>       <li>(Refer to the scope and usage section for common uses)</li>     </ul>   </div>
  </TabItem>

# EpisodeOfCare

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare.mdx

title: EpisodeOfCare
sidebar_position: 47

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
