# EpisodeOfCare

An association between a patient and an organization / healthcare provider(s) during which time encounters may occur. The managing organization assumes a level of responsibility for the patient during this time.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a>          <p>       The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link> Resource contains information about an association of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> with a Healthcare Provider for a period       of time under which related healthcare activities may occur.     </p>     <p>       In many cases, this represents a period of time where the Healthcare Provider has some level of responsibility for the care       of the patient regarding a specific condition or problem, even if not currently participating in an encounter.     </p>     <p>       These resources are typically known in existing systems as:     </p>     <ul>       <li>EpisodeOfCare: Case, Program, Problem, Episode</li>       <li>Encounter: Visit, Contact</li>     </ul>     <p></p>     <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Multiple <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organizations</Link> and Transfer of Care <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/episodeofcare.html#8.10.1.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3>     <p>       Many organizations can be involved in an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link>; however each organization will have its own <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link> resource instance       that tracks its responsibility with the patient.     </p>     <p>       When an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link> completes their involvement with the patient and transfers care to another <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link>.       This is often in the form of a referral to another <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link> (or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organizations</Link>).<br/>     </p>     <p>       When an incoming referral is received a new <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link> may be created for this organization.       The initial step(s) in the intake workflow for the referral often involve some form of assessment(s),       eligibility, capacity, care levels, which could take some time.<br/>       Once the intake process is completed and the patient is accepted, a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</Link> is often created.     </p>   </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div>  <a name="bnr"></a>         <p>       The primary difference between the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link> and the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link> is that the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link> records the details of an       activity directly relating to the patient, while the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link> is the container that can link a series of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounters</Link>       together for problems/issues.<br/>       The Example scenarios below give some good examples as to when you might want to be using an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link>.     </p>     <p>       This difference is a similar difference between the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link> and a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</Link>.        The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link> is a tracking resource, rather than a planning resource.<br/>       The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link> usually exists before the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</Link>.       You don't need a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</Link> to use an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link>.     </p>   </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div>  <a name="bnc"></a>         <p>       Systems collect a coherent group of activities (such as encounters) related to a patient's health condition or problem often referred to as a Care Episode.       Information about an episode is often shared across systems, and in some cases organizational and disciplinary boundaries.       An <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link> contains details about the purpose of the care and can exist without any activities.<br/>       The minimal information that would be required in an episode of care would be a patient, organization and a reason for the ongoing association.       Other reasons for creating an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link> could be for tracking the details required for government reporting or billing.     </p>     <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Expected Implementations <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/episodeofcare.html#8.10.3.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3>     <ul>       <li>Chronic Disease Management Systems</li>       <li>         Community Care Systems         <ul>           <li>Tracking progress of a specific condition</li>           <li>Tracking government funding</li>         </ul>       </li>       <li>Problem based General Practice systems</li>       <li>Disability Support Systems</li>       <li>Aged Care Systems (Community and Residential)</li>     </ul>   </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitem">ChargeItem</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/documentreference">DocumentReference</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</a></li>

<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationdispense">MedicationDispense</a></li>

# EventDefinition

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/eventdefinition.mdx

title: EventDefinition
sidebar_position: 48

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

# Evidence

The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/evidence">Evidence</Link> resource describes the conditional state (population and any exposures being compared within the population) and outcome (if specified) that the knowledge (evidence, assertion, recommendation) is about.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p>The scope of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/evidence">Evidence</Link> resource is to describe the conditional state (population and exposures being considered or compared within a population) with or without the outcomes that knowledge (evidence, assertion, recommendation) is about. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/evidence">Evidence</Link> resource is a commonly bundled series of evidence variables from the "PICO" specification of medical knowledge: <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/population">Population</Link> - the population within which exposures and outcomes are being considered  Intervention - the conditional state or exposure state being described for which one is expressing the risk of or effect on an outcome  Comparison - the alternative conditional state or alternative exposure state when one is comparing states for the effect on an outcome  Outcome - the result or effect of an intervention or exposure in a population PICO (and its variants like PECO or PICOT) is a universal acronym used in evidence-based medicine communities to clearly express research questions and evidence findings. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/evidence">Evidence</Link> resource allows expression of the higher-order concept for recommendations in healthcare where multiple outcomes are considered, and the higher-order concept/combination for framing research questions.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/evidence">Evidence</Link> resource references the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/evidencevariable">EvidenceVariable</Link> resource two or more times to clearly specify the relationship among evidence variable concepts in framing a research question, evidence assertion, or recommendation.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>

</Tabs>

# ExplanationOfBenefit

This resource provides: the claim details; adjudication details from the processing of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>; and optionally account balance information, for informing the subscriber of the benefits provided.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</Link> (EOB) resource combines key information from a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>, a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> and optional <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/account">Account</Link> information to inform  a patient of the goods and services rendered by a provider and the settlement made under the patient's coverage in respect of that <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>. The  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</Link> resource may also be used as a resource for data exchange for bulk data analysis, as the resource  encompasses <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverage">Coverage</Link>/Eligibility information. </p> <p> This is the logical combination of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> and some <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverage">Coverage</Link> accounting information  in respect of a single payor prepared for consumption by the subscriber and/or patient. It is not   simply a series of pointers to referred-to content models, is a physical subset scoped to the   adjudication by a single payor which details the services rendered, the amounts to be settled and   to whom, and optionally the coverage allowed under the policy and the amounts used to date. </p> <p> Typically the EOB is only used to convey <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> (use=claim) and the associated <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> information to patients or subscribers. It may also be   used to convey consolidated predetermination and preauthorization request and response information to patients or subscribers. An EOB will never   be created for patient or subscriber information exchange if an error was detected in the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>.  </p> <p> It is also recognized that "EOB" is a term that carries additional meaning in certain areas of the industry. When the resource was originally  being developed there was substantial discussion about the adoption of an alternative name for the resource but after much discussion it was  resolved that the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</Link> name has the advantage of familiarity that has been proven through the early adoption of the resource  for multiple purposes.  </p> <p><b>Note:</b> when creating profiles for EOB as a patient focused information exchange the payment details, other than date, should be excluded if  the payee is the provider as that would leak business confidential information.</p> <p><b>Note:</b> the EOB <b>SHALL NOT</b> be used as a replacement for a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> when responding to <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claims</Link>. Only the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> contains  the appropriate adjudication information for a payor response to a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>.</p> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</Link> resource is an "event" resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">Workflow Event.</a></p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Additional Information <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/explanationofbenefit.html#13.10.1.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> Additional information regarding electronic claims content and usage may be found at: </p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#resource-status">Financial Resource Status Lifecycle</a>: how .status is used in the financial resources.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#secondary-use">Secondary Use of Resources</a>: how resources such as <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</Link> may used for  reporting and data exchange for analytics, not just for eClaims exchange between providers and payors.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#subrogation">Subrogation</a>: how eClaims may handle patient insurance coverages when another insurer rather than  the provider will settle the claim and potentially recover costs against specified coverages.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#cob">Coordination of Benefit</a>: how eClaims may handle multiple patient insurance coverages.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#real-time">RealTime Exchange and Obtaining EOBs</a>: EOBs may be obtained using Polling or FHIR REST (SEARCH).</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#attachments">Attachments and Supporting Information</a>: how eClaims may handle the provision of supporting  information, whether provided by content or reference, within the eClaim resource when submitted to the payor or later in a resource which refers  to the subject eClaim resource. This also includes how payors may request additional supporting information from providers.</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</Link> resource is for reporting out to patients or transferring data to patient centered applications, such as patient health Record (PHR) application, the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</a>  should be used instead of the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</a> and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</a> resources as those resources may contain provider and payer specific information which is not appropriate for sharing with the patient.</p> <p>When using the resources for reporting and transferring claims data, which may have originated in some standard other than FHIR, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> resource is useful if only the request side of the information exchange is of interest. If, however, both the request and the adjudication information is to be reported then the  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</a> should be used instead. </p> <p>The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</a> resource is used to request the adjudication and/or authorization of a set of healthcare-related goods and services for a patient against the patient's insurance coverages, or to request what the adjudication would be for a supplied set of goods or services should they be actually supplied to the patient. </p> <p>When requesting whether the patient's coverage is inforce, whether it is valid at this or a specified date, or requesting the benefit details or preauthorization requirements  associated with a coverage <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityrequest">CoverageEligibilityRequest</a> should be used instead. </p> <b>The eClaim domain includes a number of related resources</b> <table border="1" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="2" frame="box"> <tbody><tr> <td>ExplanationOfBenefit</td> <td>This resource combines the information from the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> and the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link>, stripping out any provider or payor proprietary information, into a unified information model  suitable for use for: patient reporting; transferring information to a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> Health Record system; and, supporting complete claim and adjudication information exchange with regulatory and analytics organizations and other parts of the provider's organization. </td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</a></td> <td>A suite of goods and services and insurances coverages under which adjudication or authorization is requested.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</a></td> <td>A payor's adjudication and/or authorization response to the suite of services provided in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>. Typically the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> references the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> but does not duplicate the clinical or financial information provided in the claim.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/coverageeligibilityrequest">CoverageEligibilityRequest</a></td> <td>A request to a payor to: ascertain whether a coverage is in-force at the current or at a specified time; list the table of benefits; determine whether coverage is provided for specified categories or specific services; and whether preauthorization is required, and if so what supporting information would be required.</td> </tr> </tbody></table> </div>
  </TabItem>

# Flag

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag.mdx

title: Flag
sidebar_position: 54

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/flag.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# Flag

Prospective warnings of potential issues when providing care to the patient.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> A flag is a warning or notification of some sort presented to the user - who may be a clinician or some other person involve in patient care. It usually represents something of sufficient significance to warrant a special display of some sort - rather than just a note in the resource. A flag has a subject representing the resource that will trigger its display. This subject can be of different types, as described in the examples below: </p> <ul>     <li>A note that a patient has an overdue account, which the provider may wish to discuss with them - in case of hardship for example (subject = <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link>) </li>     <li>An outbreak of Ebola in a particular region (subject=Location) so that all patients from that region have a higher risk of having that condition</li>     <li>A particular provider is unavailable for referrals over a given period (subject = <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link>)</li>     <li>A patient who is enrolled in a clinical trial (subject=Group)</li>     <li>Special guidance or caveats to be aware of when following a protocol (subject=PlanDefinition)</li>     <li>Warnings about using a drug in a formulary requires special approval (subject=Medication)</li>     <li>etc.</li> </ul> <p>      A flag is typically presented as a label in a prominent location in the record to notify the clinician of the potential issues,  though it may also appear in other contexts; e.g. notes applicable to a radiology technician, or to a clinician performing a home visit.  For patients, the information in the flag will often be derived from the record, and therefore, for a thorough and careful clinician, who has the time to review the notes will be redundant.   However, given the volume of information frequently found in patients' records and the potentially serious consequences of losing sight of some facts, this  redundancy is deemed appropriate.  As well, some flags may reflect information not captured by any other resource in the record.   (E.g. "Patient has large dog at home") </p> <p> In line with its purpose, a flag is concise, highlighting a small set of high-priority issues among the much larger set of  data in the chart. Readers who want more detail should consult the chart or other source of information.  Caution should be exercised in creating <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flag</Link> instances. If entries are created for information that could be gleaned in a sufficiently timely fashion by reviewing the patient record,  the flag list will itself become overwhelming and will cease to serve its intended purpose. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flags</Link> are expected to persist in a record for some period of time and are, at most, targeted to particular types of practitioners or to practitioners in particular system.   </p>      <p>Examples of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> related issues that might appear in flags:</p> <ul> <li>Risks to the patient (functional risk of falls, spousal restraining order, latex allergy)</li> <li>Patient's needs for special accommodations (hard of hearing, need for easy-open caps)</li> <li>Risks to providers (dog in house, patient may bite, infection control precautions)</li> <li>Administrative concerns (incomplete information, pre-payment required due to credit risk)</li> </ul>  <p>     Examples of issues that should not appear <b>only</b> in flags: </p> <ul> <li>Potential allergy or drug interaction to planned therapy (use <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/detectedissue">DetectedIssue</a>)</li> <li>Known adverse reaction to a substance (use <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</a>)</li> </ul>     <p> Note that we include "latex allergy" in the "in scope" list, and "allergy" in the "not in scope" list. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flag</Link> resource is not  designed to replace the normal order checking process, and one should not expect to see all allergies in <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flags</Link>. However, if there  is an activity that might occur prior to careful evaluation of the record (e.g. donning of latex gloves) and that activity might  pose a risk to the patient, that is the sort of eventuality the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flag</Link> is intended to support. </p> <p> Specific guidelines about what type of information is appropriate to expose using <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flag</Link>, as well as what categories of individuals  should see particular flags, will vary by interoperability community. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flags</Link> may highlight a highly condensed view of information found in the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</a>,  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a> and possibly  other resources.  A <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/extension-flag-detail.html">common extension</a> allows the linkage of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flag</Link> to the supporting detail resource. The purpose of these other resources is to provide detailed clinical information.  The purpose of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flag</Link> is to alert practitioners to  information that is important to influence their interaction with a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> prior to detailed review of the record. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flags</Link> are not used to convey information to a specific individual or organization (e.g. an abnormal lab result reported to the ordering  clinician, reporting of an adverse reaction to a regulatory authority).  These are handled using the  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communicationrequest">CommunicationRequest</a> and the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communication">Communication</a> resources. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/flag">Flags</Link> are not raised as a result of a reported or proposed action (e.g. drug-drug interactions, duplicate therapy warnings).   These would be handled using <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/detectedissue">DetectedIssue</a>. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

</Tabs>

# Goal

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/goal.mdx

title: Goal

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';

# Goal

Describes the intended objective(s) for a patient, group or organization care, for example, weight loss, restoring an activity of daily living, obtaining herd immunity via immunization, meeting a process improvement objective, etc. Refer to the [US Core Goal profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-goal.html).

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p>    A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/goal">Goal</Link> in health care services delivery is generally an expressed desired health state to be achieved by a subject of care (or family/group) over a period or at a specific point of time.  This desired target health state may be achieved as a result of health care intervention(s) or resulting from natural recovery over time.  For example: </p> <ul> <li> A goal of a plan for a condition such as a diabetes might specify desired outcome(s) (e.g. HgbA1c level =&lt;5.6% in 3 months) as a result of interventions such as medication therapy, nutritional management and/or increase physical activity. </li> <li> A goal of a procedure might be to meet the intended objective of the procedure (e.g. wet-dry-dressing changes twice a day; goal: wound healed completely in 2 weeks) or to prevent an unintended complication (e.g. repositioning a patient every two hours: goal to maintain skin integrity) </li> </ul> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/goal">Goals</Link> may address the prevention of illness, cure or mitigation of a condition, prolongation of life, or mitigation of pain and discomfort. </p> <p> When dealing with groups, goals may also reflect health state, such as a reduction of addiction behaviors.  However, they may also reflect population health objectives such as education, screening, etc. </p> <p> Organizational goals are typically not health state specific but may instead identify measurement targets such as infection control, cost management, patient satisfaction, etc. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/goal">Goals</Link> are typically established in the context of a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</a>.  However, goals may also be directly     referenced by request-type resources (e.g. <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationrequest">MedicationRequest</a> or <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</a>) by using an extension. </p> <p> A goal represents a specific goal instance for a particular patient, group, etc.  It is not intended to be used to define types of potential goals as part of an order set or protocol definition.  Protocol definitions and order sets are supported through <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</a>.  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/goal">Goal</Link> resource is intended to be used once an order set is instantiated or assigned to a patient, which is when the potential goals become the actual goals, if not changed or deleted. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/goal">Goals</Link> are often evaluated using <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observations</a>. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# GraphDefinition

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/graphdefinition.mdx

title: GraphDefinition
sidebar_position: 56

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';

# GraphDefinition

A formal computable definition of a graph of resources - that is, a coherent set of resources that form a graph by following references. The Graph Definition resource defines a set and makes rules about the set.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/graphdefinition">GraphDefinition</Link> resource provides a formal computable definition of a graph of resources - that is, a coherent set of resources that form  a graph by following references. The Graph Definition resource defines a set and makes rules about the set. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/graphdefinition">GraphDefinition</Link> resource can be used to: </p> <ul>  <li>Summarize a set of profiles on resources</li>  <li>Define a graph of resources to return in a query</li>  <li>Define a graph of resources to include in a document</li>  <li>Document rules about the relationship between a set of resources e.g. must all resources concern the same patient?</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> There is a close relationship between <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/structuredefinition">Profiles</a> and  <code>GraphDefinitions</code>: </p> <ul>  <li>A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/structuredefinition">StructureDefinition</Link> defines a profile, and profiles can make rules about the relationships between resources. A carefully defined set of profiles implies part of what is in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/graphdefinition">GraphDefinition</Link></li>  <li>A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/graphdefinition">GraphDefinition</Link> defines rules about the relationships between resources, and in so doing, implies some constraints that would need to be represented in their profiles</li> </ul> <p> Profiles and Graph Definitions can be used together, or separately. When used together, they should be consistent. Note, though, that a graph definition may contain a subset or a superset of the relationships explicitly described in the profiles it refers to. </p> <p> It is possible that in some circumstances, a graph definition makes incompatible rules with  the Profiles it refers to - in this case, no graph if resources will meet the constraints expressed.  Applications should - but are not required - detect when such incompatibilities arise. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/messagedefinition">MessageDefinition</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# Group

Represents a defined collection of entities that may be discussed or acted upon collectively but which are not expected to act collectively, and are not formally or legally recognized; i.e. a collection of entities that isn't an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link>.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <a name="use"></a> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Use Cases <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</Link> resource is used in one of two ways:</p> <ol>   <li>To define a group of specific people, animals, devices, etc. that is being tracked, examined or otherwise referenced as part of healthcare-related activities</li>   <li>To define a set of <i>possible</i> people, animals, devices, etc. that are of interest for some intended future healthcare-related activities</li> </ol> <p>Examples of the former could include group therapy or treatment sessions, exposed entities tracked as part of public health, etc.  The latter might be used to define expected subjects for a clinical study.</p> <p>Both use cases are handled by a single resource because the data elements captured tend to be similar.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> There are a number of mechanisms in FHIR for communicating collections of resources: </p> <ul> <li> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</a> resource - enumerates a flat collection of resources and provides features for managing the collection.   While a particular <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> instance may represent a "snapshot", from a business process perspective the notion of "List"  is dynamic – items are added and removed over time.  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> resource references other resources.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">Lists</Link> may be  curated and have specific business meaning. </li> <li> This <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</Link> resource - defines a group of specific people, animals, devices etc. by enumerating them,  or by describing qualities that group members have. The group resource refers to other resources, possibly implicitly.   <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Groups</Link> are intended to be acted upon or observed as a whole; e.g. performing therapy on a group, calculating risk for a group,  etc.  This resource will commonly be used for public health (e.g. describing an at-risk population), clinical trials (e.g.  defining a test subject pool) and similar purposes. </li> <li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careteam">CareTeam</a>. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</Link> is distinct from <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careteam">CareTeam</Link>. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</Link> is patient-independent and identifies an  undifferentiated set of individuals who are intended to be the target of one or more clinical activities (e.g. set of  clinical trial participants, set of individuals impacted by or at risk of a public health event, a herd or flock, etc.)  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careteam">CareTeam</Link> resource establishes a set of relationships and roles and is specific to a particular <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link>.  The actors are the individual members or organized group of individuals. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careteam">CareTeam</Link> can be referenced by <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/episodeofcare">EpisodeOfCare</Link>,  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/encounter">Encounter</Link>, or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</Link> to identify the set of individuals (and their respective roles) who are intended to be involved  in providing the care defined by those resources. </li> <li> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</a> resource - is an infrastructure container for a group of resources.  It does not have narrative  and is used to group collections of resources for transmission, persistence or processing (e.g. messages, documents, transactions,  query responses, etc.)  The content of bundles is typically algorithmically determined for a particular exchange or persistence purpose. </li> <li> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</a> resource - defines a set of healthcare-related information that is assembled  together into a single logical document that provides a single coherent statement of meaning, establishes its own context and  that has clinical attestation with regard to who is making the statement. The composition resource provides the basic structure  of a FHIR <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/documents.html">document</a>.  The full content of the document is expressed using a bundle.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Compositions</Link> will  often reference <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">Lists</Link> as the focus of particular sections. </li> <li> The <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/domainresource.html">DomainResource</a>.<code>contained</code> element - allows multiple resources to be nested inside any DomainResource.  This is a special type of grouping where the grouped resources lose independent existence - they no longer have their own identifiers, can't easily be queried independently, etc.  Use of this grouping is a technical  mechanism for managing the independence of resources and has no impact on meaning.   </li> </ul> Contained, bundled and remotely referenced resources convey the same meaning. </div>
  </TabItem>

# GuidanceResponse

# GuidanceResponse

A guidance response is the formal response to a guidance request, including any output parameters returned by the evaluation, as well as the description of any proposed actions to be taken.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/guidanceresponse">GuidanceResponse</Link> resource is used to represent the result of invoking a decision support service. It provides a container for the status of the response, any warnings or messages returned by the service, as well as any output data from the service and any suggested actions to be performed.</p> <p>Use cases for the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/guidanceresponse">GuidanceResponse</Link> resource include:</p> <ul> <li>Keeping a record of past service requests, including the ability to reference the context of the request such as the disease state</li> <li>Representing additional data requirements for subsequent service requests</li> <li>Representing Public Health case reporting and recording</li> <li>Sharing the results of decision support guidance and determination of reportability with clinicians and public health agencies</li> </ul> <p>In addition, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/guidanceresponse">GuidanceResponse</Link> resource is aligned with the CDS Hooks response structure and so provides a mechanism to record the results of CDS Hooks interactions. For a detailed discussion of how the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/guidanceresponse">GuidanceResponse</Link> resource can be used for this purpose, refer to the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/clinicalreasoning-cds-on-fhir.html#evaluation">Evaluation</a> topic in the Clinical Reasoning module.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# ImagingStudy

# ImagingStudy

Representation of the content produced in a DICOM imaging study. A study comprises a set of series, each of which includes a set of Service-Object Pair Instances (SOP Instances - images or other data) acquired or produced in a common context. A series is of only one modality (e.g. X-ray, CT, MR, ultrasound), but a study may have multiple series of different modalities.

<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/imagingstudy">ImagingStudy</Link> provides information on a DICOM imaging study, and the series and imaging objects in  that study. It also provides information on how to retrieve that information (in a native DICOM  format, or in a rendered format, such as JPEG). <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/imagingstudy">ImagingStudy</Link> is used to make available information  about all parts of a single DICOM study. </p> <p> This resource provides mappings of its elements to DICOM attributes.  DICOM attributes are identified  by a 32-bit tag, presented in canonical form as two four-digit hexadecimal values within parentheses  and separated by a comma, e.g. (0008,103E).  The name and value representation (data type) of  each attribute can be found  in <a href="http://medical.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/html/part06.html">DICOM Part 6 Data Dictionary </a>.   The use of the attributes in the context of information objects, including detailed description of use, can be found  in <a href="http://medical.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/html/part03.html">DICOM Part 3 Information Object Definitions  </a>.   Attributes used in the DICOM query information models, such as "Number of Instances in Study", can be found  in <a href="http://medical.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/html/part04.html#chapter_C">DICOM Part 4 Annex C </a>. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/imagingstudy">ImagingStudy</Link> provides access to significant DICOM information but will only eliminate the need for DICOM  query (e.g., QIDO-RS) in the simplest cases. The DICOM instances are not stored in the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/imagingstudy">ImagingStudy</Link>  resource; use of a DICOM WADO-RS server or other storage mechanism is needed. </p> <p>  An <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/imagingstudy">ImagingStudy</Link> SHALL reference one DICOM Study, and MAY reference a subset of that Study. More than one <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/imagingstudy">ImagingStudy</Link> MAY reference the same DICOM Study or different subsets of the same DICOM Study. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

Use <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/media">Media</a> to  track non-DICOM images, video, or audio.  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/binary">Binary</a> can be used to store arbitrary content.  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/documentreference">DocumentReference</a> allow indexing and retrieval of clinical “documents” with relevant metadata. </p> </div>

# Immunization

Describes the event of a patient being administered a vaccine or a record of an immunization as reported by a patient, a clinician or another party. Refer to the [US Core Immunizations profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-immunization.html).

<div> <a name="dstu"></a> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunization">Immunization</Link> resource is intended to cover the recording of current and historical administration of vaccines to patients across all healthcare disciplines in all care settings and all regions. This includes immunization of both humans and animals but does not include the administration of non-vaccine agents, even those that may have or claim to have immunological effects.  While the terms "immunization" and "vaccination" are not clinically identical, for the purposes of the FHIR resources, the terms are used synonymously. </p> <p> Additionally, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunization">Immunization</Link> resource is expected to cover key concepts related to the creation, revision and querying of a patient's immunization history. This resource - through consultation with the Public Health work group - is believed to meet key use cases and information requirements as defined in the existing <a href="http://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=185">HL7 v2 </a> immunization implementation guide, <a href="https://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=186">HL7 v3 </a> POIZ domain and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunization">Immunization</Link> Domain Analysis Model. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> Administration of vaccines is intended to be handled using the <b>Immunization</b> resource.  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationadministration">MedicationAdministration</a> is intended for tracking the administration of non-vaccine medications.  Some systems treat immunizations in the same way as any other medication administration.  Such systems SHOULD use an immunization resource to represent these.  If systems need to use a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationadministration">MedicationAdministration</a> resource to capture vaccinations for workflow or other reasons, they SHOULD also expose an equivalent <b>Immunization</b> instance. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunization">Immunization</Link>.reaction may be an indication of an allergy or intolerance. If this is deemed to be the case, a separate <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</Link> resource instance should be created to indicate it, as most systems will not query against past <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunization">Immunization</Link>.reaction. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# ImmunizationEvaluation

# ImmunizationEvaluation

Describes a comparison of an immunization event against published recommendations to determine if the administration is "valid" in relation to those recommendations.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunizationevaluation">ImmunizationEvaluation</Link> resource is intended to cover communicating the results of an evaluation of a vaccine administration event (documented using the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunization">Immunization</Link> resource) against a set of published recommendations (protocols). Evaluating administered doses in a patient's immunization history is central to ensuring that the patient if fully protected against vaccine-preventable diseases. It is also a necessary prerequisite to generating a customized set of immunization recommendations for the patient. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunizationevaluation">ImmunizationEvaluation</Link> resource communicates the results of an evaluation of an instance of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunization">Immunization</Link> resource relative to a set of published recommendations. It is intended to communicate if the vaccine administration event was "valid" or "not valid" relative to the recommendations. Once all vaccine administration events in a patient's record have been evaluated, it is then possible to generate a set of vaccination related recommendations, unique for the patient. These recommendations are communicated using the ImmunizationRecommedation resource. </p> <p> As the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunizationevaluation">ImmunizationEvaluation</Link> resource is focused on the evaluation of a single vaccine administration event, it does not include data regarding the overall patient status relative to the recommendations used in the evaluation. For example, a total of 3 doses of hepatitis B vaccine may be required for patient protection, but an instance of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunizationevaluation">ImmunizationEvaluation</Link> resource will be concerned with only one of the doses (although other instances of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunizationevaluation">ImmunizationEvaluation</Link> should exist for the other doses). The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunizationrecommendation">ImmunizationRecommendation</Link> resource is used to convey the overall patient status (eg. a dose is due or the patient is complete) relative to the hepatitis B series. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <p> Through FHIR Release 3, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunization">Immunization</Link> resource contained a  "protocol" backbone element which functioned as an evaluation of the vaccine administration event. Beginning in Release 4, this new resource replaces the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunization">Immunization</Link>.protocol element. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunizationrecommendation">ImmunizationRecommendation</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# ImplementationGuide

A set of rules of how a particular interoperability or standards problem is solved - typically through the use of FHIR resources. This resource is used to gather all the parts of an implementation guide into a logical whole and to publish a computable definition of all the parts.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> An implementation guide (IG) is a set of rules about how FHIR resources are used (or should be used) to solve a particular problem, with associated documentation to support and clarify the usage. Classically, FHIR implementation guides are published on the web after they are generated using the  <a href="https://confluence.hl7.org/display/FHIR/IG+Publisher+Documentation">FHIR Implementation Guide Publisher </a>. </p> <p> The <code>ImplementationGuide</code> resource is a single resource that defines the logical content of the IG, along with the important entry pages into the publication, so that the  logical package that the IG represents, so that the contents are computable.  </p> <p> In particular, validators are able to use the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/implementationguide">ImplementationGuide</Link> resource to validate content against the implementation guide as a whole. The significant conformance expectation introduced  by the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/implementationguide">ImplementationGuide</Link> resource is the idea of <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/#default">Default Profiles</a>.  Implementations may conform to multiple implementation guides at once, but this requires that  the implementation guides are compatible (see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/#compatibility">below</a>). </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> Implementation Guides contain two different types of resource references: </p> <ul>  <li>Contents: A set of logical statements which implementations must conform to. These are almost always <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/conformance-module.html">conformance resources</a></li>  <li>Examples: Examples that illustrate the intent of the profiles defined in the implementation guide. These can be any kind of resource</li> </ul> <p> An application's <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/capabilitystatement">Capability Statement</a> may identify one or more implementation guides that an application conforms to. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/elementdefinition">ElementDefinition</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/capabilitystatement">CapabilityStatement</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# Invoice

# Invoice

Invoice containing collected <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitem">ChargeItems</Link> from an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/account">Account</Link> with calculated individual and total price for Billing purpose.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> Tracking Financial information is vital in <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> Administration and Finance systems in most Healthcare <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organizations</Link>. An invoice is a financial document issued by a healthcare provider to a patient or a payer indicating the goods and services (ChargeItems) performed with their quantities and prices.   </p>  <p>Example implementations:  </p><ul>  <li>Any solution that tracks billing information and needs to issue invoices</li> <li>Private Insurance Providers who want to deliver structured information to patients to increase cost transparency</li> <li>Patient apps that want to include information on the amount and reason of the charged costs for the healthcare services a patient received</li> </ul>  <p></p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p> The existing <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> resource is constricted to use cases where <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claims</Link> are sent to insurances for reimbursement, in a message-like style. It neither references <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitem">ChargeItems</Link> nor <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/account">Accounts</Link>. </p><p> Competing invoicing standards such as EDIFACT or X12 are aiming at inter-organizational exchange and do not offer human readable representations or traceable links to services rendered which is a requirement for invoicing towards patients. This resource is used where existing <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitem">ChargeItems</Link> in an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/account">Account</Link> are collected to create an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/invoice">Invoice</Link> to be sent out to Individuals or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organizations</Link> in a structured way. The invoice is the hospital's view, whereas the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> is the payer's view on the performed services.</p> <p> Since the individual <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitem">ChargeItem</Link> resources that make up the line items of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/invoice">Invoice</Link> do not carry any pricing information, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitemdefinition">ChargeItemDefinitions</Link> will have to be applied to the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitem">ChargeItems</Link> in order to calculate the price components for the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/invoice">Invoice</Link> depending on the context of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/chargeitem">ChargeItem</Link></p> </div>
  </TabItem>

</Tabs>

# Library

title: Library
sidebar_position: 67

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

# Library

The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/library">Library</Link> resource is a general-purpose container for knowledge asset definitions. It can be used to describe and expose existing knowledge assets such as logic libraries and information model descriptions, as well as to describe a collection of knowledge assets.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/library">Library</Link> resource is a general purpose container for clinical knowledge assets. These assets may be defined using a non-FHIR representation, such as a shareable library of clinical logic, written in Clinical Quality Language (CQL), or the XML Schema for an information model, or they may be defined using FHIR resources such as the description of a protocol represented by a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> resource. In addition to representing the metadata of the library, the resource has elements for tracking dependencies, as well as for representing the parameters and data requirements for any expression functionality provided by the library.</p> <p>For non-FHIR assets, the actual content of the library is represented using the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/attachment">Attachment</Link> data type, and may either be referenced with a URL, or the content may be embedded as a base-64 encoded string. Either way, the <code>contentType</code> element of the attachment is used to indicate the representation of the library content.</p> <p>Note that because the library content may be embedded as well as be retrievable from an external repository via the attachment URL, the possibility exists for the embedded content to be different from the content on the repository. With proper versioning and governance, this should never occur, but to minimize the potential impact of this possibility, implementers SHALL give precedence to the embedded content of a library when it is present.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/library">Library</Link> resource is definitional in nature, meaning it is intended to represent shareable knowledge independent of any particular patient. This is in contrast to the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/documentreference">DocumentReference</a> resource, which captures non-FHIR content related to a specific patient, and the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/media">Media</a> and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/binary">Binary</a> resources which capture multimedia content and raw binary content, respectively.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/activitydefinition">ActivityDefinition</a></li>

# Linkage

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/linkage.mdx

title: Linkage
sidebar_position: 68

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/linkage.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# Linkage

Identifies two or more records (resource instances) that refer to the same real-world "occurrence".

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> This resource allows the assertion of linkages between multiple resource instances (generally of the same type) that are referring to the same underlying business objects.  For example, multiple <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</Link> records that refer to the same underlying problem/issue for a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link>; multiple <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</Link> records that refer to the same reaction susceptibility; multiple <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> and/or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/relatedperson">RelatedPerson</Link> records that refer to the same human being or animal. </p> <p> FHIR supports a process for sharing electronic records.  It is common for multiple records to exist that deal with the same real-world phenomenon.  This can result from information being captured by different systems, information being captured within a single system by different users (either deliberately to represent distinct perspectives or accidentally when a new record is created rather than updating an existing record).  These multiple records may be referred to as "duplicate" records, but in practice they aren't often actually "duplicate" in that the data represented (and the history of the records) will be at least somewhat distinct. </p> <p> In some cases, the solution after identifying duplicates is to deprecate one of the records (e.g. by changing the status to "Entered in Error") and to move all relevant information to the surviving record.  In other cases, the resource may support the ability to establish a linkage directly between the resources.  However, in some cases, both records may need to survive or there might be a desire to have both resources continue to be maintained, perhaps because the resources live on different servers or have different 'owners'.  The <b>Linkage</b> resource is intended to satisfy this use-case. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/person">Person</a> resource should be used to link a person independent of a specific health-related context. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/linkage">Linkage</Link> can be used for all other use cases. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

</Tabs>

# List

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/list.mdx

title: List
sidebar_position: 69

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/list.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# List

A list is a curated collection of resources.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> resource is a flat, possibly ordered collection of records. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> resources are used in many places,  including allergies, medications, alerts, family history, medical history, etc. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> resources can be used to  support patient-specific clinical lists as well as lists that manage workflows such as tracking patients, managing  teaching cases, etc. Resources supported by the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> resource can be homogeneous – consisting of only one type of  resource (e.g. allergy lists) as well as heterogeneous – containing a variety of resources (e.g. a problem list  including <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Conditions</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerances</a>,  recent <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedures</a>, etc.). </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">Lists</Link> will typically include references to the resources that make up the list, however in some cases the details  of the content of the list might be expressed in narrative only; e.g. a text record of a family history.  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link>  resource is only needed if there is a need to filter the set of resources by a mechanism that cannot be accomplished  via a simple query; e.g. there is no need to have a list for all <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerances</a> that exist on a server for a given patient.  However, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> is an appropriate mechanism to provide a filtered list of the  subset of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerances</Link> that are deemed to be "current". <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">Lists</Link> are allowed to contain other <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">Lists</Link>, to create a nested collection of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">Lists</Link>. </p> <p> Querying a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> of resources such as <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</Link> or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medication">Medication</Link>-related resources is different than querying the resource-specific endpoint. For example, a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</Link> resources would represent a curated point-in-time snapshot of the patient's allergies and intolerances. On the other hand, querying the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</Link> endpoint would typically produce a larger set of records as it would both be non-curated (potentially containing duplicate or out-of-date records) and current - generated based on information as of "now" rather than the last time a human manually revised the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> resource instance. Which mechanism is most appropriate for data retrieval will vary by use-case. In some cases, systems might not have an appropriate curated <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> to query. </p> <p> Note that the presence of an item in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> resource SHALL NOT change the meaning of any information that would be  understood by looking at the item outside the context of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link>, because items may be accessed directly outside  the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> by RESTful means or after a document is processed. For example, a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> with a code that means  "refuted conditions" cannot have items that are <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</a> resources that do not have a  <code>verificationStatus</code> of <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/valueset-condition-clinical.html#refuted">refuted</a>. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> There are five mechanisms in FHIR for communicating collections of resources: </p> <ul> <li> This <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> resource - enumerates a flat collection of resources and provides features for managing the collection.   While a particular <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> instance may represent a "snapshot", from a business process perspective the notion of "List"  is dynamic – items are added and removed over time.  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> resource references other resources.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">Lists</Link> may be  curated and have specific business meaning. </li> <li> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</a> resource - defines a group of specific people, animals, devices, etc. by enumerating them,  or by describing qualities that group members have. The group resource refers to other resources, possibly implicitly.   <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Groups</Link> are intended to be acted upon or observed as a whole; e.g. performing therapy on a group, calculating risk for a group,  etc.  This resource will commonly be used for public health (e.g. describing an at-risk population), clinical trials (e.g. defining a test subject pool) and similar purposes. </li> <li> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</a> resource - defines a set of healthcare-related information that is assembled  together into a single logical document that provides a single coherent statement of meaning, establishes its own context and  that has clinical attestation with regard to who is making the statement. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Composition</Link> resource provides the basic structure  of a FHIR <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/documents.html">document</a>.  The full content of the document is expressed using a bundle.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/composition">Compositions</Link> will  often reference <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">Lists</Link> as the focus of particular sections. </li> <li> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</a> resource - is an infrastructure container for a group of resources.  It does not have a narrative  and is used to group collections of resources for transmission, persistence or processing (e.g. messages, documents, transactions,  query responses, etc.)  The content of bundles is typically algorithmically determined for a particular exchange or persistence purpose. </li> <li> The <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/domainresource.html">DomainResource</a>.<code>contained</code> element - allows multiple resources to be nested inside any DomainResource.  This is a special type of grouping where the grouped resources lose independent existence - they no longer have their own identifiers, can't easily be queried independently, etc.  Use of this grouping is a technical  mechanism for managing the independence of resources and has no impact on meaning. Contained, bundled, and remotely referenced resources convey the same meaning. </li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measurereport">MeasureReport</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# Location

Details and position information for a physical place where services are provided and resources and participants may be stored, found, contained, or accommodated.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/location">Location</Link> includes both incidental locations (a place which is used for healthcare without prior designation or authorization) and  dedicated, formally appointed locations. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/location">Locations</Link> may be private, public, mobile or fixed and scale from small  freezers to full hospital buildings or parking garages. </p> <p>Examples of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/location">Locations</Link> are:</p> <ul> <li>Building, ward, corridor, room or bed</li> <li>Mobile Clinic</li> <li>Freezer, incubator</li> <li>Vehicle or lift</li> <li>Home, shed, or a garage</li> <li>Road, parking place, a park</li> <li>Ambulance (generic)</li> <li>Ambulance (specific)</li> <li>Patient's Home (generic)</li> <li>Jurisdiction</li> </ul>   <p>     These locations are not intended to cover locations on a patient where something occurred     (i.e. a patient's broken leg), but can happily cover the location where the patient broke the leg (the playground)   </p> </div>

This jurisdiction may be considered a classified boundary which could be a combination of a physical boundary, and some other discriminator(s): </p> <ul> <li>Nation - Country-wide community or Federal Government (Ministry of Health)</li> <li>Province or State (community or Government)</li> <li>Business (throughout an enterprise)</li> <li>Business scope (CDC/FDA)</li> <li>Business segment (UK Pharmacy)</li> </ul> </div>
