# Measure

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure.mdx

title: Measure
sidebar_position: 71

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/measure.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# Measure

The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure">Measure</Link> resource provides the definition of a quality measure.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure">Measure</Link> resource represents a structured, computable definition of a health-related measure such as a clinical quality measure, public health indicator, or population analytics measure. A quality measure is a quantitative tool to assess the performance of an individual or organization with respect to a specified process or outcome via the measurement of actions, processes, or outcomes of clinical care. Quality measures are often derived from clinical guidelines and are designed to determine whether the appropriate care has been provided given a set of clinical criteria and an evidence base.</p> <p>Note that the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure">Measure</Link> itself does not typically contain any logic; rather a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/library">Library</a> resource is referenced that contains the logic required by the measure, and the various expression elements, such as population criteria, reference named expressions within that library (or libraries). In addition, if the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure">Measure</Link> references multiple libraries, then any expression references within the resource must be qualified with the name of the library that contains the referenced expression.</p> <p>For a detailed discussion of how to use the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure">Measure</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measurereport">MeasureReport</Link> resources, refer to the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/clinicalreasoning-quality-reporting.html">Quality Reporting</a> topic.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure">Measure</Link> resource describes a specific quality measure, or population analytic, providing the structure of the measure in terms of the calculation elements (the <i>populations</i> involved). The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</a> resource is also capable of describing a population, however, the complexity involved in specifying the criteria in the general case requires the use of a high-level query language such as Clinical Quality Language (CQL). As such, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure">Measure</Link> resource defines only the top-level populations and references expressions for the actual criteria. These expressions are typically provided using a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/library">Library</a> resource containing CQL or ELM expressions. In addition, the individual members of a population may be cases such as encounters or procedures and in these cases, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</Link> resource would be unable to represent the population characteristics accurately.</p> <p>A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure">Measure</Link> is also similar to an <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a> resource, with the exception that the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure">Measure</Link> is purely definitional, it contains no actual measurements, only a description of how to calculate a particular measurement or set of measurements.</p> <p>A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure">Measure</Link> is also similar to a clinical document, but as with the relationship to <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link>, a Document is specific to a particular subject.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communication">Communication</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/familymemberhistory">FamilyMemberHistory</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measurereport">MeasureReport</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# MeasureReport

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/measurereport.mdx

title: MeasureReport
sidebar_position: 72

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

# MeasureReport

The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measurereport">MeasureReport</Link> resource contains the results of the calculation of a measure; and optionally a reference to the resources involved in that calculation.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measurereport">MeasureReport</Link> resource represents the results of calculating a measure for a specific subject or group of subjects. The <code>$evaluate-measure</code> operation of the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure">Measure</a> resource is defined to return a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measurereport">MeasureReport</Link>. The resource is capable of representing three different levels of report: individual, subject-list, and summary. </p> <p> The resource draws requirements from the HL7 CDA R2 Implementation Guide: Quality Reporting Document Architecture - Category 1 (QRDA I) DSTU Release 3 (US Realm) and the HL7 Implementation Guide for CDA Release 2: Quality Reporting Document Architecture - Category III (QRDA III), DSTU Release 1 implementation guides. </p> <p>For a detailed discussion of how to use the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measure">Measure</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measurereport">MeasureReport</Link> resources, refer to the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/clinicalreasoning-quality-reporting.html">Quality Reporting</a> topic.</p> <p>Note that this resource is a special case of the more general notion of a query evaluation result. However, because the general case requires the ability to represent arbitrary content, this resource uses a simple indicator structure to describe population sizes for each population type defined in the measure. The intent is to be able to represent the more general case as well, either by generalizing this resource, or by making this structure a profile of a more general resource, and we are actively seeking comments about what approaches might be taken to achieve that aim.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p>Although the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/measurereport">MeasureReport</Link> is conceptually an <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a>, there is enough specific information required to support the quality reporting use case to warrant a separate resource.</p> <p>The resource is differentiated from a general purpose query result because it communicates specific information related to quality measurement evaluation that would be difficult to convey generally without imposing some other structure on top of the general results.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>

</Tabs>

<div> <a name="scope"></a> <a name="dstu"></a> <blockquote class="stu-note"><p><b>Trial-Use Note:</b> The Orders and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observations</Link> workgroups wants to make the balloter aware than observations that require the attachment data types are represented by the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/media">Media</Link> resource instead of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link>.  There have been several significant changes to  the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/media">Media</Link> resource in order to align it with <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a> and the workflow <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/event.html">event</a> pattern including:</p> <ol> <li>The addition of the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/media-definitions.html#Media.partOf">partOf</a> and <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/media-definitions.html#issued">issued</a> elements.</li> <li>The required <code>type</code> was changed an optional <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/media-definitions.html#category">category</a> and the <code>subtype</code> element was renamed to  <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/media-definitions.html#modality">modality</a>.</li> <li>Additional reference targets added to the <code>subject</code>,<code>operator</code>, and <code>basedOn</code> elements</li> <li>The additions of several standard <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/media-profiles.html#extensions">event extensions</a>.</li> </ol> </blockquote> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/media">Media</Link> resource contains photos, videos, and audio recordings. It is used with media acquired or used as part of the healthcare process. Here are some typical usages: </p> <ul>  <li>Photos and videos of diagnostic or care provision procedures for recording purposes </li>  <li>Images contained in diagnostic reports</li>  </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> This resource captures a specific type of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> - an <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a> whose value is audio, video or image data.   This resource is the preferred representation of such forms of information as it exposes the metadata relevant for  interpreting the information.  However, in some legacy environments, media information may occasionally appear in  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> instead.  Systems should be aware of this possibility. </p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/media">Media</Link> resource is able to contain medical images in a DICOM format. These images may also be made accessible  through an <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/imagingstudy">ImagingStudy</a> resource, which provides a direct reference to the image to a <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/ftp://medical.nema.org/medical/dicom/final/sup161_ft.pdf">WADO-RS server</a>. </p> <p> For such images, the WADO-RS framework is a preferred method for representing the images - the WADO-RS service may include rendering the image with annotations and display parameters from an associated DICOM  presentation state, for instance.  </p> <p> On the other hand, the media resource allows for a robust transfer of an image across boundaries where the WADO-RS service is not available. For this reason, medical images can also be represented in  a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/media">Media</Link> resource, but the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/media">Media</Link>.content.url should provide a reference to a source WADO-RS service  for the image. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# Medication

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/medication.mdx

title: Medication

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';

# Medication

This resource is primarily used for the identification and definition of a medication for the purposes of prescribing, dispensing, and administering a medication as well as for making statements about medication use. Refer to the [US Core Medication profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-medication.html).

At Medplum, we encourage using [`MedicationKnowledge`](/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationknowledge) rather than `Medication`. For more information, see [Modeling a Formulary](/docs/medications/formulary).

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> Representing medications in the majority of healthcare settings is a matter of identifying an item from a list and then conveying a reference  for the item selected either into a patient-related resource or to other applications.  Additional information about the medication is frequently  provided for human verification, but a full representation of the details of composition and efficacy of the medicine is conveyed by referring to drug dictionaries by means of the codes they define. There are some occasions where it is necessary to identify slightly more detail, such as when dispensing a package containing a particular medication requires identification both of the medicine and the package at once.   There are also some occasions (e.g. custom formulations) where the composition of a medicine must be represented.   In these cases, the ingredients of the medicine have to be specified together with the amount contained, though the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medication">Medication</Link> resource  does not provide full details. </p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medication">Medication</Link> resource allows for medications to be characterized by the form of the drug and the ingredient (or ingredients), as well as how it is packaged. The medication will include the ingredient(s) and their strength(s) and the package can include the amount (for example, number of tablets, volume, etc.) that is contained in a particular container (for example, 100 capsules of Amoxicillin 500mg per bottle). </p>     <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medication">Medication</Link> resource can be used to describe a compounded (aka extemporaneous or magistral) product that is manufactured by the pharmacy at the time of dispensing.  In this case there will be multiple ingredients which are typically base chemicals (for example, hydrocortisone powder) and there may be other ingredients that are manufactured products (for example, Glaxal Base).</p> <p> When a medication includes a package, further details about the composition can be provided. A package has a container (vacuum packed box, jar, etc.) and a list of the products or other packages that are in the package. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# MedicationAdministration

Describes the event of a patient consuming or otherwise being administered a medication. This may be as simple as swallowing a tablet or it may be a long running infusion. Related resources tie this event to the authorizing prescription, and the specific encounter between patient and health care practitioner.

Please refer to the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunization">Immunization</a> Resource/Profile for the treatment of vaccines. It will principally be used within care settings (including inpatient) to record the capture of medication administrations, including self-administrations of oral medications, injections, intra-venous adjustments, etc.  It can also be used in outpatient settings to record allergy shots and other non-immunization administrations.  In some cases, it might be used for home-health reporting, such as recording self-administered or even device-administered insulin.  </p>     <p>MedicationAdministration is an event resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event"> Workflow Event </a>     </p> </div>

# MedicationRequest

An order or request for both supply of the medication and the instructions for administration of the medication to a patient. The resource is called "MedicationRequest" rather than "MedicationPrescription" or "MedicationOrder" to generalize the use across inpatient and outpatient settings, including care plans, etc., and to harmonize with workflow patterns. Refer to the [US Core Medication Request profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-medicationrequest.html).

For Medplum best practices on using the `MedicationRequest` resource, please refer to [Representing Prescriptions and Medication Orders](/docs/medications/representing-prescriptions-and-medication-orders).

# MedicationStatement

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationstatement.mdx

title: MedicationStatement
sidebar_position: 79

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/medicationstatement.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# MedicationStatement

A record of a medication that is being consumed by a patient. A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationstatement">MedicationStatement</Link> may indicate that the patient may be taking the medication now or has taken the medication in the past or will be taking the medication in the future. The source of this information can be the patient, significant other (such as a family member or spouse), or a clinician. A common scenario where this information is captured is during the history taking process during a patient visit or stay. The medication information may come from sources such as the patient's memory, from a prescription bottle, or from a list of medications the patient, clinician or other party maintains. The primary difference between a medication statement and a medication administration is that the medication administration has complete administration information and is based on actual administration information from the person who administered the medication. A medication statement is often, if not always, less specific. There is no required date/time when the medication was administered, in fact we only know that a source has reported the patient is taking this medication, where details such as time, quantity, or rate or even medication product may be incomplete or missing or less precise. As stated earlier, the medication statement information may come from the patient's memory, from a prescription bottle or from a list of medications the patient, clinician or other party maintains. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medication">Medication</Link> administration is more formal and is not missing detailed information.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div>         <a name="scope"></a>                  <p> Common usage includes: </p>         <ul>             <li>the recording of non-prescription and/or recreational drugs</li>             <li>the recording of an intake medication list upon admission to hospital</li>             <li>the summarization of a patient's "active medications" in a patient profile</li>         </ul>         <p>A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationstatement">MedicationStatement</Link> may be used to record substance abuse or the use of other agents such as tobacco or alcohol.  This would typically be done if these substances are intended to be included in clinical decision support checking (for example, interaction checking) and as part of an active medication list.  If the intent is to populate social history and/or to include additional information (for example, desire to quit, amount per day, negative health effects), then it is better to record as an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> that could then be used to populate Social History.</p>         <p> This resource does not produce a medication list, but it does produce individual             medication statements that may be used in the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> resource to construct various types             of medication lists. Note that other medication lists can also be constructed from the             other Pharmacy resources (e.g., <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationrequest">MedicationRequest</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationadministration">MedicationAdministration</Link>). </p><p> A             medication statement is not a part of the prescribe -&gt; dispense -&gt; administer sequence,             but is a report by a patient, significant other or a clinician that one or more of the             prescribe, dispense or administer actions has occurred, resulting is a belief that the             patient is, has, or will be using a particular medication. </p>         <p>MedicationStatement is an event resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">Workflow Event</a></p>     </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div>         <a name="bnr"></a>                  <p>             </p><p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationstatement">MedicationStatement</Link> resource is used to record a medications or substances that the patient reports as being taken, not taking, have taken in the past or may take in the future.  It can also be used to record medication use that is derived from other records such as a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationrequest">MedicationRequest</Link>. The statement is not used to request or order a medication, supply or device. When requesting medication, supplies or devices when there is a patient focus or instructions regarding their use, a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationrequest">MedicationRequest</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/supplyrequest">SupplyRequest</a> or <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/devicerequest">DeviceRequest</a> should be used instead</p>         <p></p>         <p>             <b>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medication">Medication</Link> domain includes a number of related resources</b>         </p>         <table border="1" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="2" frame="box">             <tbody><tr>                 <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationrequest">MedicationRequest</a></td>                 <td>An order for both supply of the medication and the instructions for                     administration of the medicine to a patient.</td>             </tr>             <tr>                 <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationdispense">MedicationDispense</a></td>                 <td>Provision of a supply of a medication with the intention that it is subsequently                     consumed by a patient (usually in response to a prescription). </td>             </tr>             <tr>                 <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationadministration">MedicationAdministration</a></td>                 <td>When a patient actually consumes a medicine, or it is otherwise administered to                     them</td>             </tr>             <tr>                 <td>MedicationStatement</td>                 <td>This is a record of a medication being taken by a patient or that a medication                     has been given to a patient, where the record is the result of a report from the                     patient or another clinician, or derived from supporting information (for                     example, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationrequest">MedicationRequest</Link>). A medication statement is                     not a part of the prescribe-&gt;dispense-&gt;administer sequence but is a report that                     such a sequence (or at least a part of it) did take place, resulting in a belief                     that the patient has received a particular medication. </td>             </tr>         </tbody></table>         <p> This resource is distinct from <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationrequest">MedicationRequest</a>,                 <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationdispense">MedicationDispense</a> and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationadministration">MedicationAdministration</a>. Each of those             resources refers to specific events - an individual order, an individual provisioning of             medication or an individual dosing. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationstatement">MedicationStatement</Link> is a broader assertion covering             a wider timespan and is independent of specific events. The existence of resource             instances of any of the preceding three types may be used to infer a medication             statement. However, medication statements can also be captured on the basis of other             information, including an assertion by the patient or a care-giver, the results of a lab             test, etc. </p>  </div>
  </TabItem>

# MessageHeader

The header for a message exchange that is either requesting or responding to an action. The reference(s) that are the subject of the action as well as other information related to the action are typically transmitted in a bundle in which the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/messageheader">MessageHeader</Link> resource instance is the first resource in the bundle.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/messageheader">MessageHeader</Link> resource is defined in order to support <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/messaging.html">Messaging using FHIR resources</a>. The principal usage of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/messageheader">MessageHeader</Link> resource is when messages are exchanged. However, as a  resource that can be used with the RESTful framework, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/messageheader">MessageHeader</Link> resource has the normal resource end-point ([base-url]/MessageHeader), which is used to manage a set of static messages resources. This could be used to  make an archive of past messages available. <b>Creating or updating Message resources in this fashion does not represent the actual occurrence of any event, nor can it trigger any logic associated with the actual event.</b> It is just for managing a set of message resources. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# MolecularSequence

Raw data describing a biological sequence.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}

## Inherited Elements

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div>      <p>     The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/molecularsequence">MolecularSequence</Link> resource is designed to describe an atomic sequence which contains the alignment sequencing test result and multiple variations. Atomic sequences can be connected by link element and they will lead to sequence graph. By this method, a sequence can be reported. Complete genetic sequence information, of which specific genetic variations are a part, is reported by reference to the GA4GH repository.  Thus, the FHIR <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/molecularsequence">MolecularSequence</Link> resource avoids large genomic payloads in a manner analogous to how the FHIR <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/imagingstudy">ImagingStudy</Link> resource references large images maintained in other systems.     For use cases, details on how this resource interact with other Clinical Genomics resources or profiles, please refer to implementation guidance document <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/genomics.html">here</a>. </p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Genetic Standards and Resources include: <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/molecularsequence.html#10.6.1.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <ul>     <li>Variant Databases: <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/projects/SNP/snp_ref.cgi">dbSNP </a> , <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/">ClinVar </a>, and <a href="http://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/cosmic/">COSMIC </a> </li>     <li>Reference Sequences: <a href="http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/refseq/">RefSeq </a> and <a href="http://www.ensembl.org/index.html">ENSEMBL </a> </li> </ul> <p>     This resource is designed to describe sequence variations with clinical significance with information such as: </p>     <ul>         <li>Name of the variation represented</li>         <li>Type of the variation</li>         <li>Gene region occupied by the variation</li>         <li>Tissue source used to determine genotype of the variation</li>  <li>Quality of the result</li>     </ul> <p>     It is strongly encouraged to provide all available information in this resource for any reported variants, because receiving systems (e.g. discovery research, outcomes analysis, and public health reporting) may use this information to normalize variants over time or across sources.  However, these data should not be used to dynamically correct/change variant representations for clinical use outside of the laboratory, due to insufficient information. </p> <p>     Implementers should be aware that semantic equivalency of results of genetic variants cannot be guaranteed unless there is an agreed upon standard between sending and receiving systems. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p>     Focus of the resource is to provide sequencing alignment data immediately relevant to what the interpretation on clinical decision-making originates from. Hence data such as precise read of DNA sequences and sequence alignment are not included; such data are nonetheless accessible through references to <a href="http://ga4gh.org/#/">GA4GH </a> (Global Alliance for Genomics and Health) API.          The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/molecularsequence">MolecularSequence</Link> resource will be referenced by <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a> to provide variant information. As clinical assessments/diagnosis of a patient are typically captured in the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</a> resource or the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/clinicalimpression">ClinicalImpression</Link> resource, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/molecularsequence">MolecularSequence</Link> resource can be referenced by the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</Link> resource to provide specific genetic data to support assertions. This is analogous to how <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</Link> references other resources, such as <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a>, and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</a> resources. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a></li></ul>

# NamingSystem

A curated namespace that issues unique symbols within that namespace for the identification of concepts, people, devices, etc. Represents a "System" used within the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/identifier">Identifier</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/coding">Coding</Link> data types.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> Defines a specific code system or identifier system, so that it can be noted in a registry for other systems to find and understand an identifier. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p> The <code>CodeSystem</code> resource defines the content of a code system, and also its preferred identifier. The <code>NamingSystem</code> resource identifies the existence of a code or identifier system, and its possible and preferred identifiers.  The key difference between the resources is who creates and manages them - <code>CodeSystem</code> resources are managed by the owner of the code system resource, who can properly define the features and content of the code system. <code>NamingSystem</code> resources, on the other hand, are frequently defined by 3rd parties that encounter the code system in use, and need to describe the use, but do not have the authority to define the features and content.  Additionally, there may be multiple authoritative <code>NamingSystem</code> resources for a code system, but there should only be one <code>CodeSystem</code> resource. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> For discussion of policy for creating well maintained OIDs and URIs for resources, see <a href="https://confluence.hl7.org/display/FHIR/Migrating+OIDs+to+FHIR">The HL7 Confluence site </a>. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

</Tabs>

# NutritionOrder

A request to supply a diet, formula feeding (enteral) or oral nutritional supplement to a patient/resident.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}

## Search Parameters

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p><strong>This resource is a <em>request</em> resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">Workflow</a>.  It is the intent of the Orders and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> Workgroup to align this resource with  the workflow  pattern for <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html"><em>request</em> resources</a>.</strong></p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/nutritionorder">NutritionOrder</Link> resource describes a request for oral diets (including general diets such as General Healthy diet, or therapeutic diets such as Consistent Carbohydrate, 2 gram Sodium, or Fluid Restricted), oral nutrition supplements (such as nutritionally complete pre-packed drinks), enteral nutrition (tube feedings) and infant formula which govern the distribution of food and nutritional products used to feed patients within an in-patient setting. It does not cover orders for parenteral (IV) nutrition which are typically filled by pharmacy. These nutrition orders are combined with information on a patient's food allergies and intolerances, and ethnic or cultural food preferences (e.g. Kosher or Vegetarian) to inform healthcare personnel about the type, texture, and/or quantity of foods that the patient should receive or consume. </p> <p> Enteral orders are distinguished from supplements because they have some unique attributes and typically include administration information whereas oral nutritional supplements may simply be supplied (e.g. home health or outpatient settings).  In a simple case, the requestor may designate type of product, product name and the route of administration along with free text instructions without a having to complete the additional structured details. </p> <p> This resource is intended to be used by providers from a variety of specialties such as physicians, dietitian/nutritionists, or speech therapists.  One provider may simply order a base element oral diet such as General Healthful diet.   Another provider, based on scope of practice, may use other elements to communicate additional therapeutic needs or patient preferences. The optionality included gives an ordering provider the capability to write a simple order for an oral diet, nutritional supplement or formula with minimal requirements beyond that of specifying the diet, supplement or formula product, but also supports  the ability to provide more detailed information that may be further augmented by a dietitian or nutrition specialist. For example, a physician may order a 2 g sodium diet.  A speech therapist, based on the results of a swallowing evaluation, then orders a mechanically altered texture with nectar thick liquids. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p>     The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/nutritionorder">NutritionOrder</Link> resource is used for requesting oral diets, oral nutrition supplements and enteral feedings in an in-patient setting. The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationrequest">MedicationRequest</a> resource should be used for requesting parenteral (IV) nutrition and prescribing dietary supplements such as vitamin or mineral supplements.</p> <p> The Nutrition Order is a record of the request for the supply of a diet, oral supplement or enteral formulas for a patient. However, to initiate the request requires the use of the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/task">Task</a> resource and its associated workflow with the Nutrition Order referenced from <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/task">Task</Link>.basedOn, or by using the Nutrition <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/task">Task</Link> resource in the context of a messaging or service workflow where the request is explicit or implicit. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# Observation

Measurements and simple assertions made about a patient, device or other subject. US Core Profiles related to Observations are as follows:

- [US Core Laboratory Result profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-observation-lab.html)
- [US Core Smoking Status Observation profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-smokingstatus.html).
- [US Core Pulse Oximetry Profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-pulse-oximetry.html)
- [US Core Pediatric BMI for Age Profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-pediatric-bmi-for-age.html)
- [US Core Pediatric Weight for Height](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-pediatric-weight-for-height.html)
- [US Core Pediatric Head Circumference](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-head-occipital-frontal-circumference-percentile.html)
- [US Core Observation Survey](http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/StructureDefinition-us-core-observation-survey.html)
- [US Core Observation Social History](http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/StructureDefinition-us-core-observation-social-history.html)
- [US Core Clinical Test Result](http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/StructureDefinition-us-core-observation-clinical-test.html)
- [US Core Observation Sexual Orientation](http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/StructureDefinition-us-core-observation-sexual-orientation.html)

  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div>          <p>This resource is an <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">         <em>event resource</em>       </a> from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">Workflow</a>.</p>     <p>Observations are a central element in healthcare, used to support diagnosis, monitor progress, determine baselines and patterns and even capture demographic characteristics.  Most observations are simple name/value pair assertions with some metadata, but some observations group other observations together logically, or even are multi-component observations. Note that the  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</a> resource provides a clinical or workflow context for a set of observations and the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> resource is referenced by <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> to represent laboratory, imaging, and other clinical and diagnostic data to form a complete report. </p>     <p>Uses for the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> resource include:</p>     <ul>       <li>Vital signs such as <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-example.html">body weight</a>,  <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-example-bloodpressure.html">blood pressure</a>, and <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-example-f202-temperature.html">temperature</a>       </li>       <li>Laboratory Data like <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-example-f001-glucose.html">blood glucose</a>, or an <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-example-f205-egfr.html">estimated GFR</a>       </li>       <li>Imaging results like  <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-example-bmd.html">bone density</a> or fetal measurements</li>       <li>Clinical Findings<sup>†</sup> such as  <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-example-abdo-tender.html">abdominal tenderness</a>       </li>       <li>Device measurements such as  <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-example-sample-data.html">EKG data</a> or  <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-example-satO2.html">Pulse Oximetry data</a>       </li>       <li>Clinical assessment tools such as <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-example-5minute-apgar-score.html">APGAR</a> or a <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-example-glasgow.html">Glasgow Coma Score</a>       </li>       <li>Personal characteristics: such as  <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-example-eye-color.html">eye-color</a>       </li>       <li>Social history like tobacco use,  family support, or cognitive status</li>       <li>Core characteristics like pregnancy status, or a death assertion</li>     </ul>     <p>     <sup>†</sup>The boundaries between clinical findings and disorders remains a challenge in medical ontology.  Refer the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/#bnr">Boundaries</a> section below and in <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</a> for general guidance.  These boundaries can be clarified by profiling <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> for a particular use case.     </p>     <a name="core"></a>     <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Core Profiles for <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/versions.html#std-process" title="Standards Status = Trial Use">Trial Use</a> <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3>     <p>The following core <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/profiling.html">profiles</a> for the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> resource have been defined as well. If implementations use this Resource when expressing the profile-specific concepts as structured data, they <strong>SHALL</strong> conform to the following profiles:</p>     <table class="grid">       <thead>         <tr>           <th>Profile</th>           <th>Description</th>         </tr>       </thead>       <tbody>         <tr>           <td>             <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/observation-vitalsigns.html">Vital signs</a>           </td>           <td>The FHIR Vital Signs profile sets minimum expectations for the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> Resource to record, search and fetch the vital signs (e.g. temperature, blood pressure, respiration rate, etc.) associated with a patient </td>         </tr>       </tbody>     </table>   </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div>     <a name="bnr">     </a>          <p> At its core, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> allows expressing a name-value pair or structured collection of name-value pairs. As such, it can support conveying any type of information desired. However, that is not its intent. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> is intended for capturing measurements and subjective point-in-time assessments. It is not intended to be used for those specific contexts and use cases already covered by other FHIR resources.   For example, the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</a> resource represents a patient allergies, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationstatement">MedicationStatement</a> resource: medications taken by a patient, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/familymemberhistory"> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/familymemberhistory">FamilyMemberHistory</Link></a> resource: a patient's family history, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a> resource: information about a procedure, and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaireresponse">QuestionnaireResponse</a> resource: a set of answers to a set of questions. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> resource should not be used to record clinical diagnosis about a patient or subject that are typically captured in the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</a> resource or the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/clinicalimpression">ClinicalImpression</Link> resource.  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> resource is often referenced by the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/condition">Condition</Link> resource to provide specific subjective and objective data to support its assertions.  There will however be situations of overlap. For example, a response to a question of "have you ever taken illicit drugs" could in principle be represented using <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationstatement">MedicationStatement</Link>, but most systems would treat such an assertion as an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link>.  In some cases, such as when source data is coming from an <a href="http://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=185">HL7 v2 </a> feed, a system might not have information that allows it to distinguish diagnosis, allergy and other "specialized" types of observations from laboratory, vital sign and other observation types intended to be conveyed with this resource.  In those circumstances, such specialized observations may also appear using this resource. Adhering to such convention is an appropriate use of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link>. If implementers are uncertain whether a proposed use of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> is appropriate, they're encouraged to consult with implementers on <a href="https://chat.fhir.org/"> chat.fhir.org implementer's stream </a>     </p>   <p>   The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/media">Media</a> resource captures a specific type of observation whose value is audio, video or image data. This resource is used instead of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> to represent such forms of information as it exposes the metadata relevant for interpreting the information.   See <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/media">Media</Link>'s <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/media">boundaries section</a> to see how <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/media">Media</Link> (and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link>) differs from <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/imagingstudy">ImagingStudy</a> and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/documentreference">DocumentReference</a>.   </p>   <p>   In contrast to the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> resource, the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</a> resource typically includes additional clinical context and some mix of atomic results, images, imaging reports, textual and coded interpretation, and formatted representations.  Laboratory reports, pathology reports, and imaging reports should be represented using the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> resource. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> resource is referenced by the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> to provide the atomic results for a particular investigation.  "Laboratories routinely have a variable that is summative across a series of discrete variables - these are usually called 'impressions' or 'interpretations'. Sometimes they are algorithmically specified and sometimes they have the imprimatur of pathologists and they are conveyed in <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> instead of the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/clinicalimpression">Clinical Impression</a> resource.  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> resource should not be used to record clinical diagnosis about a patient or subject as discussed above.   </p>   </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/adverseevent">AdverseEvent</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/appointment">Appointment</a></li>

# ObservationDefinition

# ObservationDefinition

Set of definitional characteristics for a kind of observation or measurement produced or consumed by an orderable health care service.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="bnc"> </a> <blockquote class="stu-note">   <a name="dstu"></a> <strong>Note that this content is preliminary has not undergone proper review by the appropriate Workgroups.</strong> </blockquote> <p> An instance of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observationdefinition">ObservationDefinition</Link> represents the definitional aspects of a kind of observation. This resource is used in a catalog of products or services for healthcare. It provides the definition of observations, which are used as input or produced as outcome of these products and services. The focus of the definitional aspects of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observationdefinition">ObservationDefinition</Link> is not on the action of performing observations of that kind. Rather, it is on the outcome of the observations. An instance of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observationdefinition">ObservationDefinition</Link> represents a set of constraints applicable to the value produced by observations of this kind. This set of constraints may have two utilities: 1) It guides the entry of the result of an observation of the kind defined. 2) It helps the consumer of the results of observations of that kind, to interpret properly these results. </p> <p> For instance, in a catalog of laboratory in vitro diagnostic services, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observationdefinition">ObservationDefinition</Link> resources describe the observations that should be provided by the orderer alongside with an ordered service (questions asked at order entry or at specimen collection, prior results) as well as the observations that will be reported once the service has been performed. </p> <p> In a catalog of medications, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observationdefinition">ObservationDefinition</Link> resources can be used to describe observations the result thereof need to be checked against the prescription of a particular medicinal product (therapeutic range, units ...) </p> <p> In the catalog of tests of an in vitro diagnostic device, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observationdefinition">ObservationDefinition</Link> resources can be used to characterize (absolute range, unit, decimal precision, critical values ...) the observations that will be produced by the IVD tests performed by the device. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observationdefinition">ObservationDefinition</Link> may be used to characterize observations from any discipline. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p> This resource relates to these other resource:. </p>  <ul> <li>Resource <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observationdefinition">ObservationDefinition</Link> is referenced by resource <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/catalogentry">CatalogEntry</Link>. This enables items of catalogs, representing healthcare services or products, to declare the observations, which are consumed or produced by these items.</li> <li>Observation.basedOn references <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observationdefinition">ObservationDefinition</Link> resource.</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>

<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationdefinition">OperationDefinition</Link> resource provides a formal computable definition of an <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/operations.html">operation</a> or <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/search.html#advanced">a named query</a>. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationdefinition">OperationDefinition</Link> serves two principal purposes: </p> <ul>  <li>To allow for automatic determination of system compatibility</li>  <li>To allow for dynamic generation of forms to drive the operations</li> </ul> <p> See below for further information about these, and about how operations and named queries are executed. </p> </div>

This allows for a server to describe a limited implementation of a standard operation, or to allow traceability if the server has to rename the operation due to a name clash</li> </ul> </div>

# OperationOutcome

A collection of error, warning, or information messages that result from a system action.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}

  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> Operation outcomes are sets of error, warning and information messages that provide detailed information about the outcome of an attempted system operation.   They are provided as a direct system response, or component of one, and provide information about the outcome of the operation. </p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationoutcome">OperationOutcome</Link> resource is used in the following circumstances: </p> <ul>  <li>When a <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/http.html#operations">RESTful interaction</a> or <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/operations.html">operation</a> fails</li>  <li>As the response on a <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/http.html#validate">validation operation</a> to provide information about the outcome</li>  <li>As part of a message response, usually when the message has not been processed correctly</li>  <li>As the response to a batch/transaction, when requested</li>  <li>As part of a search's <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</Link> response containing information about the search</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> This resource is not used for reporting clinical or workflow issues associated with a proposed or ongoing action;  these would be handled using <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/detectedissue">DetectedIssue</a> or other resources. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationoutcome">OperationOutcome</Link>   is not designed to be persisted or referenced from other parts of the workflow.  </p> <p> It is possible to have both <code>OperationOutcome</code> and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/detectedissue">DetectedIssue</a> together, where the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationoutcome">OperationOutcome</Link> might  indicate that a requested action was rejected due to a clinical issue and the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/detectedissue">DetectedIssue</Link> provides the details of the issue. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

A formally or informally recognized grouping of people or organizations formed for the purpose of achieving some form of collective action. Includes companies, institutions, corporations, departments, community groups, healthcare practice groups, payer/insurer, etc.

The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</a> resource is used to identify a collection of people (or animals, devices, etc.)  that are gathered for the purpose of analysis or acting upon, but are not expected to act themselves. </p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link> resource often exists as a hierarchy of organization resources, using the <i>part-of</i> property to provide the association of the child to its parent organization.<br/> This organizational hierarchy helps communicate the conceptual structure, whereas the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/location">Location</Link> resource provides the physical representation of the hierarchy.<br/> The linkage between <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/location">Location</Link> is from each point in the location hierarchy to the appropriate level in the  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link> hierarchy. These links don't all have to be to the top level <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link>.<br/> When populating the organization and location hierarchies there is often not a clear distinction between these 2, however to assist in making the decision, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/location">Locations</Link> are always used for recording where a service occurs, and hence where encounters and observations are associated. # OrganizationAffiliation

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/organizationaffiliation.mdx

title: OrganizationAffiliation
sidebar_position: 100

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/organizationaffiliation.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# OrganizationAffiliation

Defines an affiliation/assotiation/relationship between 2 distinct oganizations, that is not a part-of relationship/sub-division relationship.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> A relationship between 2 organizations over a period of time, where the entities are separate business entities. The relationship can optionally include details of locations/services from the participating organization. </p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organizationaffiliation">OrganizationAffiliation</Link> enables defining  non-hierarchical relationships between organizations. For example: </p> <ul>   <li>One organization may provide services to another organization<br/>   <i>e.g. An agency service providing casual staff, a radiology service,    a diagnostic lab, catering services, community care services etc.</i></li>   <li>Two or more organizations may form a partnership or joint venture</li>   <li>An organization may be a member of an association, but not owned by it<br/>   <i>e.g. a hospital is a member the American Hospital Association,    a hospital is a member of a health information exchange network</i></li>      </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link>.partOf is used to form a hierarchical relationships within an organization which eventually resolves  to a single organization. Each child in the tree is a subdivision of the parent.<br/> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organizationaffiliation">OrganizationAffiliation</Link> is used to describe the relationship between two distinct organizations. It does not require a hierarchical relationship. A resource instance is for a singular linkage between 2 organizations (it does not contain all members), to create multiple affiliations, create additional resources for the other relationship between other organizations.<br/> Each instance contains its own period, and optionally links to specific related services/locations that are available. These referenced locations/services should be associated with the participating organization, and are available to the primary organization. </p> <p> This resource should not be used when the affiliates are part of a single organization. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

</Tabs>

A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> record is generally  created and maintained by each organization providing care for a patient. Such fields vary widely between jurisdictions and often have different  names and valuesets for the similar concepts, but they are not similar enough to be able to map and exchange. </p> </div>

# PaymentNotice

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentnotice.mdx

title: PaymentNotice
sidebar_position: 103

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';

import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# PaymentNotice

This resource provides the status of the payment for goods and services rendered, and the request and response resource references.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentnotice">PaymentNotice</Link> resource indicates the resource for which the payment has been indicated and  reports the current status information of that payment. The payment notice may be used by providers and payers  to advise the provider or regulatory bodies of the state of a payment (check in the mail/EFT sent,  payment cashed, payment canceled). Employers or Insurance Exchanges may use this to advise payers of  premium payment. </p> <p> Payers and/or providers may have the need to advise providers and/or regulators of the status of claim settlement and payment completion.  This same resource may be used by employers and insurance exchanges to advise payers that premium payments have been  issued and settled. </p> <p>    </p> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentnotice">PaymentNotice</Link> resource is a "event" resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">Workflow Event.</a></p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Additional Information <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/paymentnotice.html#13.8.1.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> Additional information regarding electronic payment notice content and usage may be found at: </p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#resource-status">Financial Resource Status Lifecycle</a>: how .status is used in the financial resources.</li> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#batch">Batches</a>: how eClaims may handle batches of eligibility, claims, payments and responses.</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentnotice">PaymentNotice</Link> resource is used to indicate that a payment is, or is about to occur. The resource is used commonly when tracking of payment occurences is required for regulatory or business purposes, such as ensuring that payment of claim adjudications occurs within a specific timeframe. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentnotice">PaymentNotice</Link> is not used to report adjudicated amounts (see <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</a>) or to reconcile adjudicated amounts against actual payment (see <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentreconciliation">PaymentReconciliation</a>)  </p> <p> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</a> resource is an insurer's adjudication and/or authorization of a set of healthcare-related goods and services for a patient against the patient's insurance coverages and does not indicate that payment has occured. </p> <p> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentreconciliation">PaymentReconciliation</a> resource serves to correlate payment amounts to the adjudicated claim amounts appearing on one or more <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponses</a>. </p> <p> <b>The eClaim domain includes a number of related resources</b> </p> <table border="1" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="2" frame="box"> <tbody><tr> <td>PaymentNotice</td> <td>An indication that a payment has occured, is about to occur, or has been cancelled.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</a></td> <td>A payor's adjudication and/or authorization response to the suite of services provided in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>. Typically the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> references the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> but does not duplicate the clinical or financial information provided in the claim.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentreconciliation">PaymentReconciliation</a></td> <td>Provides the bulk payment details  associated with a payment by the payor for goods and services rendered by a provider to patients  covered by insurance plans offered by that payor.</td> </tr> </tbody></table> </div>
  </TabItem>

</Tabs>

# PaymentReconciliation

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentreconciliation.mdx

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';

# PaymentReconciliation

This resource provides the details including amount of a payment and allocates the payment items being paid.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentreconciliation">PaymentReconciliation</Link> resource provides the bulk payment details  associated with a payment by the payor for receivable amounts, such as for goods and services rendered by a provider to patients  covered by insurance plans offered by that payor. These are the payment reconciliation details which may align to the individual payment amounts indicated on discrete <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponses</a> or <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/invoice">Invoices</a> for example. </p> <p> Bulk payments need to provide a means to associate the amounts paid against specific <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claims</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/invoice">Invoices</Link>,  and other financial exchanges and adjustments, to the bulk payment itself in order to reconcile  accounts receivable. </p> <p>    </p> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentreconciliation">PaymentReconciliation</Link> resource is a "event" resource from a FHIR workflow perspective - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">Workflow Event.</a></p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Additional Information <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/paymentreconciliation.html#13.9.1.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> Additional information regarding electronic payment notice content and usage may be found at: </p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/financial-module.html#resource-status">Financial Resource Status Lifecycle</a>: how .status is used in the financial resources.</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentreconciliation">PaymentReconciliation</Link> resource serves to correlate a payment amount to the adjudicated claim amounts appearing on one or more <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponses</a>. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentreconciliation">PaymentReconciliation</Link> provides the bulk payment details  associated with a payment by the payor for goods and services rendered by a provider to patients  covered by insurance plans offered by that payor. </p> <p> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentnotice">PaymentNotice</a> resource is used to indicate that a payment has, or is about to occur. The resource is used commonly when tracking of payment occurences is required for regulatory or business purposes.  </p> <p> The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</a> resource is an insurer's adjudication and/or authorization of a set of healthcare-related goods and services for a patient against the patient's insurance coverages and does not indicate that payment has occured. </p> <p> For reporting out to patients or transferring data to patient centered applications, such as patient health Record (PHR) application, the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</a>  should be used instead. </p> <p> <b>The eClaim domain includes a number of related resources</b> </p> <table border="1" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="2" frame="box"> <tbody><tr> <td>PaymentReconciliation</td> <td>Provides the bulk payment details  associated with a payment by the payor for goods and services rendered by a provider to patients  covered by insurance plans offered by that payor.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</a></td> <td>A payor's adjudication and/or authorization response to the suite of services provided in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link>. Typically the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link> references the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> but does not duplicate the clinical or financial information provided in the claim.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/explanationofbenefit">ExplanationOfBenefit</a></td> <td>This resource combines the information from the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claim">Claim</Link> and the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/claimresponse">ClaimResponse</Link>, stripping out any provider or payor proprietary information, into a unified information model  suitable for use for: patient reporting; transferring information to a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> Health Record system; and, supporting complete claim and adjudication information exchange  with regulatory and analytics organizations and other parts of the provider's organization. </td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/paymentnotice">PaymentNotice</a></td> <td>An indication that a payment has occured, is about to occur, or has been cancelled.</td> </tr> </tbody></table> </div>
  </TabItem>
