# Person

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/person.mdx

title: Person
sidebar_position: 105

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/person.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# Person

Demographics and administrative information about a person independent of a specific health-related context.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p>   The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/person">Person</Link> resource serves as a linkage resource that may provide a reference set of common demographics    for an individual (human or animal) across multiple roles.<br/>   This linkage can be direct to role-specific FHIR resources (Patient, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/relatedperson">RelatedPerson</Link>)   residing on the same or possibly distinct FHIR systems/applications, or indirectly through the use of   business identifiers. </p>   <p>   The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/person">Person</Link> resource may be used in many situations/contexts, including:   </p>   <ul>   <li>A set of demographics that can be used to co-ordinate the maintenance of this   de-normalized information across practitioners, patients and/or related persons<br/>   <i>e.g. link known resources of the different types together within a system</i></li>   <li>A state/network based Master <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/person">Person</Link> Index<br/>   <i>e.g. A National <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/identifier">Identifier</Link> Index or a Network membership/subscriber list</i></li>   <li>A central register that links patient resources from multiple servers, indicating they   all correspond to the same individual<br/>   <i>e.g. Within a large organization with many systems to be able to link the various records,    without having to modify the source information with external links</i></li>   <li>A support for access monitoring software that is able to assert what practitioner,    patient and related person records correspond to the same human being to assist in    detecting improper querying.<br/>   <i>e.g. asserting that a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> A is the same individual as a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/relatedperson">RelatedPerson</Link> B who is   related to <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> C, who is also <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> D.  As such, monitoring for <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link>   D’s accesses to <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> A’s records should be carefully scrutinized.</i></li>   <li>Local record(s) on a mobile device listing links to remote server patient resources<br/>   <i>e.g. A mobile phone application storing references to the hospitals they have access to</i></li>   </ul>   <blockquote class="stu-note">     <a name="advanced"></a>     <p>     <b>Note:</b>  The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/person">Person</Link> resource is an advanced feature.  Many systems don’t have a way     to relate information across resource types, or systems, especially from <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> to     <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link>, and therefore might not implement this functionality. Some do have ways     of relating the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/relatedperson">RelatedPerson</Link> resource types. FHIR is also able to do this     without the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/person">Person</Link> resource, utilizing the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link>.link property     <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">(as shown in the Mother and newborn relationship example)</a>     </p>   </blockquote> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div>   <p>     <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/person">Person</Link> resources may have references to <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/relatedperson">RelatedPerson</Link> and/or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> resources.      These linkages assert that all the records relate to the same individual.   </p>   <p>     <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/person">Person</Link> instances are never directly referenced as actors (authors, subjects, performers, etc.)     Individual actors are always identified as either <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/relatedperson">RelatedPerson</Link>, depending on the role     of the individual when undertaking the action. Therefore this resource SHALL NOT be referenced by any     other clinical or administrative resources.       E.g. it can be the focus of an operation or message or included in a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/bundle">Bundle</Link>,      but cannot be a member of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">List</Link> or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</Link>, the subject of an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link>, or other similar non-infrastructural usage.   </p>   <p>     In some use cases the linkages will be indirect, and through business <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/identifier">Identifiers</Link>, such as in the case of     the various types of Master <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/person">Person</Link> Indexes, where the records are not there for the purpose of healthcare,      but simply describing a population of people, and has other purposes and not just to represent a population patients.   </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

</Tabs>

# PlanDefinition

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition.mdx

title: PlanDefinition
sidebar_position: 106

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/plandefinition.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# PlanDefinition

This resource allows for the definition of various types of plans as a sharable, consumable, and executable artifact. The resource is general enough to support the description of a broad range of clinical artifacts such as clinical decision support rules, order sets and protocols.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p><strong>This resource is a <em>definition</em> resource from a FHIR workflow perspective</strong> - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">Workflow</a>, specifically <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#definition">Definition</a>.</p> <p>A plan definition is a pre-defined group of actions to be taken in particular circumstances, often including conditional elements, options, and other decision points. The resource is flexible enough to be used to represent a variety of workflows, as well as clinical decision support and quality improvement assets, including order sets, protocols, and decision support rules.</p> <p>PlanDefinitions can contain hierarchical groups of action definitions, where each action definition describes an activity to be performed (often in terms of an <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/activitydefinition">ActivityDefinition</a> resource), and each group defines additional behavior, relationships, and applicable conditions between the actions in the overall definition.</p> <p>In addition to describing what should take place, each action in a plan definition can specify <i>when</i> and <i>whether</i> the action should take place. For when the action should be taken, the <code>trigger</code> element specifies the action should be taken in response to some trigger occurring (such as a particular point in a workflow being reached, or as the result of a prescription being ordered). For whether the action should be taken, the <code>condition</code> element can be used to provide an expression that evaluates to true or false to indicate the applicability of the action to the specific context.</p> <p>The process of applying a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> to a particular context typically produces request resources representing the actions that should be performed, typically grouped within a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</a> and/or <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/requestgroup">RequestGroup</a> to capture relationships between the resulting request resources.</p> <p>Each <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/activitydefinition">ActivityDefinition</Link> is used to construct a specific resource, based on the definition of the activity and combined with contextual information for the particular patient that the plan definition is being applied to.</p> <p>As with the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/activitydefinition">ActivityDefinition</Link>, a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> may provide information about how to transform the activity to a specific intent resource, either by specifying a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/structuremap">StructureMap</a> that can be used to perform the transformation completely, or by specifying values for specific elements of the resulting resource using <code>dynamicValue</code> elements in the action.</p> <p>Note that these mechanisms are provided on both the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/activitydefinition">ActivityDefinition</Link> and the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> to allow both reusable transformation descriptions, as well as customization of those descriptions within specific contexts. As such, the transform descriptions specified on the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> <i>override</i> transform descriptions defined on the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/activitydefinition">ActivityDefinition</Link>.</p> <p>Dynamic values within the definitions can be provided by specifying the expression directly, or by referencing an expression defined within a library. For more information on how to reference expressions within resources, refer to the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/clinicalreasoning-topics-using-expressions.html">Using <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/expression">Expressions</Link></a> topic.</p> <p>As an example, the Low Suicide Risk example order set from the Clinical Decision Support Knowledge Artifact Specification can be represented using the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/activitydefinition">ActivityDefinition</Link> structures: <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/plandefinition-example.html">Low Suicide Risk Example Order Set</a>.</p> <p>In addition to the representation of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinitions</Link>, the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/plandefinition-operation-apply.html">$apply</a> operation allows <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinitions</Link> to be applied to a specific context such as a patient, practitioner, or institution. For Order Sets specifically, this operation is expected to place the orders defined by the order set, consistent with the service functional requirements defined by the <a href="http://www.hl7.org/implement/standards/product_brief.cfm?product_id=287">Order Set specification </a>.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> resource is used to describe series, sequences, or groups of actions to be taken, while the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/activitydefinition">ActivityDefinition</a> resource is used to define each specific step or activity to be performed.</p> <p>As the name implies, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> resource is strictly definitional. It does not represent the intention to take any action, nor does it represent that any actions have been taken. Rather, the resource provides a definition that can be applied in the appropriate circumstances. When the plan definition is applied, the result will in general be a set of actions that should be (or potentially even have been) performed.</p> <p>Note that the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> still has action-level information, as well as a reference to an <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/activitydefinition">ActivityDefinition</a>. The action-level information defined in the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> itself is used to describe how the actions are related to each other within the plan, where the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/activitydefinition">ActivityDefinition</Link> contains only information about the activity itself. In addition, there is some overlapping information that allows the resources to be used independently, or in combination. See the Applying a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> section for more information.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">

# Practitioner

# Practitioner

A person who is directly or indirectly involved in the provisioning of healthcare.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> covers all individuals who are engaged in the healthcare process and healthcare-related services as part of their formal  responsibilities and this Resource is used for attribution of activities and responsibilities to these individuals. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioners</Link> include (but are not limited to): </p> <ul> <li>physicians,&nbsp;dentists,&nbsp;pharmacists</li> <li>physician assistants,&nbsp;nurses, scribes</li> <li>midwives,&nbsp;dietitians,&nbsp;therapists,&nbsp;optometrists, paramedics</li> <li>medical technicians,&nbsp;laboratory scientists, prosthetic technicians, radiographers</li> <li>social workers, professional homecare providers, official volunteers</li> <li>receptionists handling patient registration</li> <li>IT personnel merging or unmerging patient records</li> <li>Service animal (e.g., ward assigned dog capable of detecting cancer in patients)</li> </ul> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> The Resource SHALL NOT be used for persons involved without a formal responsibility like individuals taking care for friends,  relatives or neighbors. These can be registered as a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link>'s Contact.  If performing some action or being referenced by another resource, use the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/relatedperson">RelatedPerson</a> resource. </p> <p> The primary distinction between a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> and a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/relatedperson">RelatedPerson</Link> is based on whether: </p> <ul> <li> The person/animal operates on behalf of the care delivery organization over multiple patients (Practitioner) or, </li> <li> Where the person/animal is not associated with the organization, and instead is allocated tasks specifically for the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/relatedperson">RelatedPerson</Link>'s <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link> (RelatedPerson). </li> </ul> <p> A standard extension <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/extension-practitioner-animalspecies.html">animalSpecies</a> can be used to indicate the species of a service animal. </p> <p>   The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitionerrole">PractitionerRole</a> resource provides the details of roles that the practitioner    is approved to perform for which organizations (and at which locations, and optionally what services too). </p> <p>   <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioners</Link> are also often grouped into <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careteam">CareTeams</a> independently of roles, where the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careteam">CareTeam</Link>   defines what specific role that they are fulfilling within the team, and might or might not have actual practitioner role resources   created for the practitioner (and in the care team context, the organization the practitioner is representing) </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> performs different roles within the same or even different organizations. Depending on jurisdiction and custom,  it may be necessary to maintain a specific <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> Resource for each such role or have a single <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> with multiple roles. The role can be limited to a specific period, after which authorization for this role ends. Note that the represented organization need not necessarily be the (direct) employer of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link>. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# PractitionerRole

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitionerrole.mdx

title: PractitionerRole
sidebar_position: 108

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';

# PractitionerRole

A specific set of Roles/Locations/specialties/services that a practitioner may perform at an organization for a period of time.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitionerrole">PractitionerRole</Link> covers the recording of the location and types of services that <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioners</Link> are able to provide for an organization. </p> <p> The role, specialty, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/location">Location</Link> telecom and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/healthcareservice">HealthcareService</Link> properties can be repeated if required in other instances of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitionerrole">PractitionerRole</Link>. Some systems record a collection of service values for a single location, others record the  single service and the list of locations it is available. Both are acceptable options for representing this data.<br/> Where availability, telecom, or other details are not the same across all healthcareservices, or locations  a seperate <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitionerrole">PractitionerRole</Link> instance should be created. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> Qualifications (from the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> resource) do not imply a Role, but might be considered when an <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/organization">Organization</Link>    allocates practitioners to roles within their organization, and could provide useful information (such as expiry information)   which could need to be tracked in some situations to ensure they continue to be eligible for a specific role. </p> <p>   The <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careteam">CareTeam</a> resource is also often used to provide details of a role that a practitioner is   allocated to perform, but is usually scoped to a much finer granularity of care, and often within the specific context   of a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</a>, or functional role (e.g. Crisis planning team). In contrast the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitionerrole">PractitionerRole</Link>   is used in a more general sense to cover all the places that the practitioner is allocated to work (and specific details   relevant to that role - such as a specific contact number, or electronic services endpoint). </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> performs different roles within the same or even different organizations. Depending on jurisdiction and custom,  it may be necessary to maintain a specific <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> Resource for each such role or have a single <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link> with multiple roles. The role can be limited to a specific period, after which authorization for this role ends. Note that the represented organization need not necessarily be the (direct) employer of a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link>. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# Procedure

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure.mdx

title: Procedure
sidebar_position: 109

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';

# Procedure

An action that is or was performed on or for a patient. This can be a physical intervention like an operation, or less invasive like long term services, counseling, or hypnotherapy. Refer to the [US Core Procedure profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-procedure.html).

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p>Procedure is one of the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">event</a> resources in the FHIR <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">workflow</a> specification.</p> <p> This resource is used to record the details of current and historical procedures performed on or for a patient. A procedure is an activity  that is performed on, with, or for a patient as part of the provision of care. Examples include surgical  procedures, diagnostic procedures, endoscopic procedures, biopsies, counseling, physiotherapy, personal support services, adult day care services, non-emergency transportation, home modification, exercise, etc. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedures</Link> may be performed by a healthcare professional, a service provider, a friend or relative or in some cases by the patient themselves. </p> <p> This resource provides summary information about the occurrence of the procedure and is not intended to provide real-time snapshots of a procedure as it unfolds, though for long-running procedures such as psychotherapy, it could represent summary level information about overall progress.  The creation of a resource to support detailed real-time procedure information awaits the identification of a specific implementation use-case to share such information. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</Link> resource should not be used to capture an event if a more specific resource already exists - i.e.  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunization">immunizations</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationadministration">drug administrations</a> and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communication">communications</a>. The boundary between determining whether an action is a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</Link>  (training or counseling) as opposed to a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communication">Communication</Link> is based on whether there's a specific intent to change the mind-set of the patient.  Mere disclosure of information would be considered a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communication">Communication</Link>.  A process that involves verification of the patient's comprehension or to change the patient's mental state would be a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</Link>. </p> <p> Note that many diagnostic processes are procedures that generate <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observations</a> and  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReports</a>. In many cases,  such an observation does not require an explicit representation of the procedure used to create the  observation, but where there are details of interest about how the diagnostic procedure was performed,  the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</Link> resource is used to describe the activity. </p> <p> Some diagnostic procedures might not have a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</Link> record. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</Link> record is only necessary when  there is a need to capture information about the physical intervention that was performed to capture the diagnostic  information (e.g. anesthetic, incision, scope size, etc.)</p> <p> A <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/task">Task</a> is a workflow step such as cancelling an order, fulfilling an order, signing an order, merging a set of records, admitting a patient.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedures</Link> are actions that are intended to result in a physical or mental change to or for the subject (e.g. surgery, physiotherapy, training, counseling).  A <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/task">Task</a> resource often exists in parallel with clinical resources. For example, a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/task">Task</a> might request fulfillment of a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</a> ordering a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</Link>. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# Provenance

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance.mdx

title: Provenance
sidebar_position: 110

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/provenance.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# Provenance

Provenance of a resource is a record that describes entities and processes involved in producing and delivering or otherwise influencing that resource. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> provides a critical foundation for assessing authenticity, enabling trust, and allowing reproducibility. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> assertions are a form of contextual metadata and can themselves become important records with their own provenance. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> statement indicates clinical significance in terms of confidence in authenticity, reliability, and trustworthiness, integrity, and stage in lifecycle (e.g. Document Completion - has the artifact been legally authenticated), all of which may impact security, privacy, and trust policies.

Refer to the [US Core Provenance profile](https://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/stu3.1.1/StructureDefinition-us-core-provenance.html).

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resource tracks information about the activity that created, revised, deleted, or signed a version of a resource, describing the entities and agents involved. This information can be used to form assessments about its quality, reliability, trustworthiness, or to provide pointers for where to go to further investigate the origins of the resource and the information in it.  </p> <p> <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance resources</a> are a record-keeping assertion that gathers information about the context in which the information in a resource was obtained.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resources are prepared by the application that initiates the create/update etc. of the resource. An <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/auditevent">AuditEvent</a> resource contains overlapping information, but is created as events occur, to track and audit the events.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/auditevent">AuditEvent</Link> resources are often (though not exclusively) created by the application responding to the read/query/create/update/etc. event.  </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <a name="overlap"></a> <p> Many other FHIR resources contain some elements that represent information about how the resource was obtained, and therefore they overlap with the  functionality of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resource. These properties in other resources should always be used in preference to the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resource, and the  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resource should be used where additional information is required, or explicit record or provenance is desired.  </p> <p> The relationship between a resource and its provenance is established by a reference from the provenance resource to its target. In this way, provenance may be provided about any resource or version, including past versions. There may be multiple provenance records for a given resource or version of a resource. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resource is based on the <a href="http://www.w3.org/TR/2013/NOTE-prov-overview-20130430/">W3C <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> specification </a>,  and mappings are provided. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resource is tailored to fit the FHIR use-cases for provenance more directly.  In terms of <a href="http://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/">W3C <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> </a> the FHIR <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance resource</a> covers "Generation" of "Entity" with  respect to FHIR defined resources for creation or updating;  whereas <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/auditevent">AuditEvent</a> covers "Usage" of "Entity" and all other "Activity" as defined in W3C <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link>. </p> <p> The W3C <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> Specification has the following fundamental model: </p> <p> </p> <p> Where: </p> <ul> <li>Entity - An entity is a physical, digital, conceptual or other kind of thing with some fixed aspects; entities may be real or imaginary.</li> <li>Agent - An agent is something that bears some form of responsibility for an activity taking place, for the existence of an entity, or for another agent's activity.</li> <li>Activity - An activity is something that occurs over a time period and acts upon or with entities. It may include consuming, processing, transforming, modifying, relocating, using, or generating entities.</li> </ul> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resource corresponds to a single activity that identifies a set of resources (<i>target</i>) generated by the activity. The activity also references other entities (<i>entity</i>) that were used and the agents (<i>agent</i>) that were associated with the activity.  To record multiple activities that resulted in one (<i>target</i>), record each (<i>activity</i>) in independent <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> records all pointing at that (<i>target</i>). </p> <p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resource depends upon having <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/reference">References</Link> to all the resources, entities, and agents involved in the  activity. These <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/reference">References</Link> need not be resolvable. The references must provide a unique and unambiguous identification.  If a resource, entity, or agent can have different versions that must be identified, then the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/reference">Reference</Link> must have  versioning information included. </p><p> Versioning and unique identification are not mandated for all systems that provide Resources, entities, and agents.  But, inclusion of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> requirements may introduce requirements for versioning and unique identification on those systems </p><p> The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resource is based on leveraging the W3C <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> specification  to represent HL7 support of provenance throughout  its standards and explicitly modeled as functional capabilities in ISO/HL7 10781 EHR System Functional Model Release 2 and  ISO 21089 Trusted End-to-End Information Flows.  Mappings are provided. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resource is tailored to fit the  FHIR use-cases for provenance more directly. In terms of W3C <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> the FHIR <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link> resources  covers "Generation" of "Entity" with respect to FHIR defined resources for creation or updating; whereas <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/auditevent">AuditEvent</Link>  covers "Usage" of "Entity" and all other "Activity" as defined in W3C <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/provenance">Provenance</Link>.  </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/devicerequest">DeviceRequest</a></li>

# Questionnaire

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire.mdx

title: Questionnaire
sidebar_position: 111

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/questionnaire.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# Questionnaire

A structured set of questions intended to guide the collection of answers from end-users. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaires</Link> provide detailed control over order, presentation, phraseology and grouping to allow coherent, consistent data collection.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> A <b>Questionnaire</b> is an organized collection of questions intended to solicit information from patients, providers or other individuals involved in the healthcare domain.  They may be simple flat lists of questions or can be hierarchically organized in groups and sub-groups, each containing questions.  The <b>Questionnaire</b> defines the questions to be asked, how they are ordered and grouped, any intervening instructional text and what the constraints are on the allowed answers.  The results of a <b>Questionnaire</b> can be communicated using the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaireresponse">QuestionnaireResponse</a> resource. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaires</Link> cover the need to communicate data originating from forms used in medical history examinations, research questionnaires and sometimes full clinical specialty records. In many systems this data is collected using user-defined screens and forms. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaires</Link> define specifics about data capture - exactly what questions were asked, in what order, what choices for answers were, etc. Each of these questions is part of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link>, and as such the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link> is a separately identifiable Resource, whereas the individual questions are not.  (Questionnaire questions can be linked to shared data elements using the <code>Questionnaire.item.definition</code> element.) </p> <p>Examples of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaires</Link> include:</p> <ul> <li>Past medical history (PMH)</li> <li>Family diseases</li> <li>Social history</li> <li>Research questionnaires/Clinical research forms (CRFs)</li> <li>Quality and evaluation forms</li> <li>Patient intake form (e.g. clipboard)</li> <li>Forms to support insurance claims</li> </ul> <p> This resource is limited in scope to support the characteristics of simple questionnaires.  However, common extensions have been defined to allow more sophisticated behavior.  This includes: </p> <ul>   <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/questionnaire-extensions.html">Questionnaire core extensions</a> which defines the additional descriptive characteristics for questionnaires and their groups and questions</li>   <li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/element-extensions.html">Element extensions</a> which can describe additional constraints on allowed answers for questionnaires such as string length and date and numeric ranges</li> </ul> <p> Additional implementation guides, in particular the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/#sdc">Structured Data Capture <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link> IG</a> provide guidance, extensions and operations that support additional capabilities and allow the definition of more sophisticated questionnaires and their corresponding responses. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> <b>Questionnaires</b> differ from <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">Lists</a> because <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/list">Lists</a> group existing resources, while <b>Questionnaires</b> group arbitrary questions. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaires</Link> are distinct from <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observations</a> and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReports</a> in that both of these resources are intended to capture only certain types of information (lab, imaging, vitals, etc.) and should not be used to capture the full breadth of healthcare information (allergies, medications, care plans, etc.), while <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaires</Link> are able to capture any information at all.  More importantly, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> focus on capturing the discrete information in a standardized form so that the information can be used consistently regardless of where or how it is captured.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link> focuses on information capture.  The same information can be captured using a wide variety of questionnaires with differently phrased questions organized in different manners.  As such, the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link> resource provides a means to standardize the information gathering process (how information is captured), but not how data is interoperably compared, analyzed or computed upon (typically managed using <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</Link> as well as other resources). </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link> supports data-collection workflow to a limited extent, in that - once triggered - a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link> can guide a user through a data collection process that ensures appropriate information is collected based on answers to particular questions.  However, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link> doesn't provide support for capturing sets of information at different times or highly interactive data capture.  Broader workflow is typically managed using <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/task">Task</Link> or using other mechanisms such as CDSHooks. </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaires</Link> are similar to the notion of "logical models" supported by the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/structuredefinition">StructureDefinition</a> resource.  Both support the representation of a collection of data points with labels, data types and hierarchy.  It will be common to find the two of them mapped together.  The primary difference is that <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link> is focused on user-facing data collection.  It describes specific questions and includes information such as what number/label should be displayed beside each question, conditions in which questions should be displayed (or not), what instructions should be provided to the user, etc.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/structuredefinition">StructureDefinition</Link>, on the other hand, merely defines a data structure with no guidance on display or rules around capture mechanism, only what data should exist in the end.  As well, logical models are not intended to capture data directly.  Rather, they provide a basis for mapping between data capture structures. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Groups</Link> and questions that make up a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link> can use the <code>definition</code> element to refer to data elements in external code systems and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/structuredefinition">StructureDefinitions</a>.  In this way, it's possible to leverage standard definitions of questions and their associated data types and answer sets across questionnaires. This also allows extraction of the data from a questionnaire response into other data structures (e.g. populating a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</a> or <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</a> from information in a completed questionnaire response. It can also support other sorts of post-processing of the data contained in a questionnaire response. However, use of the definition element is not required and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaires</Link> may be quite loosely defined. The section <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/#qversusr">Questionnaire versus Resources</a> below discusses the issues of collecting data in such loosely defined <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaires</Link> versus collecting data as well-defined separate Resources. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communication">Communication</a></li>

# QuestionnaireResponse

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaireresponse.mdx

title: QuestionnaireResponse
sidebar_position: 112

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/questionnaireresponse.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# QuestionnaireResponse

A structured set of questions and their answers. The questions are ordered and grouped into coherent subsets, corresponding to the structure of the grouping of the questionnaire being responded to. Read related on [US Core QuestionnaireResponse](http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/StructureDefinition-us-core-questionnaireresponse.html) profile.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> <b>QuestionnaireResponse</b> provides a complete or partial list of answers to a set of questions filled when responding to a questionnaire.   The questions may be included directly or by reference to a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</a> resource that defines the questions as well as the constraints on the allowed answers.  In some cases, both formal rules for editing the questionnaire (via link to <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</a>) as well as sufficient local information to allow rendering of the questionnaire may be provided. </p> <p> Each time a questionnaire is completed for a different subject or at a different time, a distinct <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaireresponse">QuestionnaireResponse</Link> is generated, though it may be possible for a previously entered set of answers to be edited or updated.</p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link> responses cover the need to communicate data originating from forms used in medical history examinations, research questionnaires and sometimes full clinical specialty records. In many systems this data is collected using user-defined screens and forms. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link> responses record specifics about data capture - exactly what questions were asked, in what order, what answers were given, etc. Each of these questions is part of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link>,  and as such the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</Link> is a separately identifiable Resource, whereas the individual questions are not. </p> <p> Examples of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaires</Link> include: </p> <ul> <li>Past medical history (PMH)</li> <li>Family diseases</li> <li>Social history</li> <li>Research questionnaires and Case report forms (CRFs)</li> <li>Quality and evaluation forms</li> <li>Patient intake form (e.g. clipboard)</li> <li>Insurance claim form</li> </ul> <p> <b>QuestionnaireResponse</b> resources can be validated against their corresponding <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</a> to verify that required groups and questions are answered and that answers fit constraints in terms of cardinality, data type, etc. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> The <b>QuestionnaireResponse</b> resource captures the responses to a questionnaire, while <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/questionnaire">Questionnaire</a> represents the definition of the questionnaire form, including what questions are asked, how they're organized and the constraints on the allowed answers. </p> <p> While <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a>, with its nested <code>relatedObservation</code> structure, can create complex hierarchies of  questions and answers, the focus is different.  First, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a> is used primarily for capturing data elements that are "true" observations - lab measurements, vital signs, social assessments, etc., while <b>QuestionnaireResponse</b> can be used to capture any types of data, including data that would typically map to other resources (<a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/medicationstatement">MedicationStatement</a>, etc.).  Second, the focus of <b>QuestionnaireResponse</b> includes the specific phrasing and organization of the questions.  All data must be explicitly captured as a question.  With <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a>, the focus is only on the meaning of the answer, not what question was asked (assuming a question was even asked at all).  Additional information such as normal ranges, interpretation, date, etc., may also be captured. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/clinicalimpression">ClinicalImpression</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/consent">Consent</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/contract">Contract</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/deviceusestatement">DeviceUseStatement</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/familymemberhistory">FamilyMemberHistory</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# RelatedPerson

Information about a person that is involved in the care for a patient, but who is not the target of healthcare, nor has a formal responsibility in the care process.

<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/relatedperson">RelatedPersons</Link> typically have a personal or non-healthcare-specific professional relationship to the patient. A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/relatedperson">RelatedPerson</Link>  resource is primarily used for attribution of information,  since <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/relatedperson">RelatedPersons</Link> are often a source of information about the patient.  For keeping information about people for contact purposes for a patient, use a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</Link>'s Contact element. # RequestGroup

A group of related requests that can be used to capture intended activities that have inter-dependencies such as "give this medication after that one".

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p><strong>This resource is a <em>request</em> resource from a FHIR workflow perspective</strong> - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">Workflow</a>, specifically <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#request">Request</a>.</p> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/requestgroup">RequestGroup</Link> resource is used to represent a group of optional activities that may be performed for a specific patient or context. This resource is often, but not always, the result of applying a specific <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</a> to a particular patient. Other than differences that tie the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/requestgroup">RequestGroup</Link> to a particular subject and setting, the <code>actionDefinition</code> element of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/plandefinition">PlanDefinition</Link> is identical to the <code>action</code> element of the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/requestgroup">RequestGroup</Link>, allowing the same features and functionality to be used in both places to describe optionality of and relationships between activities in a workflow.</p> <p>RequestGroups can contain hierarchical groups of actions, where each specific action references the action to be performed (in terms of a <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#request">Request</a> resource), and each group describes additional behavior, relationships, and applicable conditions between the actions in the overall group.</p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# ResearchStudy

A process where a researcher or organization plans and then executes a series of steps intended to increase the field of healthcare-related knowledge. This includes studies of safety, efficacy, comparative effectiveness and other information about medications, devices, therapies and other interventional and investigative techniques. A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/researchstudy">ResearchStudy</Link> involves the gathering of information about human or animal subjects.

Studies are designed to answer specific questions on how to prevent, diagnose, or treat diseases and disorders. The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/researchstudy">ResearchStudy</Link> resource describes essential information about the study, including the purpose, objective, sponsor, investigator, therapy, condition being studied, schedule of activities, and other key items.</p>     <p>Uses for the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/researchstudy">ResearchStudy</Link> resource include:</p>     <ul>       <li>Registering a clinical trial in trial registry such as clinicaltrials.gov       </li>       <li>Communicating study protocol information between study stakeholders       </li>       <li>Supporting study set up of sites, forms   </li>       <li>Grouping <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</Link> resources by study       </li>       <li>Setting up a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/schedule">Schedule</Link> of Activities for the study and its subjects   </li>       </ul> </div>

# RiskAssessment

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/riskassessment.mdx

title: RiskAssessment
sidebar_position: 119

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/riskassessment.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# RiskAssessment

An assessment of the likely outcome(s) for a patient or other subject as well as the likelihood of each outcome.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p><strong>This resource is an <em>event</em> resource from a FHIR workflow perspective</strong> - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">Workflow</a>, specifically <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html#event">Event</a>.</p> <p> This resource captures predicted outcomes for a patient or population on the basis of source information.  Examples include: </p> <ul>   <li>A prognosis statement for a particular condition</li>   <li>Risk of health outcome (heart attack, particular type of cancer) on the basis of lifestyle factors and/or family history</li>   <li>List of potential health risks based on a patient's genetic analysis</li>   <li>A prediction of outbreak infection rates within a geography based on immunization rates</li> </ul> <p> This resource can be used to represent the results of formal scoring/decision support tools that evaluate risk.  It can also be used to capture a practitioner's subjective assessment of the patient's risk based on existing knowledge and previous experience. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a> <p> Risk assessments are a specialized type of observation.  A specialized resource is used to provide a simpler mechanism to capture of a series of risks and to associate those risks with time-ranges, probabilities, etc.  All risk assertions are captured at one time based on a single set of source inputs.  Capture of a single risk MAY be done using the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a> class, particularly in circumstances where it's treated as a generic observation, but for consistency, all risk assessments and prognosis SHOULD be captured using <b>RiskAssessment</b>. </p> <p> Risk assessments may be based on a variety of factors, including: </p> <ul> <li>Basic demographic information from the <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/patient">Patient</a> or <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/group">Group</a> resources</li> <li>Various <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observations</a> including vital signs, lab information, assessments, genetic information, etc.</li> <li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/familymemberhistory">FamilyMemberHistory</a></li> <li>Current, past and proposed therapies <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/immunization">Immunization</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</a>, etc.</li> </ul> <p> Because so many resources can potentially be used, no limit is placed on what resources can be sent in <code>RiskAssessment.basis</code>.  However, some resources would be nonsensical for this use (e.g. <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/messageheader">MessageHeader</a>). </p> <p> <b>AllergyIntolerance and <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/riskassessment">RiskAssessment</Link></b></p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/allergyintolerance">AllergyIntolerance</Link> describes a specific type of risk - propensity to reaction to a substance while <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/riskassessment">RiskAssessment</a> describes  general risks to a subject, not generally based on a reaction. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="backgroundAndContext" label="Background and Context">
<div> <a name="bnc"></a> <p> Risk Assessments can be determined manually by health-care providers based on their professional expertise, by using an algorithmic scoring system or through a combination.  Risk assessments can also be computed by decision support systems.  <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/operationdefinition">OperationDefinitions</a> may be defined by servers to generate risk assessments based on particular combinations of source resources or other inputs. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/clinicalimpression">ClinicalImpression</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/goal">Goal</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# Schedule

# Schedule

A container for slots of time that may be available for booking appointments.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/schedule">Schedule</Link> resources provide a container for time-slots that can be booked using an appointment. It provides the window of time (period) that slots are defined for and what type of appointments can be booked.<br/> The schedule does not provide any information about actual appointments. This separation greatly assists where access to the appointments would not be permitted for security or privacy reasons, while still being able to determine if an appointment might be available. </p>     <p>       Note: A schedule is not used for the delivery of medication, the <a href="https://hl7.org/fhir/datatypes.html#Timing">Timing</a> data type should be used for that purpose.     </p> <h3 class="self-link-parent">  Context  <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/schedule.html#12.12.1.1" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3>     <p>       A schedule controls the dates and times available for the performance of a service       and/or the use of a resource.  One schedule applies to one service or resource, since       each service or resource can be reserved independently of the others.<br/>       If two or more services, people, locations, or things cannot be reserved independently       of one another, they are considered to be one activity or resource.     </p>     <p>       A schedule consists of slots of time during which the controlled service or resource is potentially available for provision or use.  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/slot">Slots</Link> are categorized as open, booked, or blocked.  An open slot on a schedule indicates that the service or resource is available for provision or use during that period of time.  A booked slot indicates that the service or resource is not available during the time period, because an appointment has been scheduled.  A blocked slot indicates that a service or resource is unavailable for reasons other than a scheduled appointment. </p> <p> The real-world, non-automated analogue of the schedule described above is a standard appointment book.  These books are generally organized with rows of time slots, during which a service or resource is available. </p> <p> A slot is one unit on a schedule.  A slot represents the smallest unit of time or quantity that a service or resource may be booked.  Depending on the nature of the service or resource, there may be more than one defined slot at a given instant of time. For example, if a service is an open group therapy session with twelve available seats, then there are twelve slots for the given block of time. </p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Actor - What the schedule applies to <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/schedule.html#12.12.1.2" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> The schedule belongs to a single instance of a service or resource. This is normally a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/healthcareservice">HealthcareService</Link>,  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/practitioner">Practitioner</Link>, <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/location">Location</Link> or <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/device">Device</Link>.  In the case where a single resource can provide  different services, potentially at different location, then the schedulable resource is considered the composite  of the actors.  <br/> For example, if a practitioner can provide services at multiple locations, they might have one schedule per location, where each schedule includes both the practitioner and location actors.   When booking an appointment with multiple schedulable resources, multiple schedules may need to be checked  depending on the configuration of the system. </p> <p> If an appointment has two practitioners, a specific medical device and a room then there could be a schedule for each of these resources that may need to be consulted to ensure that no collisions occur.<br/> If the schedule needed to be consulted, then there would be one created covering the planning horizon for the time of the appointment. </p> <h3 class="self-link-parent"> Checking availability - Searching <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/schedule.html#12.12.1.3" title="link to here" class="self-link"></a></h3> <p> When checking availability for an appointment, the creator of the appointment should determine which schedules are applicable, then check for available slots within each schedule. </p> <p> Determining which schedules should be consulted often will involve searching via the properties of the referenced actors,  such as the ServiceCategory on the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/healthcareservice">HealthcareService</Link>, or the <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/datatypes/address">Address</Link> on a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/location">Location</Link>. </p> <p> The type parameter can be used to filter the type of services that can be booked within the associated slots. <br/> </p> <p> If all slots are busy, the caller may attempt to book an appointment into an already-booked slot, but the server business rules will dictate whether overbooking is allowed, or whether the appointment may be given a higher precedence and allocated  the overbooked slot. </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/metadatatypes.html#TriggerDefinition">TriggerDefinition</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/slot">Slot</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

# ServiceRequest

A record of a request for service such as diagnostic investigations, treatments, or operations to be performed.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <a name="dstu"></a> <p> <strong>This resource is a request resource from a FHIR workflow perspective</strong> - see <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/workflow.html">Workflow</a>.</p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</Link> is a record of a request for a procedure or diagnostic or other service to be planned, proposed, or performed, as distinguished by the <code>ServiceRequest.intent</code> field value, with or on a patient. The procedure will lead to either a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a> or <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</a>, which in turn may reference one or more <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observations</a>, which summarize the performance of the procedures and associated documentation such as observations, images, findings that are relevant to the treatment/management of the subject. This resource may be used to share relevant information required to support a referral or a transfer of care request from one practitioner or organization to another when a patient is required to be referred to another provider for a consultation /second opinion and/or for short term or longer term management of one or more health issues or problems. </p> <p> Examples include: </p> <ul> <li>  diagnostic tests/studies</li> <li>  endoscopic procedures</li> <li>  counseling</li> <li>  biopsies</li> <li>  therapies (e.g., physio-, social-, psychological-)</li> <li>  (exploratory) surgeries or procedures</li> <li>  exercises</li> <li>  specialist consultation and assessments</li> <li>  community services</li> <li>  nursing services</li> <li>  pharmacist medication review, and</li> <li>  other clinical interventions.</li> </ul> <p>   <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedures</Link> may be performed by a healthcare professional, a friend or relative or in some cases by the patient themselves. </p> <p>The principal intention of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</Link> is to support ordering procedures for one patient (which includes non-human patients in veterinary medicine). However, in many contexts, healthcare related processes include performing diagnostic investigations on groups of subjects, devices involved in the provision of healthcare, and even environmental locations such as ducts, bodies of water, etc. <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</Link> supports all these usages.  The service request may represent an order that is entered by a practitioner in a CPOE system as well as a proposal made by a clinical decision support (CDS) system based on a patient's clinical record and context of care. Planned procedures referenced by a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/careplan">CarePlan</a> may also be represented by this resource. </p> <p>The general work flow that this resource facilitates is that a clinical system creates a service request. The service request is then accessed by or exchanged with a system, perhaps via intermediaries, that represents an organization (e.g., diagnostic or imaging service, surgical team, physical therapy department) that can perform the procedure. The organization receiving the service request will, after it accepts the request, update the request as the work is performed, and then finally issue a report that references the requests that it fulfilled.</p> <p>The <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</Link> resource allows requesting only a single procedure. If a workflow requires requesting multiple procedures simultaneously, this is done using multiple instances of this resource. These instances can be linked in different ways, depending on the needs of the workflow. For guidance, refer to the <a href="https://www.hl7.org/fhir/request.html">Request pattern</a> </p> </div>
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="relationships" label="Relationships">
<div> <a name="bnr"></a>     <p>  <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</Link> is a record of a proposal/plan or order for a service to be performed that would result in a <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/procedure">Procedure</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/observation">Observation</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/diagnosticreport">DiagnosticReport</a>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/imagingstudy">ImagingStudy</a> or similar resource. In contrast to <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</Link>, <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/task">Task</a> which spans both intent and event and tracks the execution through to completion and is intended for "administrative" actions like requesting and tracking things to be done to a record, or keeping track of a checklist of steps such to be performed as part of a fulfilment process. A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</Link> can be higher-level authorization that triggered the creation of <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/task">Task</Link>, or it can be the "request" resource <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/task">Task</Link> is seeking to fulfill.     </p> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</Link> and <a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communicationrequest">CommunicationRequest</a> are related. A <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communicationrequest">CommunicationRequest</Link> is a request to merely disclose information. Whereas a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</Link> would be used to request information as part of training or counseling - i.e. when the process will involve verification of the patient's comprehension or an attempt to change the patient's mental state. In some workflows both may exist.  For example, upon receiving a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/communicationrequest">CommunicationRequest</Link> a practitioner might initiate a <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/servicerequest">ServiceRequest</Link>.     </p> </div>
  </TabItem>

# Slot

Source: https://github.com/medplum/medplum/blob/main/packages/docs/docs/api/fhir/resources/slot.mdx

title: Slot
sidebar_position: 124

import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';
import Tabs from '@theme/Tabs';
import TabItem from '@theme/TabItem';
import definition from '@site/static/data/resourceDefinitions/slot.json';
import { ResourcePropertiesTable, SearchParamsTable } from '@site/src/components/ResourceTables';

# Slot

A slot of time on a schedule that may be available for booking appointments.

<Tabs queryString="section">
  <TabItem value="schema" label="Schema" default>

## Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable
  properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => !(p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource')))}
/>

## Search Parameters

<SearchParamsTable searchParams={definition.searchParameters} />

## Inherited Elements

<ResourcePropertiesTable properties={definition.properties.filter((p) => p.inherited && p.base.includes('Resource'))} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="usage" label="Usage">
<div> <a name="scope"></a> <p> <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/slot">Slot</Link> resources are used to provide time-slots that can be booked using an appointment. They do not provide any information about appointments that are available, just the time, and optionally what the time can be used for. These are effectively spaces of free/busy time.<br/>       <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/slot">Slots</Link> can also be marked as busy without having appointments associated.     </p> <p> A slot can have more than one appointment allocated to it. A scheduling system may permit multiple allocations up to a specific number of places. An example of this type of usage        could be where the slot is being used for a group service that permits 5 participants at        the same time. </p> <p> A slot can be marked as over-booked indicating that there are too many appointments allocated to it. </p> <p> In some situations a service may have a specific set of slots reserved for specific uses, such  as "walk-ins" or a specific organization has a "standing booking" for Thursday mornings. These should be represented using the appointmentType field with a specified and agreed value.<br/> Security Permissions or specific business rules on the system could enforce that only eligible appointments are allocated to them. </p>     <p>       If a service had a weekly schedule created that permitted eight 1 hour appointments each       day of a working week (Monday - Friday), this would be constructed by a single <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/schedule">Schedule</Link>       resource with the dates for the start and end of the week set, and then 40 (5x8) <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/slot">Slot</Link>        resources associated with it.<br/>       As appointments fill up the schedule, these slots would individually be marked as busy       as the appointments are filled into the slots.<br/>       The slots in a schedule do not need to be the same size, and can be different for different       days of the week.<br/>   </p><p>       <Link to="/docs/api/fhir/resources/slot">Slot</Link> instances do not have any recurrence information included. If recurring information is       desired, this will be managed outside these resources, or included as extensions.   </p>   <p>       Note that booking an appointment does not necessarily require that slot resources be identified.   When attempting to book an appointment, if the requestor knows ahead of time which schedulable     resources are required, then identifying individual slots from the resources' schedules prior to creating   the appointment is appropriate.   However, in some medical scheduling scenarios, determining which resources are required for an appointment   is very complex, and options other than using schedule+slot may be a better solution.        </p>     <p></p>   </div>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem value="referencedBy" label="Referenced By">
<ul><li><a href="/docs/api/fhir/resources/appointment">Appointment</a></li></ul>
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>
